examples: paint: rampOver(dist.linear({from: p('start'), to: p('end'), angle: p('angle')}), stops(p('colorSpace')), {edges: p('edges')})
paint.dist.linear.signature: dist.linear(slots: {from: PropRef; to: PropRef; angle: FieldScalar}): Field

paint.dist.radial.name: radial
paint.dist.radial.summary: A round or elliptical gradient spreading out from a center.
paint.dist.radial.description: 0 at `center`, 1 at `radius` (a fraction of the canvas height). `aspect` 1 is a circle, larger values squeeze it horizontally. `skew` in degrees tilts the ellipse.
examples: paint: rampOver(rings(dist.radial({center: p('center'), radius: p('radius'), aspect: p('aspect'), skew: p('skewAngle')}), p('repeat')), stops(p('colorSpace')))
paint.dist.radial.signature: dist.radial(slots: {center: PropRef; radius: FieldScalar; aspect: FieldScalar; skew: FieldScalar}): Field

params.name: slots
params.type: {center: PropRef; radius: FieldScalar; aspect: FieldScalar; skew: FieldScalar}

paint.dist.conic.name: conic
paint.dist.conic.summary: A sweep around a center, like a clock hand: 0 to 1 once around.
paint.dist.conic.description: The sweep starts at the left of the center and runs counter-clockwise. `rotation` in degrees moves the start. Wrap it in `tiles` to repeat the sweep.
examples: paint: rampOver(tiles(dist.conic({center: p('center'), rotation: p('rotation')}), p('repeat')), stops(p('colorSpace')))

paint.dist.diamond.name: diamond
paint.dist.diamond.summary: A diamond-shaped gradient spreading out from a center.
paint.dist.diamond.description: 0 at `center`, 1 at `size` (a fraction of the canvas height). `roundness` 0 is a sharp diamond and 1 is a square. `rotation` in degrees tilts it.
examples: paint: rampOver(rings(dist.diamond({center: p('center'), size: p('size'), rotation: p('rotation'), roundness: p('roundness')}), p('repeat')), stops(p('colorSpace')))
paint.dist.diamond.signature: dist.diamond(slots: {center: PropRef; size: FieldScalar; rotation: FieldScalar; roundness: FieldScalar}): Field

params.name: slots
params.type: {center: PropRef; size: FieldScalar; rotation: FieldScalar; roundness: FieldScalar}

paint.dist.spiral.name: spiral
paint.dist.spiral.summary: A turning spiral stripe: 0 on the background, 1 on the stroke.
paint.dist.spiral.description: It spins on the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`. `scale` sets how many turns fit, `width` (0–2) the stroke thickness, `falloff` (0–1) thins the stroke away from the center, `softness` (0–1) blurs its edge. Unlike the other distance fields this one is already 0–1, so pair it with a palette of background and stroke colors.
examples: paint: rampOver(dist.spiral({center: p('center'), scale: p('scale'), width: p('strokeWidth'), falloff: p('strokeFalloff'), softness: p('softness')}), pair(p('background'), p('stroke'), p('colorSpace')))
paint.dist.spiral.signature: dist.spiral(slots: {center: PropRef; scale: FieldScalar; width: FieldScalar; falloff: FieldScalar; softness: FieldScalar}): Field

params.name: slots
params.type: {center: PropRef; scale: FieldScalar; width: FieldScalar; falloff: FieldScalar; softness: FieldScalar}

paint.dist.name: dist
paint.dist.summary: Distance fields: the shape of a gradient, as a number that grows away from a line or point.
paint.dist.description: Each takes position props made with `transformPosition` and returns 0 at the start and 1 at the end, unbounded beyond. Feed one to `rampOver`.
paint.dist.signature: dist: { linear, radial, conic, diamond, spiral }

paint.rings.name: rings
paint.rings.summary: Repeats a field as concentric bands.
paint.rings.description: `count` above 1 restarts the field every 1/count, so a radial gradient becomes rings. At 1 or below the field is clamped to 0–1, and values under 1 stretch the gradient further out.
examples: paint: rampOver(rings(dist.radial({center: p('center'), radius: p('radius'), aspect: 1, skew: 0}), p('repeat')), stops(p('colorSpace')))
tips: Each band restarts at the first color rather than bouncing back. For a mirrored repeat, pass `edges` to `rampOver` instead.

paint.tiles.name: tiles
paint.tiles.summary: Repeats a field `count` times, always wrapping.
paint.tiles.description: Made for sweeps: `tiles(dist.conic(...), 4)` gives four sectors. Any count works, including fractions.
examples: paint: rampOver(tiles(dist.conic({center: p('center'), rotation: p('rotation')}), p('repeat')), stops(p('colorSpace')))

paint.tone.name: tone
paint.tone.summary: Reshapes a 0–1 field with glow, contrast and balance controls, then flips it.
paint.tone.description: `glow` is a spread control: 5 leaves the field alone, lower values pull the bright parts into tight cores, higher values spread them into a wash. `contrast` scales around the middle, 1 is neutral. `balance` is 0–100 with 50 neutral. `invert` is always true: the result is flipped so the palette's first color lands where the field is high.
examples: paint: rampOver(tone(scaledVolume(noiseField('mx3'), {scale: p('scale')}), {glow: p('intensity'), contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance'), invert: true}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
tips: Raising `balance` pushes more of the canvas toward the first color.
paint.tone.signature: tone(field: Field, opts: {glow: FieldScalar; contrast: FieldScalar; balance: FieldScalar; invert: true}): Field

params.name: opts
params.type: {glow: FieldScalar; contrast: FieldScalar; balance: FieldScalar; invert: true}

paint.threshold.name: threshold
paint.threshold.summary: Turns a signed field (−1 to 1) into a soft 0–1 mask.
paint.threshold.description: The field is first mapped to 0–1 and shifted by `bias`, then eased from 0 at `low` to 1 at `high`. Bring `low` and `high` together for a hard edge.
examples: paint: rampOver(threshold(flowField({detail: p('detail')}), {low: 0.3, high: 0.7, bias: {base: p('blend'), add: -50, mul: 0.006}}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
paint.threshold.signature: threshold(field: Field, opts: {low: number; high: number; bias?: FieldScalar}): Field

paint.share.name: share
paint.share.summary: Evaluates a field once and lets several words read the same result.
paint.share.description: Wrap a field in `share` when it feeds two places, such as a `threshold` and a `pulse`.
examples:
const pattern = share(flowField({detail: p('detail')}))
// then: threshold(pattern, ...) and pulse(pattern, ...)
tips: One result per layer, whatever coordinate it is asked for. Do not use it to sample the same field at two offsets.

paint.noiseField.name: noiseField
paint.noiseField.summary: A field of smooth noise in the chosen flavor.
paint.noiseField.description: Noise needs a 3D coordinate, so put it inside `scaledVolume` (and `warped` for motion).
examples: paint: rampOver(scaledVolume(noiseField('mx3'), {scale: p('scale')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

paint.warped.name: warped
paint.warped.summary: Makes a field flow like liquid by bending its coordinate with moving noise.
paint.warped.description: `amount` sets how far the coordinate is pushed (0 is off), `amountScale` multiplies it so a 0–1 slider can reach further. The motion runs on the layer's clock times `timeScale`, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`. Needs a 3D coordinate: put it inside `scaledVolume`.
examples: scaledVolume(warped(noiseField('mx3'), {amount: p('warp'), amountScale: 4, timeScale: 0.125}), {scale: p('scale')})
paint.warped.signature: warped(field: Field, opts: {amount: FieldScalar; amountScale?: number; timeScale?: number}): Field

paint.scaledVolume.name: scaledVolume
paint.scaledVolume.summary: Gives a noise field a zoomable, aspect-correct coordinate.
paint.scaledVolume.description: Turns the pixel's uv into a 3D point so `noiseField` and `warped` can read it. `scale` zooms exponentially: 1 is neutral and each step up magnifies about 2.7 times. A 0–4 slider works well.
examples: paint: rampOver(scaledVolume(noiseField('perlin'), {scale: p('scale')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

paint.flowField.name: flowField
paint.flowField.summary: A swirling, animated wave pattern from −1 to 1.
paint.flowField.description: `detail` sets how fine the swirls are. It moves on the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`. Feed it to `threshold` for color bands or to `pulse` for a shimmer.
examples: paint: rampOver(threshold(flowField({detail: p('detail')}), {low: 0.3, high: 0.7}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

paint.pulse.name: pulse
paint.pulse.summary: A gentle brightness pulse that follows a pattern field, hovering around 1.
paint.pulse.description: The result swings between 1 − `depth` and 1 + `depth`, so `depth` around 0.02 is subtle. `speed` is how fast it breathes, `span` how much the pattern staggers the phase. Use it as the gain in `shimmered`.
examples: paint: shimmered(rampOver(threshold(pattern, {low: 0.3, high: 0.7}), stops(p('colorSpace'))), pulse(pattern, {speed: 2.5, span: 8, depth: 0.015}))
paint.pulse.signature: pulse(field: Field, opts: {speed: number; span: number; depth: number}): Field

paint.hueWheel.name: hueWheel
paint.hueWheel.summary: A rainbow color for a hue value: 0 is red, cycling through the spectrum and back every 1.
paint.hueWheel.description: Takes any number and wraps it. Returns an rgb color with no alpha.
examples: const rgb = hueWheel(math.add(math.mul(angle, 0.42), animatedTime(params)))

paint.shimmered.name: shimmered
paint.shimmered.summary: Multiplies a paint's color and alpha by a gain field, for a slow shimmer over a pattern.
paint.shimmered.description: The gain is read at the raw canvas uv. Build it with `pulse`.
examples: paint: shimmered(rampOver(field, stops(p('colorSpace'))), pulse(field, {speed: 2.5, span: 8, depth: 0.015}))

paint.scatterField.name: scatterField
paint.scatterField.summary: A mesh-gradient field: up to 8 drifting points scattered across the canvas, blended by nearness.
paint.scatterField.description: Each point carries a fixed 0–1 value and the result is their distance-weighted average, so a palette lookup gives soft patches of color. `at` is an aspect-corrected coordinate (x runs 0 to the aspect ratio, y 0–1). `count` is 1–8, `seed` reshuffles the layout, `drift` (0–1) sets how far points wander on `time`, `softness` sharpens the patches as it rises. Pass `anchors` from `scatteredAnchors` to skip recomputing the points per pixel.
examples:
const t = scatterField({at: uv, count: uniformOf(p('count'), params), seed, drift: uniformOf(p('drift'), params), aspect, time, softness: 3})
return standardPalette(t, params)
paint.scatterField.signature:
scatterField(opts: {
    at: Expr
    count: Expr | number
    seed: Expr | number
    drift: Expr | number
    aspect: Expr | number
    time: Expr | number
    softness: Expr | number
    /** The points precomputed each frame by `scatteredAnchors`. When given, `drift`, `aspect` and `time` are ignored here. */
    anchors?: Expr
}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    at: Expr
    count: Expr | number
    seed: Expr | number
    drift: Expr | number
    aspect: Expr | number
    time: Expr | number
    softness: Expr | number
    /** The points precomputed each frame by `scatteredAnchors`. When given, `drift`, `aspect` and `time` are ignored here. */
    anchors?: Expr
}

paint.scatteredAnchors.name: scatteredAnchors
paint.scatteredAnchors.summary: Computes the `scatterField` points once per frame instead of once per pixel.
paint.scatteredAnchors.description: Declare a field on the definition, `extraFields: {meshAnchors: {schema: schema.arrayOf(schema.vec4f, 4), initial: new Array(16).fill(0)}}`, name it in `field`, and pass the result as `anchors` to `scatterField`. The points follow the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime`.
examples:
const anchors = scatteredAnchors(params, {count: p('count'), seed: p('seed'), drift: p('drift'), field: 'meshAnchors'})
const t = scatterField({at: uv, count: uniformOf(p('count'), params), seed, drift: 0, aspect: 1, time: 0, softness: 3, anchors})
paint.scatteredAnchors.signature: scatteredAnchors(params: GpuFragmentParams, slots: {count: PropRef; seed: PropRef; drift: PropRef; field: string}): Expr

params.name: slots
params.type: {count: PropRef; seed: PropRef; drift: PropRef; field: string}

paint.wrapRamp.name: wrapRamp
paint.wrapRamp.summary: Runs a palette value back and forth `cycles` times so a ramp repeats without a seam.
paint.wrapRamp.description: At `cycles` 1 the value passes through unchanged. Where the bands get thinner than a pixel they fade to the palette's middle instead of flickering. Use it on the value before the palette lookup, in a `paint:` function.
examples: return standardPalette(wrapRamp({t: field, cycles: math.add(1, math.mul(uniformOf(p('wrapping'), params), 6))}), params)
tips: Not for use inside a `guarded` branch. Reach for `foldRamp` there.
paint.wrapRamp.signature: wrapRamp(opts: {t: Expr; cycles: Expr | number}): Expr

paint.foldRamp.name: foldRamp
paint.foldRamp.summary: Folds any number into 0–1 as a seamless zigzag: up from 0 to 1, back down, every 2 units.
paint.foldRamp.description: Scale the value first to set the cycle length. Safe anywhere, including inside a `guarded` branch.
examples: const rgb = stops(p('colorSpace'))(foldRamp(phase), params).member('rgb')

paint.warpedPoint.name: warpedPoint
paint.warpedPoint.summary: A 3D position pushed around by moving noise, for reading several fields at one warped spot.
paint.warpedPoint.description: `at` is the 3D point to warp, `time` drives the motion, `amount` how far it is pushed. `levels` 2 (default) is the full warp, 1 is a cheaper single pass for low-power devices. Use `warped` instead when one field is enough.
examples: const q = warpedPoint({at: math.vec3(x, y, seed), time: math.mul(t, 0.3), amount: 0.5, levels: isMobileGpuViewport() ? 1 : 2})
paint.warpedPoint.signature: warpedPoint(opts: {at: Expr; time: Expr | number; amount: Expr | number; levels?: 1 | 2}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {at: Expr; time: Expr | number; amount: Expr | number; levels?: 1 | 2}

paint.warpStep.name: warpStep
paint.warpStep.summary: One step of a chained warp: pushes a 2D position by two noise reads and hands them back.
paint.warpStep.description: Returns a vec4: `xy` is the warped position, `zw` the two noise values, useful for shading later. Chain steps by feeding one step's `xy` into the next. `scale` sets the noise frequency, `z` is a time or seed slice, `offsets` two fixed 2D offsets that keep the reads apart, and the push distance is `reach` times `strength`.
examples:
const level1 = warpStep({at: uv, scale: 1.2, z: math.mul(t, 0.5), offsets: [[5.2, 1.3], [1.7, 9.2]], reach: 0.4, strength: uniformOf(p('warp'), params)})
const level2 = warpStep({at: level1.member('xy'), scale: 2.4, z: t, offsets: [[8.3, 2.8], [2.1, 6.4]], reach: 0.25, strength: uniformOf(p('warp'), params)})
paint.warpStep.signature:
warpStep(opts: {
    at: Expr
    scale: number
    z: Expr | number
    offsets: [[number, number], [number, number]]
    reach: number
    strength: Expr | number
}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    at: Expr
    scale: number
    z: Expr | number
    offsets: [[number, number], [number, number]]
    reach: number
    strength: Expr | number
}

paint.standardPalette.name: standardPalette
paint.standardPalette.summary: The color for a 0–1 value from the standard palette props: `colorA`, `colorB`, `stops`, `colorSpace`.
paint.standardPalette.description: Declare those four props (`stops: colorStopsPropConfig()`, `colorSpace` marked `compileTime`). It has the shape of a `Palette`, so it drops straight into `rampOver`, or call it yourself inside a `paint:` function.
examples: paint: rampOver(scaledVolume(noiseField('mx3'), {scale: p('scale')}), standardPalette)

paint.quadBlend.name: quadBlend
paint.quadBlend.summary: A four-color blend on a square: `a` to `b` across the top, `c` to `d` across the bottom, then top to bottom.
paint.quadBlend.description: Returns a function you call with two 0–1 values (across, then down) and the params. Mixes in the color space named by the `space` prop (mark it `compileTime`). For any space other than linear, declare `extraFields` named `convA`, `convB`, `convC`, `convD`, each `{schema: schema.vec3f, initial: [0, 0, 0]}`.
examples: const base = quadBlend({a: p('colorA'), b: p('colorB'), c: p('colorC'), d: p('colorD'), space: p('colorSpace')})(t1, t2, params)
paint.quadBlend.signature: quadBlend(slots: {a: PropRef; b: PropRef; c: PropRef; d: PropRef; space: PropRef}): (t1: Expr, t2: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

params.name: slots
params.type: {a: PropRef; b: PropRef; c: PropRef; d: PropRef; space: PropRef}

gradients.solidColor.name: solidColor
gradients.solidColor.summary: A flat fill in one color prop.
gradients.solidColor.description: The color's alpha passes through, so a half-transparent color gives a half-transparent layer.
examples: paint: solidColor(p('color'))

gradients.colorWheel.name: colorWheel
gradients.colorWheel.summary: A striped gradient that slides across the canvas, cycling through its colors over time.
gradients.colorWheel.description: `mode` is a `compileTime` prop: `'rainbow'` generates a full spectrum, `'custom'` loops `palette.a` to `b` to `c` and back, mixed in the color space named by the `space` prop (also `compileTime`, ignored in rainbow mode). `direction` in degrees turns the stripes about the canvas center, `scale` sets how many color cycles cross the canvas (1 is a single wide sweep). It moves on the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`.
examples: paint: colorWheel({mode: p('mode'), direction: p('angle'), scale: p('scale'), palette: {a: p('colorA'), b: p('colorB'), c: p('colorC')}, space: p('colorSpace')})

params.name: slots

gradients.pointCloudGradient.name: pointCloudGradient
gradients.pointCloudGradient.summary: Five colored points placed anywhere on the canvas, each pixel taking the colors of the points nearest it.
gradients.pointCloudGradient.description: Pass exactly five `{color, position}` prop pairs (positions made with `transformPosition`). `smoothness` (0–5) widens each point's reach as it rises. The mix happens in the color space named by the `space` prop (mark it `compileTime`).
examples: paint: pointCloudGradient({points: [{color: p('colorA'), position: p('positionA')}, {color: p('colorB'), position: p('positionB')}, {color: p('colorC'), position: p('positionC')}, {color: p('colorD'), position: p('positionD')}, {color: p('colorE'), position: p('positionE')}], smoothness: p('smoothness'), space: p('colorSpace')})
tips: For a softer, animated version with any number of points, see `scatterField` in the fields words.

params.name: slots

gradients.beamPreconvertedFields.name: beamPreconvertedFields
gradients.beamPreconvertedFields.description: Spread it as `extraFields: beamPreconvertedFields` next to the `beam` paint.
examples: extraFields: beamPreconvertedFields,

gradients.beam.name: beam
gradients.beam.summary: A glowing beam of light between two points.
gradients.beam.description: `from` and `to` are position props (made with `transformPosition`). `thickness` (0–2) and `softness` each take a `start` and `end` value so the beam can taper. The cross-section shades from `colors.inside` at the core to `colors.outside` at the edge, mixed in the color space named by the `space` prop (mark it `compileTime`). Declare `extraFields: beamPreconvertedFields` on the definition.
examples: paint: beam({from: p('startPosition'), to: p('endPosition'), thickness: {start: p('startThickness'), end: p('endThickness')}, softness: {start: p('startSoftness'), end: p('endSoftness')}, colors: {inside: p('insideColor'), outside: p('outsideColor')}, space: p('colorSpace')})

params.name: slots

patterns.cellFrame.name: cellFrame
patterns.cellFrame.summary: The shared coordinate system of a tiled pattern: how many cells fit down the canvas height and how far the whole lattice is rotated.
patterns.cellFrame.description: `cells` counts cells along the canvas height, so cells stay square as the canvas resizes. `rotation` is in degrees about the canvas centre. Pass the result as the `frame` of `gridLines`, `hexLines`, `triangleLines`, `truchetArcs`, `weaveThreads` or `isoCubeFaces`.
examples: const field = gridLines({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'flippedY'}), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), variation: p('variation')})
tips: One frame can feed several line words. It is evaluated once however many read it.
patterns.cellFrame.signature: cellFrame(slots: {cells: PropRef; rotation: PropRef; convention: CellFrameConvention}): PatternPaint

patterns.vary.name: vary
patterns.vary.summary: A color lightened or darkened per cell by a shade factor, alpha untouched.
patterns.vary.description: `factor` is the `shade` output of a lattice word: 1 keeps the color, above 1 brightens, below 1 darkens. Use it on the cell fill so every tile reads slightly different.
examples: paint: strokeOver({fill: vary(p('cellColor'), field.shade), stroke: p('color'), mask: field.lines, space: p('colorSpace')})

patterns.strokeOver.name: strokeOver
patterns.strokeOver.summary: Two colors mixed through a mask: `fill` where the mask is 0, `stroke` where it is 1.
patterns.strokeOver.description: The everyday way to color a pattern. `space` is a color-space prop (`'linear'`, `'oklch'`, `'oklab'`, `'hsl'`, `'hsv'`, `'lch'`); leave it out for a linear mix. Alpha interpolates too, so a transparent fill gives a lines-only pattern.
examples: paint: strokeOver({fill: p('colorA'), stroke: p('colorB'), mask: checkerCells({cells: p('cells'), softness: p('softness')}), space: p('colorSpace')})
tips: The `space` prop must be `compileTime: true`. Changing it recompiles the shader.
patterns.strokeOver.signature: strokeOver(layers: {fill: PaintSlot; stroke: PaintSlot; mask: PaintSlot; space?: PropRef}): PatternPaint

params.name: layers
params.type: {fill: PaintSlot; stroke: PaintSlot; mask: PaintSlot; space?: PropRef}

patterns.sampleMapsAtCellCentres.name: sampleMapsAtCellCentres
patterns.sampleMapsAtCellCentres.summary: Makes map-driven props change per whole cell instead of per pixel, so a mapped dot size or line thickness grows cell by cell rather than being cut off mid-cell.
patterns.sampleMapsAtCellCentres.description: Set it on the definition's `mapSampleUVs` field, not in `paint:`. Give it the same `cells` count and `rotation` (degrees) the pattern uses so the snapping matches the lattice. `props` lists the prop names to snap.
examples: mapSampleUVs: sampleMapsAtCellCentres({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), props: ['thickness', 'softness']})
tips: Only matters when a prop is driven by a map (an image or another layer). Plain values are unaffected.

params.name: slots

patterns.scatterPoint.name: scatterPoint
patterns.scatterPoint.summary: One random point in each cell of a square grid: the classic scatter for glitter, stars, dust and sparkles.
patterns.scatterPoint.description: `coord` is the pixel's position in any unit (CSS pixels via `uv × logicalViewportSize` keeps the spacing steady across screens); `cellSize` is the grid spacing in that unit. `jitter` is how far the point wanders from the cell's centre, 0 (dead centre) to 1 (anywhere in the cell). `seed` re-rolls every point. Returns the cell's `point` and this pixel's `offset` from it (both in `coord`'s unit), plus `random`, three independent 0–1 values for the cell (`.x` and `.y` already place the point; use `.z` and the others to vary brightness, timing or size).
examples: const {offset, random} = scatterPoint(px, {cellSize: 30, jitter: 0.6, seed: params.uniforms.seed})
tips:
A pixel only sees its own cell's point, so keep anything drawn around it smaller than
half a cell or it gets clipped at the cell edge. Use `scatterPoints` for larger shapes.

patterns.scatterPoints.name: scatterPoints
patterns.scatterPoints.summary: The scattered points of the four grid cells nearest the pixel, so anything drawn up to half a cell from its point shows whole, never clipped at a cell edge.
patterns.scatterPoints.description: Same options and same points as `scatterPoint` (one random point per cell); returns four of them instead of one. Draw something around each and add the results. Costs four times `scatterPoint`.
examples:
const glints = scatterPoints(px, {cellSize: 60, jitter: 0.6, seed: params.uniforms.seed})
    .map(({offset}) => starGlint(offset, {core: 0.9, rayLength: 0.1, rayWidth: 1.6, rays: 0.25, reach: 30}))
tips:
Pair with `starGlint`'s `reach` set to half the cell size, so a glint has faded out
before it could reach a cell this pixel doesn't look at.

patterns.withAlpha.name: withAlpha
patterns.withAlpha.summary: A color with its alpha replaced by a separately built mask.
patterns.withAlpha.description: The usual way to hang a pattern under one color: the mask becomes the coverage and the color's own alpha is dropped.
examples: paint: withAlpha(p('color'), dotLattice({density: p('density'), dotSize: p('dotSize'), offset: p('offset'), speedVariance: p('speedVariance'), twinkle: p('twinkle')}))
tips: To keep the color's own alpha as well, multiply it in: `withAlpha(color, times(alphaOf(color), mask))`.

patterns.alphaOf.name: alphaOf
patterns.alphaOf.summary: The alpha channel of a color, as a number per pixel.
examples: paint: withAlpha(streakColor, times(alphaOf(streakColor), streaks.mask))

patterns.rgbOf.name: rgbOf
patterns.rgbOf.summary: The RGB channels of a color, without its alpha.
patterns.rgbOf.description: Finish it with `opaque` or `withAlpha` to make a color again.
examples: paint: opaque(mixOf(times(rgbOf(cubeColor), faces.tone), rgbOf(p('lineColor')), faces.wire))

patterns.times.name: times
patterns.times.summary: The product of two values: a mask scaled by a prop, an RGB dimmed by a shade, two masks combined.
examples: mask: times(faces.random, p('colorVariation'))

patterns.mixOf.name: mixOf
patterns.mixOf.summary: A straight blend from one value to another by an amount from 0 to 1.
patterns.mixOf.description: Works on colors, RGB and single numbers alike, channel by channel with no color-space handling. For a color mix in a chosen color space use `strokeOver`.
examples: mixOf(alphaOf(p('colorA')), alphaOf(p('colorB')), bands)
patterns.mixOf.signature: mixOf(from: PaintSlot, to: PaintSlot, amount: PaintSlot): PatternPaint

patterns.opaque.name: opaque
patterns.opaque.summary: An RGB value finished as a fully opaque color.
examples: paint: opaque(mixOf(times(rgbOf(cubeColor), faces.tone), rgbOf(p('lineColor')), faces.wire))

patterns.checkerCells.name: checkerCells
patterns.checkerCells.summary: A checkerboard mask: 1 on one set of squares, 0 on the other, with clean edges at any size.
patterns.checkerCells.description: `cells` counts squares along the canvas height (squares stay square as the canvas resizes). `softness` 0–1 blurs the edges; 0 is crisp. Color it with `strokeOver`.
examples: paint: strokeOver({fill: p('colorA'), stroke: p('colorB'), mask: checkerCells({cells: p('cells'), softness: p('softness')}), space: p('colorSpace')})
tips: Stays sharp inside a distortion, which makes it a good test pattern for warps.

patterns.stripeBands.name: stripeBands
patterns.stripeBands.summary: A mask of straight parallel stripes that scroll with the layer's clock.
patterns.stripeBands.description: `angle` is in degrees. `density` is the number of stripe pairs across the canvas height. `balance` 0–1 is how much of each pair is the 0 side (the fill in `strokeOver`). `softness` 0–1 blurs the edges. `offset` shifts the phase; 1 is one whole pair. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition; speed 0 holds the stripes still.
examples: paint: strokeOver({fill: p('colorA'), stroke: p('colorB'), mask: stripeBands({angle: p('angle'), density: p('density'), balance: p('balance'), softness: p('softness'), offset: p('offset')}), space: p('colorSpace')})
patterns.stripeBands.signature:
stripeBands(slots: {
    angle: PropRef
    density: PropRef
    balance: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
}): PatternPaint

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    angle: PropRef
    density: PropRef
    balance: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
}

patterns.zigzagBands.name: zigzagBands
patterns.zigzagBands.summary: A mask of chevron (zigzag) stripes that scroll with the layer's clock.
patterns.zigzagBands.description: `count` is the number of stripe pairs across the canvas. `angle` is in degrees. `balance` 0–1 is how much of each pair is the 0 side. `softness` 0–1 blurs the edges. `offset` shifts the phase; 1 is one whole pair. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition.
examples: const bands = zigzagBands({count: p('count'), angle: p('angle'), balance: p('balance'), softness: p('softness'), offset: p('offset')})
tips: Reuse one `bands` value for both the color mix and an alpha mix. It is evaluated once.
patterns.zigzagBands.signature:
zigzagBands(slots: {
    count: PropRef
    angle: PropRef
    balance: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
}): PatternPaint

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    count: PropRef
    angle: PropRef
    balance: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
}

patterns.ringWaves.name: ringWaves
patterns.ringWaves.summary: A mask of concentric rings spreading out from a point, animated by the layer's clock.
patterns.ringWaves.description: `center` is a position prop. `frequency` sets how tightly the rings pack; higher is more rings. `thickness` 0–1 is how much of each ring period is ring (0.5 is even bands, 1 is solid). `softness` 0–3 blurs the ring edges. `phase` is in radians. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition; positive speed moves the rings outward.
examples: paint: strokeOver({fill: p('colorB'), stroke: p('colorA'), mask: ringWaves({center: p('center'), frequency: p('frequency'), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), phase: p('phase')})})
tips: Keep `softness` above 0. At exactly 0 the edge is an undefined hard step rather than a crisp one.
patterns.ringWaves.signature:
ringWaves(slots: {
    center: PropRef
    frequency: PropRef
    thickness: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    phase: PropRef
}): PatternPaint

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    center: PropRef
    frequency: PropRef
    thickness: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    phase: PropRef
}

patterns.fallingStreaks.name: fallingStreaks
patterns.fallingStreaks.summary: Streaks that fall across the canvas in columns, each column at its own random speed.
patterns.fallingStreaks.description: Returns two values: `mask` is the streak coverage, and `fade` runs from 0 at the tail to 1 at the leading edge, for a color ramp along each streak. `angle` is in degrees (90 falls down, 0 moves right). `density` is the number of columns across the canvas. `speedVariance` 0–1 spreads the per-column speeds. `trailLength` 0–1 is the streak length as a fraction of the spacing. `strokeWidth` 0–1 is the width as a fraction of a column. `rounding` 0–1 rounds the leading cap. `balance` 0–1 moves the midpoint of `fade`. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition.

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    angle: PropRef
    density: PropRef
    speedVariance: PropRef
    trailLength: PropRef
    strokeWidth: PropRef
    rounding: PropRef
    balance: PropRef
}

patterns.dotLattice.name: dotLattice
patterns.dotLattice.summary: A mask of round dots on a square grid, with optional row stagger, drift and twinkle.
patterns.dotLattice.description: `density` counts dots along the canvas height. `dotSize` 0–1 is the dot diameter as a fraction of a cell; 1 touches the neighbours. `offset` 0–1 shifts every other row (0.5 is the polka-dot stagger). `speedVariance` 0–1 gives rows different drift speeds. `twinkle` 0–1 pulses each dot on its own phase. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition; the drift follows that clock while the twinkle keeps running at speed 0.
examples: paint: withAlpha(p('color'), dotLattice({density: p('density'), dotSize: p('dotSize'), offset: p('offset'), speedVariance: p('speedVariance'), twinkle: p('twinkle')}))
tips: Add `sampleMapsAtCellCentres` when `dotSize` or `twinkle` is map-driven, so dots grow whole instead of being clipped.
patterns.dotLattice.signature:
dotLattice(slots: {
    density: PropRef
    dotSize: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
    speedVariance: PropRef
    twinkle: PropRef
}): PatternPaint

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    density: PropRef
    dotSize: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
    speedVariance: PropRef
    twinkle: PropRef
}

patterns.gridLines.name: gridLines
patterns.gridLines.summary: Square grid lines drawn in a `cellFrame`, plus a per-cell shade for the fill.
patterns.gridLines.description: Returns `lines` (1 on a line, 0 inside a cell) and `shade` (a brightness factor around 1 for `vary`). `thickness` 1 draws lines about 2% of a cell wide; 0 draws none. `softness` 0–1 blurs the lines. `variation` 0–1 sets how far `shade` strays from 1. Draw it with the `'flippedY'` convention.
examples:
const field = gridLines({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'flippedY'}), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), variation: p('variation')})
// paint: strokeOver({fill: vary(p('cellColor'), field.shade), stroke: p('color'), mask: field.lines, space: p('colorSpace')})
tips: Rotate the frame 45 degrees for a diamond crosshatch.

params.name: slots

patterns.hexLines.name: hexLines
patterns.hexLines.summary: Honeycomb lines (pointy-top hexagons) drawn in a `cellFrame`, plus a per-cell shade.
patterns.hexLines.description: Returns `lines` (1 on a line) and `shade` (a brightness factor around 1 for `vary`). `thickness` 1 draws lines about 2% of a cell wide; 0 draws none. `softness` 0–1 blurs the lines. `variation` 0–1 sets how far `shade` strays from 1. Draw it with the `'clockwise'` convention.
examples: const field = hexLines({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'clockwise'}), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), variation: p('variation')})

params.name: slots

patterns.triangleLines.name: triangleLines
patterns.triangleLines.summary: A lattice of equilateral triangles drawn in a `cellFrame`, with rows that can drift.
patterns.triangleLines.description: Returns `lines` (1 on a line) and `shade` (a brightness factor around 1 per triangle for `vary`). `thickness` 1 draws lines about 4% of a cell wide; 0 draws none. `softness` 0–1 blurs the lines. `variation` 0–1 sets how far `shade` strays from 1. `speedVariance` 0–1 gives rows different drift speeds. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition; speed 0 holds still. Draw it with the `'flippedY'` convention.
examples: const field = triangleLines({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'flippedY'}), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), variation: p('variation'), speedVariance: p('speedVariance')})

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    frame: PatternPaint
    thickness: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    variation: PropRef
    speedVariance: PropRef
}

patterns.brickCourses.name: brickCourses
patterns.brickCourses.summary: A brick wall: staggered rows with mortar gaps, optional rotation and per-row drift.
patterns.brickCourses.description: Returns `bricks` (1 on a brick, 0 in the mortar) and `shade` (a brightness factor around 1 per brick for `vary`). `cellsX` is bricks per row across the canvas width and `cellsY` the number of rows down its height. `mortar` 0–1 widens the gaps (1 is 30% of a brick), equal in pixels both ways. `softness` 0–1 blurs the edges. `variation` 0–1 sets how far `shade` strays from 1. `rotation` is in degrees. `offset` slides the rows; 1 is one brick. `speedVariance` 0–1 and `seed` randomise the per-row drift. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition. It brings its own frame, so there is no `frame` slot.
examples:
const field = brickCourses({cellsX: p('cellsX'), cellsY: p('cellsY'), mortar: p('mortar'), softness: p('softness'), variation: p('variation'), rotation: p('rotation'), offset: p('offset'), speedVariance: p('speedVariance'), seed: p('seed')})
// paint: strokeOver({fill: p('colorMortar'), stroke: vary(p('colorBrick'), field.shade), mask: field.bricks, space: p('colorSpace')})
patterns.brickCourses.signature:
brickCourses(slots: {
    cellsX: PropRef
    cellsY: PropRef
    mortar: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    variation: PropRef
    rotation: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
    speedVariance: PropRef
    seed: PropRef
}): {bricks: PatternPaint; shade: PatternPaint}

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    cellsX: PropRef
    cellsY: PropRef
    mortar: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    variation: PropRef
    rotation: PropRef
    offset: PropRef
    speedVariance: PropRef
    seed: PropRef
}

patterns.truchetArcs.name: truchetArcs
patterns.truchetArcs.summary: A maze of quarter-circle arcs, two per tile, flipped at random so they join into flowing curves.
patterns.truchetArcs.description: Returns the arc mask (1 on an arc). `thickness` 2 draws arcs about 2% of a tile wide; 0 draws none. `softness` 0–1 blurs the edges. `seed` picks a different set of flips. Draw it in a `'clockwise'` `cellFrame`.
examples: paint: strokeOver({fill: p('colorA'), stroke: p('colorB'), mask: truchetArcs({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'clockwise'}), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), seed: p('seed')}), space: p('colorSpace')})

params.name: slots

patterns.weaveThreads.name: weaveThreads
patterns.weaveThreads.summary: Two sets of threads woven over and under each other, returned as a finished color.
patterns.weaveThreads.description: `gap` 0–0.5 is the empty margin on each side of a thread, as a fraction of a cell; 0 packs them tight. `colors` is `[horizontal, vertical]`. The gaps are transparent, so this goes straight into `paint:`. Draw it in a `'plain'` `cellFrame`.
examples: paint: weaveThreads({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'plain'}), gap: p('gap'), colors: [p('colorA'), p('colorB')]})

params.name: slots

patterns.isoCubeFaces.name: isoCubeFaces
patterns.isoCubeFaces.summary: Tumbling blocks: three shaded rhombus faces per hexagon that read as a field of 3D cubes.
patterns.isoCubeFaces.description: Returns three values. `tone` is the face shading (1 on top, 0.74 on the right, 0.5 on the left) to multiply into the cube color. `random` is a 0–1 value per cube for varying cube colors. `wire` is the edge-line mask (1 on an edge). `thickness` 1 draws edges about 4% of a cell wide; 0 draws none. `softness` 0–1 blurs them. Draw it in a `'clockwise'` `cellFrame`.
examples:
const faces = isoCubeFaces({frame: cellFrame({cells: p('cells'), rotation: p('rotation'), convention: 'clockwise'}), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness')})
// paint: opaque(mixOf(times(rgbOf(cubeColor), faces.tone), rgbOf(p('lineColor')), faces.wire))

params.name: slots

patterns.dotScreenMask.name: dotScreenMask
patterns.dotScreenMask.summary: The dot coverage of one halftone screen: 1 inside a dot, 0 between, with the dot size set by an ink amount.
patterns.dotScreenMask.description: A raw building block for a custom press inside a gather `build`. `uv` is the pixel's uv and `aspect` the canvas aspect (`ctx.uv`, `ctx.aspect`). `angle` is the screen angle in degrees. `intensity` 0–1 is the ink amount at this pixel; 0 leaves no dot. `frequency` is the number of dots down the canvas height.
examples: const dots = dotScreenMask(ctx.uv, ctx.aspect, uniforms.angle, intensity, uniforms.frequency)
patterns.dotScreenMask.signature: dotScreenMask(uv: Expr, aspect: Expr, angle: Expr, intensity: Expr, frequency: Expr): Expr

patterns.inkTransmission.name: inkTransmission
patterns.inkTransmission.summary: How much light passes one ink plate: white where the dot mask is 0, the ink color where it is 1.
patterns.inkTransmission.description: Returns RGB. Multiply the plates together over a paper color to lay the inks down in order. The ink's alpha scales its strength.
examples: printed = printed.mul(inkTransmission(uniforms.cyanColor, dotScreenMask(ctx.uv, ctx.aspect, uniforms.cyanAngle, cyan, uniforms.frequency)))

patterns.dotScreen.name: dotScreen
patterns.dotScreen.summary: A classic halftone filter: the layer inside it redrawn as a grid of dots that grow where it is bright.
patterns.dotScreen.description: Goes in `effect:`. `angle` is the screen angle in degrees (45 is the print default). `frequency` is the number of dots down the canvas height. The dots keep the child's own color; between dots the output is transparent.
examples: effect: dotScreen({angle: p('angle'), frequency: p('frequency')})

patterns.inkPlate.name: inkPlate
patterns.inkPlate.description: `channel` is `'cyan'`, `'magenta'`, `'yellow'` or `'black'`. `screenAngle` is an angle prop in degrees and `ink` a color prop. Plates print in the order you list them.
examples: inkPlate({channel: 'cyan', screenAngle: p('cyanAngle'), ink: p('cyanColor')})

patterns.cmykPress.name: cmykPress
patterns.cmykPress.summary: A four-color print filter: the layer inside it separated into ink plates, each screened into dots at its own angle and laid down on paper in order.
patterns.cmykPress.description: Goes in `effect:`. `paper` is the color shown where no ink lands. `frequency` is the number of dots down the canvas height. `misprint` offsets each plate in uv (0 is perfect registration, 0.005 is visible fringing), in a direction that turns a quarter turn per plate starting from `misprintAngle` (degrees). `plates` is a list from `inkPlate`; the standard screen angles are cyan 15, magenta 75, yellow 0, black 45. The result keeps the child's alpha.
examples: effect: cmykPress({paper: p('paperColor'), frequency: p('frequency'), misprint: p('misprint'), misprintAngle: p('misprintAngle'), plates: [inkPlate({channel: 'cyan', screenAngle: p('cyanAngle'), ink: p('cyanColor')}), inkPlate({channel: 'black', screenAngle: p('blackAngle'), ink: p('blackColor')})]})
tips: Any subset of the four plates works. Two plates give a duotone or risograph look.
patterns.cmykPress.signature:
cmykPress(slots: {
    paper: PropRef
    frequency: PropRef
    misprint: PropRef
    misprintAngle: PropRef
    plates: InkPlateSpec[]
}): GatherEffect

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    paper: PropRef
    frequency: PropRef
    misprint: PropRef
    misprintAngle: PropRef
    plates: InkPlateSpec[]
}

patterns.chosenBy.name: chosenBy
patterns.chosenBy.summary: Picks one whole effect recipe from a select prop, decided when the shader compiles.
patterns.chosenBy.description: `prop` must be a `compileTime: true` prop. `read` turns its raw value into one of the keys of `recipes`; accept both the option string and its transformed value. Every recipe must be a gather effect with the same alpha handling and no setup step, or this throws as soon as it is called.
examples: effect: chosenBy(p('style'), (raw) => (raw === 'cmyk' || raw === 1 ? 'cmyk' : 'classic'), {classic: dotScreen({angle: p('angle'), frequency: p('frequency')}), cmyk: cmykPress({paper: p('paperColor'), frequency: p('frequency'), misprint: p('misprint'), misprintAngle: p('misprintAngle'), plates})})
tips: Changing the prop recompiles the shader, which is the point: each style pays only for its own code.
patterns.chosenBy.signature: chosenBy<K extends string>(prop: PropRef, read: (raw: unknown) => K, recipes: Record<K, GatherEffect>): GatherEffect

patterns.pixelGrid.name: pixelGrid
patterns.pixelGrid.summary: The pixel grid of a dither: the layer inside it chopped into square cells of a given size.
patterns.pixelGrid.description: `size` is a prop in pixels of the authored frame, so the cell count stays the same when the canvas renders at a higher resolution. Build it once and pass the same grid to `quantise` and `ditherInks`.
examples: const grid = pixelGrid({size: p('pixelSize')})

patterns.quantise.name: quantise
patterns.quantise.summary: Reduces each grid cell of the layer inside to 0 or 1 using a dither pattern.
patterns.quantise.description: Returns a per-pixel level for `ditherInks`. `pattern` is a `compileTime: true` select prop with one of `bayer2`, `bayer4`, `bayer8`, `clusteredDot`, `blueNoise`, `whiteNoise` or `floydSteinberg`. `threshold` 0–1 shifts the cut point; 0.5 is neutral. `spread` 0–1 is how much of the brightness range dithers; lower leaves more solid areas.
examples: const levels = quantise({grid, pattern: p('pattern'), threshold: p('threshold'), spread: p('spread')})
tips: Floyd–Steinberg is the costliest pattern: it re-reads 64 cells per pixel. Bayer 4 is the cheap default.
patterns.quantise.signature: quantise(slots: {grid: PixelGrid; pattern: PropRef; threshold: PropRef; spread: PropRef}): GatherStage

params.name: slots
params.type: {grid: PixelGrid; pattern: PropRef; threshold: PropRef; spread: PropRef}

patterns.ditherInks.name: ditherInks
patterns.ditherInks.summary: A dither filter: colors the 0/1 levels from `quantise`, either with two colors of your own or with darkened and brightened versions of the layer's own pixels.
patterns.ditherInks.description: Goes in `effect:`. `mode` is a `compileTime: true` select prop, `'custom'` or `'source'`. `colors` is `[dark, light]` for custom mode; a transparent dark color lets the background show through.
examples: effect: ditherInks({grid, levels: quantise({grid, pattern: p('pattern'), threshold: p('threshold'), spread: p('spread')}), mode: p('colorMode'), colors: [p('colorA'), p('colorB')]})

params.name: slots

figures.strokedSegment.name: strokedSegment
figures.strokedSegment.summary: A straight line between two points, solid, dashed or dotted, with square or round ends.
figures.strokedSegment.description: Dashes and dots are spaced so the pattern lands exactly on both endpoints. The edge stays antialiased at any thickness. Style and cap inputs are numbers, so give a select prop a `transform` that maps its labels to them, or pass the number directly.
examples: paint: strokedSegment({from: p('pointA'), to: p('pointB'), width: p('thickness'), style: 1, dashLength: p('dashLength'), gapLength: p('gapLength'), capStart: 1, capEnd: 1, color: p('color')})

figures.sineStroke.name: sineStroke
figures.sineStroke.summary: A wavy line that travels along itself, drawn as a soft band.
figures.sineStroke.description: The wave is centered on `position` and turned by `angle`. It moves on the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`.
examples: paint: sineStroke({position: p('position'), angle: p('angle'), frequency: p('frequency'), amplitude: p('amplitude'), thickness: p('thickness'), softness: p('softness'), color: p('color')})

compose.layered.name: layered
compose.layered.summary: Builds N variations of one thing from a data list and sums them with weights.
compose.layered.description: Give it a list of plain data and a function that turns one entry into `{value, weight}`. You get `weightedSum` and `totalWeight` back and choose the blend yourself, usually `weightedSum / (totalWeight + 0.001)`. Slice the list to change how many layers are built.
examples: const {weightedSum, totalWeight} = layered(CURTAINS.slice(0, count), ({offset, weight}) => ({value: curtain(offset), weight: math.mul(alpha, weight)}))
tips: Cheap depth: aurora curtains, cloud banks, echo trails are all a few layers of one recipe.
compose.layered.signature: layered<T>(layerData: readonly T[], build: (layer: T, index: number) => {value: Expr; weight: Expr}): {weightedSum: Expr; totalWeight: Expr}

params.name: build
params.type: (layer: T, index: number) => {value: Expr; weight: Expr}

compose.layers.name: layers
compose.layers.summary: Stacks colors into one, first entry at the back.
compose.layers.description: Each entry is a color, or `{paint, blend, opacity, behind}` (see `Layer`). Entries add together unless one asks for `'screen'`. Needs at least one entry.
examples:
const rgb = layers([
  {paint: sky, opacity: 0.6},
  {paint: stars, behind: fog.transmittance},
  {paint: glow, blend: 'screen'},
])

compose.emissiveAlpha.name: emissiveAlpha
compose.emissiveAlpha.summary: Turns an rgb light value into a color with alpha, so glows composite over transparency.
compose.emissiveAlpha.description: Alpha is the brightest channel and the color is scaled up to match, so over black the layer looks exactly like the light it is, and over anything else like a translucent tint. Use it as the last step of a glow, spill or flare. Not for opaque bodies.
examples: paint: (params) => compose.emissiveAlpha(math.mul(params.uniforms.color.member('rgb'), coverage))

compose.dithered.name: dithered
compose.dithered.summary: Adds a tiny amount of noise to a final color so long soft gradients show no banding.
compose.dithered.description: Apply it to the finished rgba, never to a value that still feeds a palette.
examples: paint: (params) => dithered(standardPalette(field, params), params)

media.imageMedia.name: imageMedia
media.imageMedia.summary: An image from a URL prop, fitted into the layer.
media.imageMedia.description: The layer is transparent until the image loads, then shows it at its real aspect ratio. Set `naturalSizeKey: {fromProp: 'url'}` on the definition so layout can measure the image. `onError` receives load failures with the URL so you can phrase the message.
examples: ...imageMedia({src: p('url'), fit: p('objectFit'), decode: 'srgb-linear-alpha-cut', label: 'Photo'})

params.name: opts

media.videoMedia.name: videoMedia
media.videoMedia.summary: A video from a URL prop, playing in the layer.
media.videoMedia.description: The video plays muted and inline. `loop` is a boolean prop. `metadataTimeoutMs` is how long to wait for the video's metadata before reporting a failure. Set `naturalSizeKey: {fromProp: 'url'}` on the definition. `onError` tells you whether loading (`'acquire'`) or playback (`'autoplay'`) failed.
examples: ...videoMedia({src: p('url'), fit: p('objectFit'), loop: p('loop'), decode: 'srgb-linear-alpha-cut', metadataTimeoutMs: 10000})

params.name: opts

media.webcamMedia.name: webcamMedia
media.webcamMedia.summary: The user's camera, live in the layer.
media.webcamMedia.description: Asks for camera permission with your `constraints`. `mirror` is a boolean prop for a selfie flip that updates instantly. This word also accepts `fit: 'none'` to show the feed at its native pixel size. Set `naturalSizeKey: {fixed: '<key>'}` on the definition and pass the same key here. `onError` receives permission denials and playback failures.
examples: ...webcamMedia({fit: p('objectFit'), mirror: p('mirror'), decode: 'srgb-linear-alpha-cut', constraints: {video: {facingMode: 'user'}}, naturalSizeKey: 'webcam'})

params.name: opts

noise.waves.name: waves
noise.waves.summary: Overlapping traveling sine waves from a schedule written as data: the organic wobble behind blob edges, water lines and drifting fills.
noise.waves.description: Pass the coordinates to wave over (`x`, optionally `y`, and `t` for the layer's clock) and a list of terms. Each term multiplies its waves and the terms add up. The result is signed: one wave runs −1 to 1, a schedule runs within about ±(sum of weights). It returns an expression, not a field, so it slots into `paint: (params) => …` recipes and math.
examples:
const wobble = waves({x: delta.member('x'), y: delta.member('y'), t: time}, [
  {waves: [{x: 3, t: 0.8}, {y: 2.2, t: -0.5}]},
  {waves: [{x: 5.1, y: -3.3, t: 0.6}], weight: 0.5},
])
tips: Keep the schedule as constants next to the definition. It is the look, so keep it where you can tune it.
noise.waves.signature: waves(axes: {x: Expr | number; y?: Expr | number; t?: Expr | number}, schedule: WaveTerm[]): Expr

params.name: axes
params.type: {x: Expr | number; y?: Expr | number; t?: Expr | number}

noise.wavyLine.name: wavyLine
noise.wavyLine.summary: The height of an animated wavy line at a point along it: a stack of traveling sines.
noise.wavyLine.description: `along` is the coordinate along the line and `time` the layer's clock. Each wave has a `freq` (tightness), a `speed` (drift along the clock), an `amount` (height) and an optional `phase` in radians. Signed, within ±(sum of amounts). Add it to a baseline to get the curve. Give each line of a family its own `hashPhase` so they do not move in step.
examples: const arc = wavyLine({along: x, time: t, waves: [{freq: 1.4, speed: 0.3, amount: 0.5}, {freq: 3.1, speed: -0.2, amount: 0.2}]})

params.name: opts

noise.organicWaves.name: organicWaves
noise.organicWaves.summary: A ready-made `waves` schedule from three knobs, for when you have no hand-tuned constants.
noise.organicWaves.description: `frequency` sets the size of the largest waves. `detail` is how many finer layers stack on top (default 3, each about 1.8× finer and half as strong). `drift` is the animation speed (default 0.5). The same `seed` always gives the same schedule. Weights are normalized so the summed wave stays within about −1 to 1. Treat the result as a starting point to tune.
examples: const wobble = waves({x: delta.member('x'), y: delta.member('y'), t: time}, organicWaves({frequency: 3, detail: 3, drift: 0.4}))
tips: The schedule uses x, y and t, so the axes you pass to `waves` must provide all three.
noise.organicWaves.signature: organicWaves(opts: {frequency: number; detail?: number; drift?: number; seed?: number}): WaveTerm[]

params.name: opts
params.type: {frequency: number; detail?: number; drift?: number; seed?: number}

noise.foldSet.name: foldSet
noise.foldSet.summary: Lays out the ridges of a draped cloth: `count` folds spread evenly across `spread`, each nudged sideways, widened and raised by a seeded amount so no two are alike.
noise.foldSet.description: `spread` is the distance the folds cover across the drape, in the units you will pass as `across` to `drapedFolds` (the canvas aspect for a full-width curtain). `width` and `height` are the typical ridge size. `jitter` (0–1, default 0.6) is how far a fold may wander from its even slot. The same `seed` always gives the same layout. `count` is a plain number, so drive it from a compile-time prop.
examples: const folds = foldSet({count: 7, seed: u.seed, spread: aspect, width: u.foldWidth, height: u.foldDepth})
tips: Call it once, outside any height function: the layout is the same at every tap.
noise.foldSet.signature:
foldSet(opts: {
    count: number
    seed: Expr | number
    spread: Expr | number
    width: Expr | number
    height: Expr | number
    jitter?: number
}): Fold[]

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    count: number
    seed: Expr | number
    spread: Expr | number
    width: Expr | number
    height: Expr | number
    jitter?: number
}

noise.drapedFolds.name: drapedFolds
noise.drapedFolds.summary: The height of a draped cloth at a point: rounded ridges running along one direction, each rippling and swaying along its length, gathered where the cloth is pinned.
noise.drapedFolds.description: `coords` come from a `directionFrame`: `along` runs 0 at the pinned edge to 1 at the free edge, `across` is the distance across the drape in the units `foldSet` laid the folds out in. `ripple.waves` is a `wavyLine` wave list each spine wanders by (every fold starts at its own phase) and `ripple.gain` scales it. `sway` moves all the folds together on the clock, like a breeze. `swell` makes each ridge rise and fall along its length so neighbours merge and part. `pinning` (0–1) gathers the folds at the pinned edge: narrow and still there, wide and free at the far edge. `sharpness` (default 2) is how tightly the ridge falls away and `crease` (0–1, default 0) flattens its crest into a plateau that meets the next fold in a tight valley: 0 is a round bell, 1 a flat face with a sharp crease. The result is a height in the units of each fold's `height`. Take its slope with `fdSlope` or `fdCurvature` for relief.
examples:
const cloth = (at: Expr) => drapedFolds(drape.coordsOf(at), folds, {time: t, ripple: {waves: RIPPLE}, sway: {amount: breeze}, pinning: u.pinning})
const relief = fdCurvature(cloth, q, 0.004)
tips: Keep the wave list and swell as constants next to the definition. They are the look.
noise.drapedFolds.signature: drapedFolds(coords: {along: Expr | number; across: Expr | number}, folds: Fold[], opts: DrapeOptions): Expr

noise.clothCoords.name: clothCoords
noise.clothCoords.summary: Where on the unfolded cloth a point lands: the material coordinates to draw a pattern in, so it follows the folds instead of floating over them.
noise.clothCoords.description: Takes the same `coords`, `folds` and options as `drapedFolds`. The cloth riding each ridge moves sideways with its spine, and each flank uses up cloth, so a pattern drawn in these coordinates bends with the ripples and bunches on the steep sides of every ridge. `foreshorten` (default 0.25) is how much cloth a flank consumes. Rebuild a point from the result with the drape's frame and hand it to a grain word in place of the screen point.
tips: One more pass over the folds per pixel. Call it once and reuse the point.
noise.clothCoords.signature: clothCoords(coords: {along: Expr | number; across: Expr | number}, folds: Fold[], opts: DrapeOptions & {foreshorten?: number}): {along: Expr; across: Expr}

noise.seededPlane.name: seededPlane
noise.seededPlane.summary: Frames a field on a zoomable plane: how big the pattern is and where it starts.
noise.seededPlane.description: Takes the canvas position, corrects it for aspect ratio, zooms it by `scale` and slides it by `seed`, then hands a 2D pattern position to the field inside. `scale` is exponential: each +1 makes the pattern about 2.7× finer, so a slider from −2 to 5 runs from coarse to fine. A different `seed` shows a different part of the pattern. The framing every noise texture opens with.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(unitized(gaborGrains({frequency: p('frequency')})), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')})), stops(p('colorSpace')))
tips: `noiseField` bases take a 3D position. Put `evolving` between `seededPlane` and the basis, even at `rate: 0`, to supply the third axis.
noise.seededPlane.signature: seededPlane(field: Field, slots: {scale: PropRef; seed: PropRef}): Field

noise.pixelGrid.name: pixelGrid
noise.pixelGrid.summary: Frames a field on the pixel grid: one value per block of `grain` device pixels.
noise.pixelGrid.description: For patterns that live on pixels rather than on the canvas (blue noise, dither). `grain` is the block size in pixels (1 = every pixel), `seed` picks a different block of the pattern. The field inside gets whole-number pixel coordinates.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(pixelGrid(blueSpeckle(), {grain: p('grain'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
noise.pixelGrid.signature: pixelGrid(field: Field, slots: {grain: PropRef; seed: PropRef}): Field

noise.scaledPlane.name: scaledPlane
noise.scaledPlane.summary: Frames a field on the aspect-corrected canvas plane, zoomed by a plain multiplier.
noise.scaledPlane.description: Unlike `seededPlane`, `scale` is linear: roughly the number of pattern cells across the canvas height. There is no seed. The position is computed once, so a recipe whose parts read it several times pays for it once.
examples: paint: rampOver(unitized(scaledPlane(waveletBands({detail: p('detail')}), {scale: p('scale')})), stops(p('colorSpace')))

noise.evolving.name: evolving
noise.evolving.summary: Makes a 3D noise basis morph in place over time instead of sliding across the canvas.
noise.evolving.description: Wraps a basis that takes a 3D position (`noiseField`): the 2D pattern position from the framing outside becomes `(x, y, time × rate)`. `rate` multiplies the layer's clock, on top of the definition's `speed` prop. It sits between the framing and the basis.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(evolving(noiseField('perlin'), {rate: 0.3}), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
tips: The clock is the definition's `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`. Without it nothing moves.

noise.gaborGrains.name: gaborGrains
noise.gaborGrains.summary: Oriented sine grains: short striped patches, each facing a random way, like brushed metal or wood grain.
noise.gaborGrains.description: `frequency` is how many stripes fit in one grain (1 to 24, default 8). The stripes slide along their grain on the layer's clock. Signed, −1 to 1: wrap it in `unitized` before a tone word. Takes a 2D position, so frame it with `seededPlane`.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(unitized(gaborGrains({frequency: p('frequency')})), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

noise.waveletBands.name: waveletBands
noise.waveletBands.summary: Rotating bands of wavelets: layered ripples that turn against each other, a watery interference look.
noise.waveletBands.description: `detail` is the frequency ratio between the four layers (1.05 to 2, default 1.24; higher adds finer ripples). The bands slide on the layer's clock. Signed, about −1 to 1: wrap it in `unitized` before a tone word. Takes a 2D position.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(unitized(waveletBands({detail: p('detail')})), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

noise.blueSpeckle.name: blueSpeckle
noise.blueSpeckle.summary: Fine, even speckle with no clumps: blue noise, one random value per pixel block.
noise.blueSpeckle.description: Still (no animation). Unit range, about 0 to 1, so it feeds `noiseTone` directly. Only makes sense over `pixelGrid`, which gives it the pixel coordinates it expects.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(pixelGrid(blueSpeckle(), {grain: p('grain'), seed: p('seed')})), stops(p('colorSpace')))
tips: A good dither or film-grain layer over another shader at low opacity.

noise.erosionRidges.name: erosionRidges
noise.erosionRidges.summary: Terrain eroded by water: sharp branching ridges with gullies running off them.
noise.erosionRidges.description: Still (no animation). Signed, centred on 0: wrap it in `unitized` before a tone word. Takes a 2D position, so frame it with `seededPlane`.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(unitized(erosionRidges()), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

noise.curlSpeed.name: curlSpeed
noise.curlSpeed.summary: How fast a swirling flow moves at each point: soft eddies and streams that morph in place.
noise.curlSpeed.description: `rate` multiplies the layer's clock. Never negative and mostly 0 to 1, so it feeds `noiseTone` directly. Takes a 2D position, so frame it with `seededPlane`.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(curlSpeed({rate: 0.2}), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

noise.scratchStreaks.name: scratchStreaks
noise.scratchStreaks.summary: Fine hairline scratches, like a scuffed surface, flickering on the layer's clock.
noise.scratchStreaks.description: `thickness` widens the bright core of each streak (0.2 to 5, default 1). The value is 0 off a streak and rises well past 1 on one, so send it through `noiseTone`, which clamps. Takes a 2D position. Works in a `paint:` only, not in a compute pass.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(scratchStreaks({thickness: p('thickness')}), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')})), linearPair(p('colorA'), p('colorB')))

noise.unitized.name: unitized
noise.unitized.summary: Turns a signed field (−1 to 1) into a unit field (0 to 1).
noise.unitized.description: Put it directly around a signed basis (`gaborGrains`, `waveletBands`, `erosionRidges`, `noiseField('mx3signed')`) so `noiseTone` and the palette see 0 to 1. Or skip it and use `signedTone`, which takes the signed value itself.
examples: seededPlane(unitized(gaborGrains({frequency: p('frequency')})), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')})

noise.noiseTone.name: noiseTone
noise.noiseTone.summary: The standard contrast and balance controls of a noise texture, turning a 0–1 field into the ramp position.
noise.noiseTone.description: `contrast` steepens the field around mid-grey (0 = unchanged, positive = sharper, negative = flatter). `balance` shifts the whole range (positive = more of the first color). Leave the slots out for a texture without those controls. The result is flipped: where the field is high the ramp shows its first color. Expects a unit field, so put `unitized` around a signed basis first.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(evolving(noiseField('perlin'), {rate: 0.3}), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
tips: Contrast here is additive: 0 is the identity, not 1. Default the prop to 0.
noise.noiseTone.signature: noiseTone(field: Field, slots?: {contrast?: PropRef; balance?: PropRef}): Field

noise.signedTone.name: signedTone
noise.signedTone.summary: Contrast and balance for a signed field (−1 to 1), applied before it is squashed to 0–1.
noise.signedTone.description: The same controls as `noiseTone` (`contrast` 0 = unchanged, `balance` shifts), but working on the raw signed value lets high contrast push further before it clips. Flipped like `noiseTone`: a high field shows the first color. Use it in place of `unitized` plus `noiseTone`.
examples: paint: rampOver(signedTone(seededPlane(evolving(noiseField('mx3signed'), {rate: 0.5}), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
noise.signedTone.signature: signedTone(field: Field, slots: {contrast: PropRef; balance: PropRef}): Field

noise.gainTone.name: gainTone
noise.gainTone.summary: Contrast as a multiplier and balance as a shift over a 0–1 field, not flipped.
noise.gainTone.description: `contrast` 1 leaves the field alone (a slider from 0.25 to 4 works well) and `balance` shifts it. Low field values read the first color. The tone inside `worleyNoise`. Reach for it when a "1 = normal" contrast slider fits better than `noiseTone`'s "0 = normal".
examples: paint: rampOver(gainTone(cellFill(cellDistances({scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}), {edgeIntensity: p('edgeIntensity')}), {contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))
noise.gainTone.signature: gainTone(field: Field, slots: {contrast: PropRef; balance: PropRef}): Field

noise.linearPair.name: linearPair
noise.linearPair.summary: A two-color palette mixed in linear RGB, for a definition with no color-space prop.
noise.linearPair.description: Reads two color props. Use `pair` or `stops` from paint when the definition has a `colorSpace` prop.
examples: paint: rampOver(noiseTone(seededPlane(scratchStreaks({thickness: p('thickness')}), {scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')})), linearPair(p('colorA'), p('colorB')))

noise.fractalNoise.name: fractalNoise
noise.fractalNoise.summary: A complete fractal-noise paint: layered simplex noise that morphs over time, read through the color ramp.
noise.fractalNoise.description: `angle` rotates the pattern (degrees). `octaves` is how many layers stack (1 to 8, changed live without a recompile), `detail` how much finer each layer is (1 to 4) and `contrast` how much weaker (0.1 to 1). `seed` re-mixes the layers. `space` is the color-space prop. Reads the definition's `colorA`, `colorB` and, when present, `stops` props.
examples: paint: fractalNoise({angle: p('angle'), detail: p('detail'), contrast: p('contrast'), octaves: p('octaves'), seed: p('seed'), space: p('colorSpace')})
tips: Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` on the definition. The morphing runs on the layer's clock.
noise.fractalNoise.signature:
fractalNoise(slots: {
    angle: PropRef
    detail: PropRef
    contrast: PropRef
    octaves: PropRef
    seed: PropRef
    space: PropRef
}): Paint

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    angle: PropRef
    detail: PropRef
    contrast: PropRef
    octaves: PropRef
    seed: PropRef
    space: PropRef
}

noise.worleyNoise.name: worleyNoise
noise.worleyNoise.summary: A complete cellular-noise paint: distances to drifting cell points, read through the color ramp.
noise.worleyNoise.description: `scale` is the number of cells across (1 to 30) and `jitter` how far the points wander from a grid (0 = rigid grid, 1 = random). `mode` picks the distance field: `'f1'` (cells), `'f2'`, `'f2MinusF1'` (edges), `'f1PlusF2'`, `'f1TimesF2'`. `distance` picks the cell shape: `'euclidean'` (round), `'manhattan'` (diamond), `'chebyshev'` (square). `octaves` (1 to 4) stacks finer layers, with `lacunarity` and `persistence` setting how much finer and weaker. `contrast` is a multiplier (1 = unchanged) and `balance` a shift. Low values read the first color. `mode`, `distance` and `octaves` are compile-time props. Reads the definition's `colorA`, `colorB` and, when present, `stops` props.
examples: paint: worleyNoise({scale: p('scale'), jitter: p('jitter'), lacunarity: p('lacunarity'), persistence: p('persistence'), contrast: p('contrast'), balance: p('balance'), seed: p('seed'), mode: p('mode'), distance: p('distance'), octaves: p('octaves'), space: p('colorSpace')})
tips: Give the `mode` and `distance` props `transformWorleyMode` and `transformWorleyDistance` as their `transform`.

params.name: slots

noise.cellDistances.name: cellDistances
noise.cellDistances.summary: Distances from each pixel to its nearest two cell points, as `(d1, d2)`: the raw material for Voronoi fills and borders.
noise.cellDistances.description: `scale` is the number of cells across and `seed` picks a different set of points. The points drift on the layer's clock. Feed it to `cellFill` or `cellBorders`, and wrap it in `share` when both read it.
examples: const cells = share(cellDistances({scale: p('scale'), seed: p('seed')}))

noise.cellFill.name: cellFill
noise.cellFill.summary: A 0–1 fill for each cell: 0 at the cell's point, 1 at its boundary, whatever the cell size.
noise.cellFill.description: `edgeIntensity` (0 to 1) is how far the boundary color reaches into the cell. Takes the `(d1, d2)` field from `cellDistances`. Ramp it directly: the first color lands at the cell centres.
examples: paint: rampOver(cellFill(cells, {edgeIntensity: p('edgeIntensity')}), stops(p('colorSpace')))

noise.cellBorders.name: cellBorders
noise.cellBorders.summary: A mask of the lines between cells: 0 on a boundary, 1 inside a cell.
noise.cellBorders.description: `softness` is the line width (0 to about 0.4). Pass the same `scale` as `cellDistances` so the lines keep their width when the cell count changes. Takes the `(d1, d2)` field. Use it as the `mask` of `borderOverlay`.
examples: cellBorders(cells, {softness: p('edgeSoftness'), scale: p('scale')})
noise.cellBorders.signature: cellBorders(cells: Field, slots: {softness: PropRef; scale: PropRef}): Field

noise.borderOverlay.name: borderOverlay
noise.borderOverlay.summary: Draws a color over a paint wherever a mask falls to 0, keeping the paint's alpha.
noise.borderOverlay.description: `mask` is 1 where the paint shows through and 0 where `color` covers it. The Voronoi border move: fill the cells, then overlay the border lines.
examples: paint: borderOverlay(rampOver(cellFill(cells, {edgeIntensity: p('edgeIntensity')}), stops(p('colorSpace'))), cellBorders(cells, {softness: p('edgeSoftness'), scale: p('scale')}), {color: p('colorBorder')})
noise.borderOverlay.signature: borderOverlay(paint: Paint, mask: Field, slots: {color: PropRef}): Paint

noise.overRgb.name: overRgb
noise.overRgb.summary: Runs color-only steps over a paint, in order, leaving its alpha alone.
noise.overRgb.description: This is how `ribbons` is closed: the ribbons come out in the working color space, `backToP3` brings them to display color and `tonePow` lifts them.
examples:
const strands = ribbons({from: p('start'), to: p('end'), count: p('lineCount'), width: p('lineWidth'), amplitude: p('amplitude'), frequency: p('frequency'), softness: p('softness'), spread: p('spread'), pinEdges: p('pinEdges'), colorScale: p('colorScale'), colorVariance: p('colorVariance')})
paint: overRgb(strands, backToP3({space: p('colorSpace')}), tonePow())

noise.backToP3.name: backToP3
noise.backToP3.summary: Brings `ribbons` color from its working color space back to display color.
noise.backToP3.description: `space` is the definition's compile-time color-space prop; leave it out for linear. Put it first in `overRgb`, right after the ribbons.
examples: paint: overRgb(strands, backToP3({space: p('colorSpace')}), tonePow())

noise.tonePow.name: tonePow
noise.tonePow.summary: A gentle lift of the mid-tones (rgb to the power 0.85), as an `overRgb` step.
examples: paint: overRgb(strands, backToP3({space: p('colorSpace')}), tonePow())

noise.ribbons.name: ribbons
noise.ribbons.summary: Flowing gradient-colored ribbons between two points: the Strands look.
noise.ribbons.description: `from` and `to` are position props. `count` is how many ribbons, `width` and `softness` their thickness and edge (0 to 1), `spread` how far apart they sit (0 to 1), `amplitude` and `frequency` the size and tightness of the wave (0 to 5). `pinEdges` is a boolean prop that gathers the ribbons at both ends. `colorScale` (1 to 6) is how many times the gradient repeats along a ribbon and `colorVariance` (0 to 1) how far each ribbon is offset in it. The gradient comes from the definition's `stops` prop. The color comes out in the working color space, so close it with `overRgb(ribbons(…), backToP3({space}), tonePow())`. The wave runs on `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` and the colors scroll on a second clock, `extraAnimatedTimes: {color: 'colorSpeed'}`. Declare both on the definition.
examples:
paint: overRgb(
  ribbons({from: p('start'), to: p('end'), count: p('lineCount'), width: p('lineWidth'), amplitude: p('amplitude'), frequency: p('frequency'), softness: p('softness'), spread: p('spread'), pinEdges: p('pinEdges'), colorScale: p('colorScale'), colorVariance: p('colorVariance')}),
  backToP3({space: p('colorSpace')}),
  tonePow(),
)
tips: Add `stops: colorStopsPropConfig()` to the props. The ribbons read the stop list, not `colorA` / `colorB`.

    to: PropRef
    count: PropRef
    width: PropRef

    frequency: PropRef
    softness: PropRef
    spread: PropRef
    pinEdges: PropRef
    colorScale: PropRef
    colorVariance: PropRef
}): Paint

noise.reliefBases.stone.name: stone
noise.reliefBases.stone.signature: reliefBases.stone: { readonly fn: TgpuFn<(p: Vec2f) => F32>; readonly hint: "stone12"; }

noise.reliefBases.wool.name: wool
noise.reliefBases.wool.signature: reliefBases.wool: { readonly fn: TgpuFn<(p: Vec2f) => F32>; readonly hint: "wool12"; }

noise.reliefBases.name: reliefBases
noise.reliefBases.summary: The height fields `noiseRelief` accepts: `stone` (marbled stone) and `wool` (interwoven fibres).
examples: gpu: {fragment: noiseRelief(reliefBases.wool)}

noise.noiseRelief.name: noiseRelief
noise.noiseRelief.summary: Embosses the layer inside with a textured surface: the child is slightly distorted, then lit by a height field so it reads as carved stone or woven cloth.
noise.noiseRelief.description: A filter, not a paint. Set it as the definition's fragment with `requiresRTT` and `requiresChild`, and give the definition props named `intensity`, `scale`, `contrast`, `distortion` and `seed`. `basis` is an entry of `reliefBases`.
examples:
export const Stone = defineShader({
  name: 'Stone',
  requiresRTT: true,
  requiresChild: true,
  props: {intensity: {default: 0.5}, scale: {default: 1}, contrast: {default: 0}, distortion: {default: 0.15}, seed: {default: 0}},
  gpu: {fragment: noiseRelief(reliefBases.stone)},
})
tips: The library shaders build those five props with `reliefStylizeProps` from the utilities, which also sets their sliders.

noise.transformWorleyMode.name: transformWorleyMode
noise.transformWorleyMode.summary: The `transform` for a `worleyNoise` `mode` prop: maps `'f1'`, `'f2'`, `'f2MinusF1'`, `'f1PlusF2'` or `'f1TimesF2'` to the number the paint reads.
examples: mode: {default: 'f1', transform: transformWorleyMode, compileTime: true}

noise.transformWorleyDistance.name: transformWorleyDistance
noise.transformWorleyDistance.summary: The `transform` for a `worleyNoise` `distance` prop: maps `'euclidean'`, `'manhattan'` or `'chebyshev'` to the number the paint reads.
examples: distance: {default: 'euclidean', transform: transformWorleyDistance, compileTime: true}

light.rayBands.name: rayBands
light.rayBands.summary: Bright bands that travel along a coordinate, for aurora curtains or shimmering rays.
light.rayBands.description: Returns a 0–1 field. `along` is the coordinate the bands cross (a uv axis, or a noise-warped one for organic rays), `frequency` the band count per unit of it, and `time` × `speed` how fast they travel. `sharpness` above 1 narrows the bright bands.
examples: const rays = rayBands({along: params.ctx.uv.member('x'), frequency: 12, time: animatedTime(params), speed: 0.3, sharpness: 2})
tips: Add a noise field to `along` before passing it and the straight bands turn into curtains.
light.rayBands.signature:
rayBands(opts: {
    along: Expr
    frequency: Expr | number
    time: Expr | number
    speed: Expr | number
    phase?: Expr | number
    sharpness: Expr | number
}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    along: Expr
    frequency: Expr | number
    time: Expr | number
    speed: Expr | number
    phase?: Expr | number
    sharpness: Expr | number
}

light.emitterFalloff.name: emitterFalloff
light.emitterFalloff.summary: How light spilling from an emitter dims with distance, with a long realistic tail.
light.emitterFalloff.description: Returns 1 at the emitter, softened over `radius`, then fading like real light. `d` and `radius` share a unit (usually aspect-corrected uv). `power` 1 fades like a line of light, `power` 2 like a point. Use it where `glowPoint` looks too much like a soft blob.
examples: const spill = emitterFalloff(frame.member('x'), {radius: p('radius'), power: 2})
light.emitterFalloff.signature: emitterFalloff(d: Expr, opts: {radius: Expr | number; power: Expr | number}): Expr

light.glowAt.name: glowAt
light.glowAt.summary: A soft round glow at a position on the canvas.
light.glowAt.description: Returns a 0–1 field, 1 at the position. `x` and `y` are in uv (0–1, y down), `aspect` is the canvas width over height so the glow stays round, and `sizeSq` is the glow radius squared. Pass several with different positions and sum them with `additive`.
examples: const glow = glowAt({uv: params.ctx.uv, aspect: params.ctx.aspect, x: 0.5, y: 0.4, sizeSq: 0.02})
tips: The radius goes in squared: a glow 0.15 across the canvas is `sizeSq: 0.0225`.
light.glowAt.signature: glowAt(opts: {uv: Expr; aspect: Expr | number; x: Expr | number; y: Expr | number; sizeSq: Expr | number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {uv: Expr; aspect: Expr | number; x: Expr | number; y: Expr | number; sizeSq: Expr | number}

light.domeNormal.name: domeNormal
light.domeNormal.summary: The surface normals of a flat disc treated as a puffy dome, ready to light with `shine`.
light.domeNormal.description: `delta` is the offset from the disc center, `dist` its length and `radius` the disc size, all in the same unit. `bulge.tilt` (default 0.2) sets how far the normals lean outward at the rim and `bulge.drop` (default 0.1) how much the dome flattens toward its edge.
examples: const highlight = shine({normal: domeNormal({delta, dist, radius}), light: vec3(0.3, -0.5, 0.8), gloss: 32})

params.name: opts

light.shine.name: shine
light.shine.summary: A specular highlight on any surface that gives you a normal.
