light.shine.description: Returns the raw 0–1 highlight, viewed straight on. Multiply it by your intensity and the shape's coverage yourself. `light` is a unit direction toward the light and `gloss` sets the highlight's tightness (8 is broad, 32 is a small hot spot). Works with `domeNormal`, a bevel, or a heightfield slope.
examples: const highlight = mul(shine({normal, light: vec3(0.3, -0.5, 0.8), gloss: p('gloss')}), mask)
light.shine.signature: shine(opts: {normal: Expr; light: Expr; gloss: Expr | number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {normal: Expr; light: Expr; gloss: Expr | number}

light.radialFrame.name: radialFrame
light.radialFrame.summary: The frame for a burst, halo or sweep around a center prop.
light.radialFrame.description: Gives each pixel its distance and angle from the center as `vec2(dist, angle)`. Distance is in aspect-corrected uv (0.5 is half the canvas height), the angle in radians. `center` is a position prop. Evaluate parts in it with `withFrame`.
examples: coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), modulate(rayLobes({count: p('rays'), spin: -1, sharpness: 4}), featherMask({radius: p('radius'), feather: 0.5})), 'burst')

light.seamlessRadialFrame.name: seamlessRadialFrame
light.seamlessRadialFrame.summary: The frame `noiseRays` needs: a radial frame around a center prop with no visible seam.
light.seamlessRadialFrame.description: Patterns that repeat around an angle show a line where the angle wraps. This frame carries what a part needs to hide it. Only `noiseRays` reads it. `center` is a position prop.
examples: coverage: withFrame(seamlessRadialFrame(p('center')), noiseRays({density: p('density'), intensity: p('intensity'), spotty: p('spotty')}))
tips: The other radial parts (`glowPoint`, `rayLobes`, `featherMask`) read `radialFrame`, not this one. Its layout is different.

light.beamFrame.name: beamFrame
light.beamFrame.summary: The frame of a beam that starts at an anchor prop and points at the canvas center.
light.beamFrame.description: Gives each pixel its distance along the beam and its sideways offset from it as `vec2(u, v)`, in aspect-corrected uv. Drag the anchor anywhere and the beam still points inward. Built for filters over a child (a light leak inside `screenGlow`), where it reads the child's uv.
examples: const frame = local(beamFrame(p('position'))(params), 'leakFrame')

light.withFrame.name: withFrame
light.withFrame.summary: Evaluate a light part in a frame.
light.withFrame.description: This is where a framed light starts: a frame, then the part (or `modulate` of several) drawn in it. Pass a name as the third argument when the part reads the frame more than once, so the frame is computed once per pixel. `modulate` always reads it more than once.
examples: coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), modulate(softRayLobes({count: p('rayCount'), softness: p('softness'), spin: -1}), featherMask({radius: p('radius'), feather: p('feather')})), 'burstFrame')
tips: Without the name, a `modulate` of two parts computes the frame twice.
light.withFrame.signature: withFrame(frame: LightValue, part: LightPart, hint?: string): LightValue

light.modulate.name: modulate
light.modulate.summary: Multiply light parts drawn in the same frame, such as a mask over a pattern.
examples: modulate(rayLobes({count: 12, spin: -1, sharpness: 4}), glowPoint({sharpness: 6}), featherMask({radius: p('radius'), feather: 0.4}))

light.rayLobes.name: rayLobes
light.rayLobes.summary: Soft rays fanning out from the center of a radial frame, turning with the layer's clock.
light.rayLobes.description: Returns a 0–1 field with `count` rays. `spin` is a plain number that scales the clock: 1 turns counter-clockwise, -1 clockwise, 0 holds still. `sharpness` above 1 narrows the bright rays, below 1 widens them.
examples: coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), rayLobes({count: p('rays'), spin: -1, sharpness: 4}))
light.rayLobes.signature: rayLobes(slots: {count: ArgSpec; spin: number; sharpness: ArgSpec}): LightPart

light.softRayLobes.name: softRayLobes
light.softRayLobes.summary: `rayLobes` with a softness slider instead of a sharpness.
light.softRayLobes.description: `softness` 0 gives crisp rays and 1 gives wide soft ones. The rays widen without moving. `spin` is a plain number scaling the layer's clock: negative turns clockwise.
examples: coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), softRayLobes({count: p('rayCount'), softness: p('softness'), spin: -1}))
light.softRayLobes.signature: softRayLobes(slots: {count: ArgSpec; softness: ArgSpec; spin: number}): LightPart

light.raySpikes.name: raySpikes
light.raySpikes.summary: Thin star spikes with dark gaps between them, like light through a camera aperture.
light.raySpikes.description: Returns a 0–1 field with twice `halfCount` spikes, so pass half the spike count you want. `power` from 3 to 8 makes them thinner. The spikes do not turn.
examples: coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), modulate(raySpikes({halfCount: 3, power: 5}), glowPoint({sharpness: 12})))

light.ringBand.name: ringBand
light.ringBand.summary: Three thin colored rings around the center, the rainbow edge of a lens or a halo.
light.ringBand.description: Returns an RGB, not a field. The red ring sits at `center` + `spread`, green at `center`, blue at `center` - `spread`, each `width` wide, all in the frame's distance unit. A positive `spread` puts red outside, as a real lens does.
examples: const rings = withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), ringBand({center: p('radius'), spread: 0.01, width: 0.02}))(params)
light.ringBand.signature: ringBand(slots: {center: ArgSpec; spread: ArgSpec; width: ArgSpec}): LightPart

light.glowPoint.name: glowPoint
light.glowPoint.summary: A soft glow at the center of a radial frame with no hard edge.
light.glowPoint.description: Returns a 0–1 field, 1 at the center. `sharpness` is one over the radius squared, so a larger value gives a tighter glow: for a glow that reaches radius `r`, pass `1 / (r * r)`.
examples: coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), glowPoint({sharpness: 8}))
tips: Sharpness is not a radius. Turning it up makes the glow smaller.

light.featherMask.name: featherMask
light.featherMask.summary: A round mask that is solid inside a radius and fades out at its edge.
light.featherMask.description: Returns 1 inside, fading to 0 at `radius` (in the frame's distance unit). `feather` is the fraction of the radius spent fading: 0 is a hard edge, 1 fades all the way from the center. Multiply it with a pattern in `modulate` to give a light an outer edge.
examples: modulate(rayLobes({count: 12, spin: -1, sharpness: 4}), featherMask({radius: p('radius'), feather: p('feather')}))

light.noiseRays.name: noiseRays
light.noiseRays.summary: Volumetric god rays: shafts of light drifting outward from the center, moving on the layer's clock.
light.noiseRays.description: Returns a 0–1 coverage. `density` sets how many shafts, `intensity` (0–1) how visible they are, and `spotty` breaks each shaft into drifting spots along its length. Draw it in `seamlessRadialFrame`, not `radialFrame`.
examples: coverage: withFrame(seamlessRadialFrame(p('center')), noiseRays({density: p('density'), intensity: p('intensity'), spotty: p('spotty')}))
light.noiseRays.signature: noiseRays(slots: {density: ArgSpec; intensity: ArgSpec; spotty: ArgSpec}): LightPart

light.slowDrift.name: slowDrift
light.slowDrift.summary: The slow breathing and drifting signals that keep a light leak alive.
light.slowDrift.description: Call the result with a clock and the params. It returns four numbers: `.x` is a brightness gain to multiply your light by (1 with `flicker` at 0, breathing between 0.25 and 1.75 at 1), and the rest are the slow drifts `beamBloom` and `beamStreaks` read. Pass the whole value to them as `drift`. `seed` re-rolls the pattern.
examples: const drift = local(slowDrift({seed: p('seed'), flicker: p('flicker')})(animatedTime(params), params), 'leakDrift')
light.slowDrift.signature: slowDrift(slots: {seed: ArgSpec; flicker: ArgSpec}): (clock: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.beamBloom.name: beamBloom
light.beamBloom.summary: The soft pool of light at the start of a beam, with a wider faint shoulder around it.
light.beamBloom.description: Call the result with a `beamFrame` value, a `slowDrift` value and the params. It returns `vec2(main, shoulder)`, two 0–1 fields you usually add together. `spread` is the pool's size in the frame's unit (aspect-corrected uv), at least 0.05.
examples:
const bloom = beamBloom({spread: p('spread')})(frame, drift, params)
const heat = add(mul(bloom.member('x'), 1.25), bloom.member('y'))
light.beamBloom.signature: beamBloom(slots: {spread: ArgSpec}): (frame: Expr, drift: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.beamStreaks.name: beamStreaks
light.beamStreaks.summary: Two bright bands crossing a beam further along it, slowly drifting, like light bouncing inside a film camera.
light.beamStreaks.description: Call the result with a `beamFrame` value, a `slowDrift` value and the params. It returns a field scaled by `strength` (0 turns the bands off). `spread` is the same value you gave `beamBloom`, so the bands sit past the pool.
examples: const streaks = beamStreaks({spread: p('spread'), strength: p('streaks')})(frame, drift, params)
light.beamStreaks.signature: beamStreaks(slots: {spread: ArgSpec; strength: ArgSpec}): (frame: Expr, drift: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.dithered.name: dithered
light.dithered.summary: Adds a trace of noise to a heat field so long soft ramps do not show bands.
light.dithered.description: Pass the summed heat, the pixel's uv and a clock. Use it right before `heatRamp`. This is for a heat field, not a color: use `compose.dithered` for a finished color.
examples: return heatRamp({hot: p('colorHot'), mid: p('colorMid'), fringe: p('colorFringe')}).taps(dithered(heat, params.ctx.uv, animatedTime(params)), params)
light.dithered.signature: dithered(heat: Expr, uv: Expr, clock: Expr): Expr

light.glowSpot.name: glowSpot
light.glowSpot.summary: A soft oval glow over an offset you have already scaled, the core of a bloom or a glare.
light.glowSpot.description: Returns a 0–1 field. Divide each axis of the offset by its own radius first: `du` and `dv` at different radii make the glow oval. `sharpness` larger gives a tighter glow.
examples: const pool = glowSpot(div(dx, p('width')), div(dy, p('height')), 2)
light.glowSpot.signature: glowSpot(du: Expr, dv: Expr, sharpness: Expr): Expr

light.starGlint.name: starGlint
light.starGlint.summary: A four-point star of light: a round core with a thin ray along each axis, like a glint off glitter or a star in a photograph.
light.starGlint.description: `offset` is the pixel's position relative to the star's centre, as a `vec2`, in whatever unit you measure the star in (CSS pixels suit small glints). Returns the brightness: 1 at the centre, falling off along the rays and faster everywhere else. `core` is the core's sharpness (larger is a smaller dot). `rayLength` and `rayWidth` are falloff rates along and across each ray (smaller rayLength is a longer ray). `rays` is the rays' brightness relative to the core.
examples: const glint = starGlint(offset, {core: 0.9, rayLength: 0.45, rayWidth: 1.6, rays: 0.25})
tips:
Multiply by a `flashes` blink for a sparkle that comes and goes. Set `reach` to half
the cell size when the glints sit on a `scatterPoints` grid, so long rays never hit a cell edge.

params.name: opts

light.streakBand.name: streakBand
light.streakBand.summary: One soft band across a single coordinate, peaking at `center`.
light.streakBand.description: Returns a 0–1 field, 1 at `center`, fading over `width` on each side. `u`, `center` and `width` share a unit. Multiply or add several for a stack of parallel bands.
examples: const bar = streakBand(params.ctx.uv.member('y'), 0.5, p('width'))
light.streakBand.signature: streakBand(u: Expr, center: Expr, width: Expr): Expr

light.segmentProject.name: segmentProject
light.segmentProject.summary: Where a pixel falls along a line from `a` to `b`, and how far it is from that line.
light.segmentProject.description: Returns `vec2(t, distance)`. `t` runs 0 at `a` to 1 at `b` and is clamped, so the ends are rounded. All three points share a unit. Feed both values to `lightBeam`.
examples: const seg = segmentProject(uv, p('start'), p('end'))
light.segmentProject.signature: segmentProject(p: Expr, a: Expr, b: Expr): Expr

light.lightBeam.name: lightBeam
light.lightBeam.summary: The glow of a beam that can be thicker or softer at one end than the other.
light.lightBeam.description: Give it the distance from the line and the position along it from `segmentProject`. Thickness and softness blend from `start` to `end` along the beam, in the distance unit. Returns `vec2(colorT, alpha)`: `alpha` is 1 inside the beam and fades to 0 outside, and `colorT` runs 0 at the core to 1 at the edge so you can shade the two differently.
examples: const beam = lightBeam(seg.member('y'), seg.member('x'), {start: p('startThickness'), end: p('endThickness')}, {start: p('startSoftness'), end: p('endSoftness')})
light.lightBeam.signature: lightBeam(dist: Expr, t: Expr, thickness: {start: Expr; end: Expr}, softness: {start: Expr; end: Expr}): Expr

light.flareFrame.name: flareFrame
light.flareFrame.summary: The shared frame of a camera lens flare, which every `flare*` part reads.
light.flareFrame.description: `position` is the light's position prop. `intensity` scales the whole flare and `edgeFade` (0–1) dims it as the light nears the canvas edge. Bind it once with a name and hand the same value to each part, then close the stack with `flareComposite`.
examples: const flare = local(flareFrame({position: p('lightPosition'), intensity: p('intensity'), edgeFade: p('edgeFade')})(params), 'flare')
light.flareFrame.signature: flareFrame(slots: {position: PropRef; intensity: ArgSpec; edgeFade: ArgSpec}): LightValue

light.lensGhost.name: lensGhost
light.lensGhost.summary: One ghost disc of a lens flare, the faint circles that line up across from the light.
light.lensGhost.description: Call the result once per ghost with the flare frame, a `disc` and a `tint`, and sum the calls with `additive`. `disc` is `[offset, size, brightness, hollow]`: how far along the axis from the light (scaled by `spread`), radius in aspect-corrected uv, brightness, and 0–1 for a solid disc to a ring. `tint` is `[r, g, b, phase]`, the color and a shimmer offset. `chroma` (0–1) adds a rainbow rim. Returns an RGB.
examples:
const ghost = lensGhost({intensity: p('ghostIntensity'), spread: p('ghostSpread'), chroma: p('ghostChroma')})
const ghosts = additive(ghost(flare, [0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.10], [1.0, 0.95, 0.90, 0.0], params), ghost(flare, [0.30, 0.12, 0.25, 0.65], [1.0, 0.85, 0.55, 2.17], params))
light.lensGhost.signature: lensGhost(slots: {intensity: ArgSpec; spread: ArgSpec; chroma: ArgSpec}): (flare: Expr, disc: [number, number, number, number], tint: [number, number, number, number], params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.flareHalo.name: flareHalo
light.flareHalo.summary: The rainbow halo ring of a lens flare, drawn across the canvas from the light.
light.flareHalo.description: Call the result with the flare frame and the params. The ring centers on the point opposite the light through the canvas center. `radius` is in aspect-corrected uv, `chroma` (0–1) splits it into colors and `softness` widens it. Returns an RGB.
examples: flareHalo({intensity: p('haloIntensity'), radius: p('haloRadius'), chroma: p('haloChroma'), softness: p('haloSoftness')})(flare, params)
light.flareHalo.signature: flareHalo(slots: {intensity: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; chroma: ArgSpec; softness: ArgSpec}): (flare: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

params.name: slots
params.type: {intensity: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; chroma: ArgSpec; softness: ArgSpec}

light.flareStarburst.name: flareStarburst
light.flareStarburst.summary: The star of thin spikes around the light in a lens flare.
light.flareStarburst.description: Call the result with the flare frame and the params. `points` is the number of spikes. They turn slowly with the layer's clock and carry a faint rainbow tint. Returns an RGB.
examples: flareStarburst({intensity: p('starburstIntensity'), points: p('starburstPoints')})(flare, params)
light.flareStarburst.signature: flareStarburst(slots: {intensity: ArgSpec; points: ArgSpec}): (flare: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.flareStreak.name: flareStreak
light.flareStreak.summary: The horizontal widescreen streak through the light in a lens flare.
light.flareStreak.description: Call the result with the flare frame and the params. `length` is the streak's reach in uv. Blue spreads furthest, giving the streak its cyan edges. Returns an RGB.
examples: flareStreak({intensity: p('streakIntensity'), length: p('streakLength')})(flare, params)
light.flareStreak.signature: flareStreak(slots: {intensity: ArgSpec; length: ArgSpec}): (flare: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.flareGlare.name: flareGlare
light.flareGlare.summary: The broad warm-white wash around the light that lifts contrast near it.
light.flareGlare.description: Call the result with the flare frame and the params. `size` is the wash radius in aspect-corrected uv. Returns an RGB.
examples: flareGlare({intensity: p('glareIntensity'), size: p('glareSize')})(flare, params)
light.flareGlare.signature: flareGlare(slots: {intensity: ArgSpec; size: ArgSpec}): (flare: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.flareCore.name: flareCore
light.flareCore.summary: The bright point at the light itself: a hard pinpoint inside a small soft glow.
light.flareCore.description: Call the result with the flare frame and the params. Returns an RGB.
examples: flareCore({intensity: p('intensity')})(flare, params)
light.flareCore.signature: flareCore(slots: {intensity: ArgSpec}): (flare: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

light.flareComposite.name: flareComposite
light.flareComposite.summary: Closes a lens flare: turns the summed flare parts into the color to return from `paint`.
light.flareComposite.description: Pass the `additive` sum of the parts and the flare frame. The frame's intensity, edge fade and shimmer are applied here, and alpha comes from how bright the flare is.
examples: return flareComposite(additive(ghosts, halo, starburst, streak, glare, core), flare)

light.vignetteMask.name: vignetteMask
light.vignetteMask.summary: Darkens the corners of the canvas.
light.vignetteMask.description: Returns a field that is 1 at the center and falls toward 0 in the corners, kept round on any canvas shape. Multiply your color by it. `strength` 0 leaves the image alone and about 2 takes the corners to black. `scale` multiplies `strength`, for mapping a 0–100 slider onto that range.
examples:
const vig = vignetteMask({strength: p('vignette'), scale: 0.025})(params)
return vec4(mul(rgb, vig), 1)

light.additive.name: additive
light.additive.summary: Adds lights together, since light from several sources simply sums.
examples: const total = additive(glare, halo, core)

light.heatRamp.name: heatRamp
light.heatRamp.summary: The colors of overexposed light, from a dim fringe through a mid tone to a hot core.
light.heatRamp.description: Pass three color props. Call `.taps(heat, params)` on the result to turn a heat field into RGB: heat 0 is black, the fringe color shows first, the mid color by 0.5, the hot color above 1, and the light keeps getting brighter up to a heat of 1.6. Each channel reads a slightly different heat, which gives bright edges their color fringing.
examples: return heatRamp({hot: p('colorHot'), mid: p('colorMid'), fringe: p('colorFringe')}).taps(heat, params)
tips: Run the heat through `dithered` first on long soft ramps.
light.heatRamp.signature: heatRamp(colors: {hot: PropRef; mid: PropRef; fringe: PropRef}): { kind: "heatRamp"; taps: (heat: Expr, params: { uniforms: Record<string, Expr>; }) => Expr; }

light.coverageMix.name: coverageMix
light.coverageMix.summary: Blends from a background color to a light color by a coverage field, as a finished paint.
light.coverageMix.description: `color` and `background` are color props, `coverage` a 0–1 light such as a `withFrame` result. Both the color and the alpha blend, so a transparent background gives a light that fades to nothing. Pass a `hint` name when the coverage is expensive. Use `coverageOver` when you want real layer compositing instead of a plain blend.
examples: paint: coverageMix({color: p('color'), background: p('background'), coverage: withFrame(radialFrame(p('center')), glowPoint({sharpness: 6}), 'glow'), hint: 'glowAlpha'})
light.coverageMix.signature: coverageMix(slots: {color: PropRef; background: PropRef; coverage: LightValue; hint?: string}): LightValue

params.name: slots
params.type: {color: PropRef; background: PropRef; coverage: LightValue; hint?: string}

light.coverageOver.name: coverageOver
light.coverageOver.summary: Lays a light color over a background color by a coverage field, like a layer with an opacity mask, as a finished paint.
light.coverageOver.description: `color` and `background` are color props, `coverage` a 0–1 light. The color's own alpha counts as opacity, so a half-transparent ray color shows the background through it.
examples: paint: coverageOver({color: p('rayColor'), background: p('backgroundColor'), coverage: withFrame(seamlessRadialFrame(p('center')), noiseRays({density: p('density'), intensity: p('intensity'), spotty: p('spotty')}))})
light.coverageOver.signature: coverageOver(slots: {color: PropRef; background: PropRef; coverage: LightValue}): LightValue

light.screenGlow.name: screenGlow
light.screenGlow.summary: An `effect` that shines emitted light onto the layer inside it, the way light hits film.
light.screenGlow.description: Pass a function that builds the light's RGB from the params. The light is screened over the child, pushed toward overexposure where it is bright, and shows even over transparent areas. Build the light with `beamFrame`, `beamBloom`, `beamStreaks` and `heatRamp`.
examples: effect: screenGlow((params) => heatRamp({hot: p('colorHot'), mid: p('colorMid'), fringe: p('colorFringe')}).taps(heat, params))

materials.guarded.name: guarded
materials.guarded.summary: Evaluates an expression only where a condition holds, and a cheap fallback everywhere else.
materials.guarded.description: Use it to skip a material's whole body for pixels outside the shape. Any value you build inside `inner` and also read after the guard must be listed in `deps`.
examples: return guarded(insideShape(field.sdf, field.pxH), vec4(rgb, silhouette(field, u.edgeSoftness)), vec4(0, 0, 0, 0), 'plastic')
tips: Values first made inside the guard are not visible after it. Put shared locals in `deps`.
materials.guarded.signature: guarded(cond: Expr, inner: Expr, fallback: Expr, hint: string = 'guarded', deps: Expr[] = []): Expr

materials.insideShape.name: insideShape
materials.insideShape.summary: True inside the shape and up to two pixels outside it.
materials.insideShape.description: Pass the signed distance and pixel size from `surfaceField`. The two-pixel margin keeps the anti-aliased edge inside the shaded region. The usual condition for `guarded`.
examples: guarded(insideShape(field.sdf, field.pxH), shaded, vec4(0, 0, 0, 0))

materials.shapedSurface.name: shapedSurface
materials.shapedSurface.summary: Turns a shape prop into a surface your material shades.
materials.shapedSurface.description: Spread the result into a definition that declares the `center`, `scale`, `rotation` and `shape` props (copy them from any shape effect). Your `surface` function receives a `SurfaceFrame` and returns the color at this pixel. Flat shapes, SVG shapes and 3D shapes all arrive through the same frame.
tips: Start from `surfaceField`, end with `guarded` around `insideShape`. Everything between is the look.

materials.surfaceField.name: surfaceField
materials.surfaceField.summary: The first line of a material: the field taps, the signed distance and the pixel size, bound once.
materials.surfaceField.description: Pass `scale` (the shape's scale prop) to divide the distance by it, as the library's metals and plastics do, so edge softness and pixel tests track the shape's size. Leave it out for `continuedField`.
examples: const field = surfaceField(frame, params, {scale: params.uniforms.scale})
materials.surfaceField.signature: surfaceField(frame: SurfaceFrame, params: GpuFragmentParams, opts: {scale?: Expr} = {}): SurfaceField

materials.geometricNormal.name: geometricNormal
materials.geometricNormal.summary: The surface normal of the shape, whichever kind of shape is active.
materials.geometricNormal.description: A 3D shape takes its normal from the marched depth. A flat shape takes a normal that tilts away from the face near the edge, over `bevelWidth` (in the units of `field.sdf`) with the profile `bevelShape` (0 round, 1 machined). `sharpness` clamps the 3D slope (default 5, lower is calmer). `eps` must match the stencil step (default 0.01). Needs a stencil with neighbour taps.
examples: const n = geometricNormal(frame, field, {bevelWidth: u.bevelWidth, bevelShape: u.bevelShape})
tips: Add relief with `nudgeNormal` or `tiltNormal` after this, never before.
materials.geometricNormal.signature: geometricNormal(frame: SurfaceFrame, field: SurfaceField, opts: {bevelWidth: Expr; bevelShape: Expr; sharpness?: number; eps?: number; hint?: string}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {bevelWidth: Expr; bevelShape: Expr; sharpness?: number; eps?: number; hint?: string}

materials.surfacePattern.name: surfacePattern
materials.surfacePattern.summary: Coordinates for a pattern that sticks to the shape's surface.
materials.surfacePattern.description: On a flat shape they are the placement coordinates centred on the shape (0,0 at its centre). On a 3D shape they follow the surface as it rotates, when the effect declares `pattern: 'raw'` or `'triplanar'`.
examples: const pat = surfacePattern(frame, field)
materials.surfacePattern.signature: surfacePattern(frame: SurfaceFrame, field: SurfaceField, opts: {uv?: Expr} = {}): Expr

materials.fieldSlope.name: fieldSlope
materials.fieldSlope.summary: The direction the shape's distance grows in: a 2D vector pointing outward at this pixel.
materials.fieldSlope.description: Its length is about 1 on a flat shape. `eps` is the tap step (default 0.01) and must match the stencil step.
examples: const grad = fieldSlope(field)

materials.viewRay.name: viewRay
materials.viewRay.summary: The direction the viewer looks along at this pixel, for reflections that sweep across a face.
materials.viewRay.description: A unit 3D vector pointing into the canvas. `fov` sets how much it leans off-axis toward the edges (0.6 is the usual value, 0.55 flatter).
examples: const view = viewRay(params, field)
materials.viewRay.signature: viewRay(params: GpuFragmentParams, field: Pick<SurfaceField, 'aspect'>, fov: number = 0.6): Expr

materials.grazingOf.name: grazingOf
materials.grazingOf.summary: How edge-on the surface is to the viewer: 0 face-on, 1 grazing.
materials.grazingOf.description: The input the fresnel words take when you have a view ray. Without one, use `grazingFlat`.
examples: const grazing = grazingOf(n, viewRay(params, field))

materials.tiltNormal.name: tiltNormal
materials.tiltNormal.summary: Tilts a normal along and across a direction, for brushed or woven relief.
materials.tiltNormal.description: `frame` is a `directionFrame` (from `frames`). `along` and `across` are slope amounts; a few tenths is a visible relief.
examples: const n = tiltNormal(nGeo, brush, {across: reliefAcross, along: reliefAlong})
materials.tiltNormal.signature: tiltNormal(n: Expr, frame: DirectionFrame, slopes: {along?: Expr; across?: Expr}, hint: string = 'n'): Expr

materials.studioSoftboxes.name: studioSoftboxes
materials.studioSoftboxes.summary: The brightness of a five-light studio seen in a reflected direction.
materials.studioSoftboxes.description: Pass the x and y of a reflected view ray. `rotation` is a `direction()` vector that turns the studio. `keyRadius` sizes the main light (0.16 crisp, 0.42 soft), `drift` slides it, `strength` scales the whole bank and `skyGain` the floor-to-sky gradient behind it (0.3–0.4).
examples: const env = studioSoftboxes(R.member('x'), R.member('y'), {rotation: direction(u.envRotation), keyRadius: 0.3, drift: 0, strength: u.environment, skyGain: 0.38})
tips: Smear it with `smearAlong` for a brushed look.

params.name: opts

materials.grainNoise.name: grainNoise
materials.grainNoise.summary: One octave of smooth signed noise along and across a direction, for grain.
materials.grainNoise.description: `coords` come from `directionFrame(...).coordsOf(p)`. `freq` sets the feature density per axis (a high across value gives fine streaks). Returns roughly −1 to 1. Sum octaves and apply gains at the call site.
examples: const sheen = grainNoise(brush.coordsOf(pat), {freq: [1.3, 6.5], drift: driftA})
materials.grainNoise.signature: grainNoise(coords: {along: Expr; across: Expr}, opts: {freq: [Expr | number, Expr | number]; offset?: [number, number]; drift?: Expr}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {freq: [Expr | number, Expr | number]; offset?: [number, number]; drift?: Expr}

materials.smearAlong.name: smearAlong
materials.smearAlong.summary: Blurs any 2D lookup along a direction, for streaked reflections and motion smear.
materials.smearAlong.description: Samples `taps` points (default 9) spread `spread` either side of `center` along the unit vector `axis`, weighted by a bell curve, and sums them. `sample` receives an x and a y.
examples: const env = smearAlong({center: R, axis: brush.tangent, spread: 0.3}, (x, y) => studioSoftboxes(x, y, studio))
materials.smearAlong.signature: smearAlong(opts: {center: Expr; axis: Expr; spread: Expr; taps?: number; sigma?: number; hint?: string}, sample: (x: Expr, y: Expr) => Expr): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {center: Expr; axis: Expr; spread: Expr; taps?: number; sigma?: number; hint?: string}

materials.lightVec3.name: lightVec3
materials.lightVec3.summary: A 3D light direction from a `direction()` vector and an elevation.
materials.lightVec3.description: `z` is negative for a light on the viewer's side of the surface (−0.6 raking to −0.9 frontal). Use it where a word wants a unit light vector. `keyLightAt` also gives the half vector for highlights.
examples: const L = lightVec3(direction(u.lightAngle), -0.7)
materials.lightVec3.signature: lightVec3(dir: Expr, z: number, hint: string = 'L'): Expr

materials.wardAlphas.name: wardAlphas
materials.wardAlphas.summary: Turns roughness and anisotropy sliders (0–1 each) into the two lobe widths `anisoSpecular` takes.
materials.wardAlphas.description: Higher roughness widens the highlight. Higher anisotropy stretches it along the grain and squeezes it across.
examples: alphas: wardAlphas(u.roughness, u.anisotropy)
materials.wardAlphas.signature: wardAlphas(roughness: Expr | number, anisotropy: Expr | number): {along: Expr; across: Expr}

materials.anisoSpecular.name: anisoSpecular
materials.anisoSpecular.summary: A highlight stretched along a grain, as on brushed metal or carbon fibre.
materials.anisoSpecular.description: `tangent` is the 2D grain direction, `light` a unit 3D light vector, `view` the view ray and `alphas` the widths from `wardAlphas`. Pass `gain` or scale the result yourself.
examples: const spec = anisoSpecular({normal: n, tangent: brush.tangent, light: lightVec3(direction(u.lightAngle), -0.7), view, alphas: wardAlphas(rough, aniso), gain: u.specular})

params.name: opts

materials.tiltAlong.name: tiltAlong
materials.tiltAlong.summary: Tilts a normal along one 2D direction by a slope amount.
materials.tiltAlong.description: `axis` is a unit 2D vector such as `direction()` or `fieldSlope`. A few tenths is a visible tilt.
examples: const n = tiltAlong(nGeo, weaveDir, mul(crown, 0.3))
materials.tiltAlong.signature: tiltAlong(n: Expr, axis: Expr, amount: Expr, hint: string = 'n'): Expr

materials.fresnelBoost.name: fresnelBoost
materials.fresnelBoost.summary: A multiplier that brightens grazing edges: 1 face-on, up to `1 + amount` at the rim.
materials.fresnelBoost.description: `grazing` comes from `grazingOf` or `grazingFlat`. `power` (default 3) sets how tightly the lift hugs the rim.
examples: const lit = mul(env, fresnelBoost(grazingOf(n, view), {amount: 0.6}))
materials.fresnelBoost.signature: fresnelBoost(grazing: Expr, opts: {power?: number; amount: Expr | number}): Expr

materials.tintRamp.name: tintRamp
materials.tintRamp.summary: Maps a lighting value (0 dark, 1 light) onto two colors.
materials.tintRamp.description: Takes color props and returns rgb. The final tint of a material lit in grey.
examples: const rgb = tintRamp(lit, u.darkColor, u.lightColor)
materials.tintRamp.signature: tintRamp(t: Expr, dark: Expr, light: Expr): Expr

materials.silhouette.name: silhouette
materials.silhouette.summary: The shape's coverage at this pixel: 1 inside, 0 outside, soft across the edge.
materials.silhouette.description: `edgeSoftness` is the softness prop; at 0 the edge is still anti-aliased over 1.5 pixels. Use it as the alpha of the color you return.
examples: return guarded(insideShape(field.sdf, field.pxH), vec4(rgb, silhouette(field, u.edgeSoftness)), vec4(0, 0, 0, 0))

materials.neutralTone.name: neutralTone
materials.neutralTone.summary: Compresses bright color back into range without shifting its hue.
materials.neutralTone.description: The last step of a metal or glass look that adds reflection on top of a base color. `exposureTone` is the cousin for emitted light.
examples: const rgb = neutralTone(mul(env, u.tint.member('rgb')))

materials.nudgeNormal.name: nudgeNormal
materials.nudgeNormal.summary: Tilts a normal by a slope in x and y, turning a height field into relief.
materials.nudgeNormal.description: Feed it the `dx`/`dy` of `fdSlope` or `perlinSlope`, scaled by how strong you want the relief. Works on a flat `vec3(0, 0, -1)` normal as well as a shape's normal.
examples: const n = nudgeNormal(vec3(0, 0, -1), mul(relief.dx, 0.08), mul(relief.dy, 0.08))
materials.nudgeNormal.signature: nudgeNormal(n: Expr, dx: Expr, dy: Expr, hint: string = 'n'): Expr

materials.marchedNormal.name: marchedNormal
materials.marchedNormal.summary: The surface normal of a 3D shape, from the marched depth.
materials.marchedNormal.description: Only meaningful when `frame.volumetric` is true. `geometricNormal` chooses between this and the flat-shape normal for you. `sharpness` clamps the slope (default 5; 4 is calmer, 6 crisper).
examples: const n = frame.volumetric ? marchedNormal(field, 4) : flatNormal
materials.marchedNormal.signature: marchedNormal(field: SurfaceField, sharpness: number = 5, hint: string = 'nGeo'): Expr

materials.keyLightAt.name: keyLightAt
materials.keyLightAt.summary: A key light from an angle: the light direction `.L` and the half vector `.H` for highlights.
materials.keyLightAt.description: `dir` is a `direction()` vector (from `frames`). `elevation` is how far the light sits toward the viewer: −0.6 raking, −0.9 frontal. Read `.L` with `member('L')` for `lambert` and `.H` for a glint.
examples: const key = keyLightAt(direction(u.lightAngle), -0.7)
tips: Elevation is negative in this engine. A positive value lights the surface from behind.
materials.keyLightAt.signature: keyLightAt(dir: Expr, elevation: number, hint: string = 'kl'): Expr

materials.keyLightXY.name: keyLightXY
materials.keyLightXY.summary: A key light from explicit x and y components, for a second or a crossed light.
examples: const fill = keyLightXY(mul(ly, -1), lx, -0.4, 'fill')
materials.keyLightXY.signature: keyLightXY(x: Expr, y: Expr, elevation: number, hint: string = 'kl'): Expr

materials.grazingFlat.name: grazingFlat
materials.grazingFlat.summary: How edge-on the surface is to a straight-on viewer: 0 face-on, 1 grazing.
materials.grazingFlat.description: Use it when the material has no `viewRay`. The fresnel input for plastics, frost and water.
examples: const grazing = grazingFlat(n)

materials.sharpGlint.name: sharpGlint
materials.sharpGlint.summary: A highlight whose tightness follows a sharpness slider.
materials.sharpGlint.description: `ndh` is the dot of the normal and the key light's `.H`. `sharpness` runs 0–1 and slides the exponent from `cfg.x` to `cfg.y` and the gain from `cfg.z` to `cfg.w`. Pass `cfg` as `vec4(soft exponent, sharp exponent, soft gain, sharp gain)`.
examples: const spec = sharpGlint(dot(n, key.member('H')), u.sharpness, vec4(60, 900, 0.4, 1.4))
materials.sharpGlint.signature: sharpGlint(ndh: Expr, sharpness: Expr, cfg: Expr): Expr

materials.perlinSlope.name: perlinSlope
materials.perlinSlope.summary: The slope of smooth noise at a point, for wavy or molten relief.
materials.perlinSlope.description: Returns a 2D slope scaled by `gain` and clamped to ±4, so relief never spikes into seams. Feed its x and y to `nudgeNormal`.
examples:
const hg = perlinSlope(pat, 0.62)
const n = nudgeNormal(nGeo, mul(hg.member('x'), -0.5), mul(hg.member('y'), -0.5))
materials.perlinSlope.signature: perlinSlope(q: Expr, gain: Expr | number): Expr

materials.opticalThickness.name: opticalThickness
materials.opticalThickness.summary: How much material the view passes through at this pixel: 0 at the edge, up to about 1.2 deep inside.
materials.opticalThickness.description: Multiply by a density prop and feed `beerLambert` for glass, ice and water.
examples: const thickness = mul(opticalThickness(field, frame), u.density)

materials.beerLambert.name: beerLambert
materials.beerLambert.summary: How much light survives a thickness of tinted material, per channel.
materials.beerLambert.description: `absorb` is an rgb absorption; higher absorbs more. Returns rgb transmission 0–1. Multiply the color behind by it.
examples: const transmit = beerLambert(mul(opticalThickness(field, frame), u.density), absorb)

materials.flowWarp.name: flowWarp
materials.flowWarp.summary: A slowly folding 2D offset to add to pattern coordinates, for molten or wind-blown motion.
materials.flowWarp.description: `warpInput` is the pattern coordinate scaled by about 0.6, `flowT` the layer's clock times a speed. Add the result to the coordinate before sampling noise.
examples: const q = add(pat, mul(flowWarp(mul(pat, 0.6), flowT), u.warp))

materials.surfaceNoise.name: surfaceNoise
materials.surfaceNoise.summary: Smooth signed noise at a 2D point, roughly −1 to 1, with features about one unit wide.
materials.surfaceNoise.description: The basis for grain, crumple and frost. Scale the inputs to set the feature size.
examples: const grain = surfaceNoise(mul(pat.member('x'), 140), mul(pat.member('y'), 140))
materials.surfaceNoise.signature: surfaceNoise(x: Expr | number, y: Expr | number): Expr

materials.surfaceNoiseAt.name: surfaceNoiseAt
materials.surfaceNoiseAt.summary: `surfaceNoise` at a 2D point you already hold.
examples: const n = surfaceNoiseAt(mul(pat, 6))

materials.volumeNoiseAt.name: volumeNoiseAt
materials.volumeNoiseAt.summary: Smooth signed noise at a 3D point, roughly −1 to 1.
materials.volumeNoiseAt.description: For anything sampled through a body rather than across its surface: gas, smoke, inclusions, density.
examples: const density = volumeNoiseAt(vec3(pos.member('x'), pos.member('y'), t))

materials.cosineRainbow.name: cosineRainbow
materials.cosineRainbow.summary: A smooth rainbow color from a value that wraps every 1.
materials.cosineRainbow.description: `phases` offset the red, green and blue cycles; `[0, 1/3, 2/3]` is the full spectrum. The color behind holographic foil and thin-film iridescence.
examples: const rgb = cosineRainbow(mul(grazing, 3), [0, 1 / 3, 2 / 3])
materials.cosineRainbow.signature: cosineRainbow(t: Expr, phases: [number, number, number]): Expr

materials.cellNoiseAt.name: cellNoiseAt
materials.cellNoiseAt.summary: Cellular noise at a 2D point: 0 at each cell's seed point, rising toward the cell walls.
materials.cellNoiseAt.description: The value is a squared distance in cell units. Use it for facets and cracks, or as the field `fdSlope` differentiates for faceted relief.
examples: const facet = fdSlope(cellNoiseAt, mul(pat, 6), 0.002)

materials.fdSlope.name: fdSlope
materials.fdSlope.summary: The value and slope of any field at a point: `value`, `dx` and `dy`.
materials.fdSlope.description: `sampleAt` is the field as a function of a 2D point, `eps` the tap distance in that point's units (a few thousandths in uv). The bridge from a height field to a normal: feed `dx` and `dy` to `nudgeNormal`.
examples: const relief = fdSlope((at) => heightField(params, at), uv, 0.0035)
tips: Three taps of the field per pixel. Keep the field cheap or `share` it.
materials.fdSlope.signature: fdSlope(sampleAt: (p: Expr) => Expr, p: Expr, eps: number, hint: string = 'fd'): {value: Expr; dx: Expr; dy: Expr}

materials.fdCurvature.name: fdCurvature
materials.fdCurvature.summary: The value, slope and curvature of any field at a point: `value`, `dx`, `dy` and `curvature`.
materials.fdCurvature.description: `fdSlope` with two more taps. The slopes are centred, so they sit on the point rather than half a step past it, and `curvature` is the field's Laplacian: negative on a crest, positive in a crease, zero on a flat or a plane. Scale it by a gain for a cavity shade that darkens creases and lifts crests. `eps` is the tap distance in the point's units.
examples:
const relief = fdCurvature(cloth, q, 0.004)
const cavity = clamp(sub(1, mul(relief.curvature, 0.005)), 0.6, 1.1)
tips: Five taps of the field per pixel. Keep the field cheap.
materials.fdCurvature.signature: fdCurvature(sampleAt: (p: Expr) => Expr, p: Expr, eps: number, hint: string = 'fd'): {value: Expr; dx: Expr; dy: Expr; curvature: Expr}

materials.hashNoise.name: hashNoise
materials.hashNoise.summary: Random 0–1 per point, with no smoothness between neighbours.
materials.hashNoise.description: For grain, flicker and per-pixel jitter. Feed it large coordinates so every pixel differs.
examples: const grain = hashNoise(mul(uv.member('x'), 991.3), mul(uv.member('y'), 787.7))
materials.hashNoise.signature: hashNoise(x: Expr | number, y: Expr | number): Expr

materials.interleavedNoise.name: interleavedNoise
materials.interleavedNoise.summary: A 0–1 dither pattern over device pixels where neighbours differ as much as possible.
materials.interleavedNoise.description: Better than `hashNoise` for jittering sample positions, which would otherwise clump into visible grain. `pixel` is the pixel coordinate (uv times the viewport size). `clock` shifts the pattern each frame.
examples: const jitter = interleavedNoise(mul(uv, viewport), frame)
materials.interleavedNoise.signature: interleavedNoise(pixel: Expr, clock: Expr | number = 0): Expr

materials.valueNoise.name: valueNoise
materials.valueNoise.summary: Smooth noise 0–1 at a 2D point, softer and blockier than `surfaceNoise`.
examples: const wobble = sub(valueNoise(mul(x, 4), mul(y, 3)), 0.5)
materials.valueNoise.signature: valueNoise(x: Expr | number, y: Expr | number): Expr

materials.rotationSensor.name: rotationSensor
materials.rotationSensor.summary: How far a 3D shape has rotated, as a 2D pan you can move content by.
materials.rotationSensor.description: Zero on flat shapes and on any shape at rest, growing as the shape turns. Constant across the frame, so it pans a star field or a backdrop without shearing it. Needs `pattern: 'raw'`.
examples: const pan = rotationSensor(frame)

materials.shellRefract.name: shellRefract
materials.shellRefract.summary: Coordinates for what sits inside a glass shell, bent where the shell curves.
materials.shellRefract.description: Returns `x` and `y` centred on the shape and displaced by the normal's tilt times `amount`, plus the unbent `centered` pair for anything fixed to the container. The bend is strongest at bevels and silhouettes, where real glass bends its interior.
examples: const interior = shellRefract(frame, n, u.bend)

materials.schlickFresnel.name: schlickFresnel
materials.schlickFresnel.summary: How mirror-like a surface is at this pixel: `r0` face-on, rising to `r0 + gain` at the rim.
materials.schlickFresnel.description: `grazing` comes from `grazingOf` or `grazingFlat`. Glass is `{r0: 0.04, gain: 0.96}`. Lower the gain to keep the rim from turning into a full mirror over an interior.
examples: const fresnel = schlickFresnel(grazingOf(n, view), {gain: 0.6})
materials.schlickFresnel.signature: schlickFresnel(grazing: Expr, opts: {r0?: number; gain: Expr | number; power?: number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {r0?: number; gain: Expr | number; power?: number}

materials.twinkle.name: twinkle
materials.twinkle.summary: A brightness factor that shimmers over time, different for each element.
materials.twinkle.description: Ranges from `1 − 2·amount` to 1. `phase` is a per-element value (a noise or a hash) that keeps the elements out of step; `rate` is how fast, `spread` how differently they flicker.
examples: shimmer: (v) => twinkle(t, v, {amount: 0.3, rate: 1.7, spread: 40})
materials.twinkle.signature: twinkle(t: Expr, phase: Expr, opts: {amount: Expr; rate: number; spread: number}): Expr

materials.pointStars.name: pointStars
materials.pointStars.summary: A plane of sparse glinting points: stars, glitter, dust.
materials.pointStars.description: `p` is the plane coordinate; scale it to set density. Returns the glint intensity, the slow per-point `variation` field, and `rgb` when `tint` is given. Radii are in the cellular noise's squared-distance units, so they are small (0.004–0.02).
examples: const stars = pointStars(mul(pat, 40), {variationFreq: 0.13, radius: [0.004, 0.013], keep: [0.35, 0.75], brightness: [0.3, 1.2], gain: u.stars, tint: {from: [0.72, 0.82, 1], to: [1, 0.92, 0.82], gain: 1.6}})

params.name: opts

materials.placementPoint.name: placementPoint
materials.placementPoint.summary: A position prop in the shape's own coordinates, so you can compare it with the field.
materials.placementPoint.description: Takes a `transformPosition` prop and applies the same center, scale and rotation the shape has. Distances from it are in placement units, not canvas units.
examples: const lightUV = placementPoint(params, params.uniforms.lightPosition)
materials.placementPoint.signature: placementPoint(params: GpuFragmentParams, position: Expr, hint: string = 'placed'): Expr

materials.continuedField.name: continuedField
materials.continuedField.summary: The distance field extended past the edge of an SVG shape's texture.
materials.continuedField.description: An SVG field stops at its 0–1 square, so a far-reaching glow or shadow would see a plateau beyond it. Returns the extended distance here, an `outward` push to add to any slope taken near the border, and `at(uv)` for the distance anywhere. Pass an unscaled `surfaceField`. Flat and 3D shapes pass through unchanged.
examples: const far = continuedField(frame, field, params)
materials.continuedField.signature: continuedField(frame: SurfaceFrame, field: SurfaceField, params: GpuFragmentParams): {sdf: Expr; outward: Expr; at: (uv: Expr) => Expr}

materials.nearestEdge.name: nearestEdge
materials.nearestEdge.summary: The closest point on the shape's edge to this pixel, and the outward normal there.
materials.nearestEdge.description: Where a rim glow or contact shadow comes from for pixels outside the shape. `slope` is `fieldSlope`; its length is guarded.
examples: const edge = nearestEdge(frame.sdfUV!, field.sdf, fieldSlope(field))
materials.nearestEdge.signature: nearestEdge(sdfUV: Expr, sdf: Expr, slope: Expr, hint: string = 'edge'): {point: Expr; normal: Expr}

materials.pointLightFrom.name: pointLightFrom
materials.pointLightFrom.summary: A point light as seen from a point on the shape: the 3D light vector `L`, the 2D direction `toLight` and the `distance`.
materials.pointLightFrom.description: `position` is in placement coordinates (see `placementPoint`). `height` lifts the light toward the viewer, in the same units. Feed `L` to `lambert` and `distance` to `inverseSquare`.
examples: const onBody = pointLightFrom({position: lightUV, height: u.lightHeight}, frame.sdfUV!)
materials.pointLightFrom.signature: pointLightFrom(light: {position: Expr; height: Expr | number}, at: Expr, hint: string = 'pl'): {L: Expr; toLight: Expr; distance: Expr}

materials.lambert.name: lambert
materials.lambert.summary: How much a light falls on a surface: 0 facing away, 1 facing it.
materials.lambert.description: `normal` and `light` are unit vectors, both 2D or both 3D. `wrap` lets light reach around the shape: 0 is a hard terminator, 1 lights it all the way round.
examples: const diffuse = lambert(n, key.member('L'), {wrap: 0.3})
materials.lambert.signature: lambert(normal: Expr, light: Expr, opts: {wrap?: Expr | number} = {}): Expr

materials.inverseSquare.name: inverseSquare
materials.inverseSquare.summary: How a point light fades with distance: 1 at the source, half at `range`.
examples: const lit = mul(lambert(n, onBody.L), inverseSquare(onBody.distance, u.lightRange))
materials.inverseSquare.signature: inverseSquare(distance: Expr, range: Expr | number): Expr

materials.exposureTone.name: exposureTone
materials.exposureTone.summary: Turns light that piles past 1 into a soft burn toward white, like film.
materials.exposureTone.description: Apply it to summed emitted light before output. `neutralTone` is the cousin for a lit, tinted surface.
examples: const glow = exposureTone(add(irradiance, emitter))

materials.sensorGrain.name: sensorGrain
materials.sensorGrain.summary: Adds a fine per-pixel brightness jitter, so rendered light reads as photographed.
materials.sensorGrain.description: Each pixel is scaled by up to half of `amount` either way. `pixel` is the pixel coordinate (uv times the viewport size); `clock` re-rolls the grain each frame.
examples: const rgb = sensorGrain(glow, {amount: 0.08, pixel: mul(uv, viewport), clock: t})
materials.sensorGrain.signature: sensorGrain(rgb: Expr, opts: {amount: Expr | number; pixel: Expr; clock: Expr | number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {amount: Expr | number; pixel: Expr; clock: Expr | number}

materials.dualLobeGlint.name: dualLobeGlint
materials.dualLobeGlint.summary: A highlight with a tight hot core and a wide dim halo.
materials.dualLobeGlint.description: `ndh` is the dot of the normal and the key light's `.H`. `core` and `halo` are `[exponent, gain]` pairs. `softness` (0–1, 0.5 neutral) widens or tightens both lobes.
examples: const spec = dualLobeGlint(dot(n, key.member('H')), {core: [140, 1.3], halo: [22, 0.14], softness: u.highlightSoftness, gain: u.highlight})

params.name: opts

materials.sheenLobe.name: sheenLobe
materials.sheenLobe.summary: The soft glow of light scattered off fibres where a surface turns edge-on to the viewer: the velvet sheen on the flanks of satin, velour and wool.
materials.sheenLobe.description: `normal` and `light` are unit 3D vectors and `view` the view ray (`viewRay`, or a constant `vec3(0, 0, 1)`). It is zero on a face-on surface and rises along each fold's flank, so it never washes a flat sheet. `roughness` (0–1) widens it: low is a thin bright rim, high a broad soft bloom. The lobe peaks at 1 and is held back by a wrapped lambert so unlit flanks stay dark; pass `gain` or scale the result yourself. Pair it with `anisoSpecular` for a satin finish: the streak is the shine, the sheen is the body.
examples: const velvet = sheenLobe({normal: n, light: L, view, roughness: 0.5, gain: u.sheen})
materials.sheenLobe.signature:
sheenLobe(opts: {
    normal: Expr
    light: Expr
    view: Expr
    roughness: Expr | number
    gain?: Expr | number
}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    normal: Expr
    light: Expr
    view: Expr
    roughness: Expr | number
    gain?: Expr | number
}

volume.interiorRay.name: interiorRay
volume.interiorRay.summary: The line of sight through a shape: where it enters, how far it travels inside, and where it is at any depth.
volume.interiorRay.description: Pass the material's `field` and `frame`, the point the ray enters at (`origin`, usually the shape's centred placement coordinates) and optionally the `view` ray. `shear` (default 1) sets how far deeper samples slide sideways along the view, which is what makes an interior read as deep rather than flat. `lengthScale` stretches or shortens the travel. On a 3D shape `length` is the real chord through it. On a flat shape it stands in for depth, growing toward the middle of the shape.
examples: const ray = interiorRay(field, frame, {origin: interior, view, shear: 0.55})
tips: Refract `origin` through the shell first (`shellRefract`) and the interior bends at the glass walls.
volume.interiorRay.signature: interiorRay(field: SurfaceField, frame: SurfaceFrame, opts: {origin: {x: Expr; y: Expr}; view?: Expr; shear?: number; lengthScale?: number}): InteriorRay

params.name: opts
params.type: {origin: {x: Expr; y: Expr}; view?: Expr; shear?: number; lengthScale?: number}

volume.parallaxPlane.name: parallaxPlane
volume.parallaxPlane.summary: A flat layer at a fixed depth inside the shape, like scenery seen through a window.
volume.parallaxPlane.description: `depth` is a fraction of the ray's length: 0 at the entry, 1 at the far side, beyond 1 for a backdrop behind the shape. Give it a `pan` (the `rotationSensor` of the frame) and the layer slides as the shape rotates, `panRate` times as far. Deeper layers with higher rates give the parallax of real depth. Returns the position to sample content at, plus its depth `z`.
examples: const far = parallaxPlane(ray, {depth: 1.1, pan: rotationSensor(frame), panRate: 1.3, hint: 'far'})
tips: Two planes at different depths and rates are enough to sell a starfield.
volume.parallaxPlane.signature: parallaxPlane(ray: InteriorRay, opts: {depth: number; pan?: {x: Expr; y: Expr}; panRate?: number; hint?: string}): {x: Expr; y: Expr; z: Expr}

params.name: opts
params.type: {depth: number; pan?: {x: Expr; y: Expr}; panRate?: number; hint?: string}

volume.turbulentMedium.name: turbulentMedium
volume.turbulentMedium.summary: A billowing cloud density at a point inside the shape.
volume.turbulentMedium.description: `frequency` sets how many cloud cells fit across the shape. `drift` is a time value that moves the clouds. `seed` moves to a different part of the cloud so two instances differ. `billow` (0–1) folds the clouds over themselves for a cumulus look. `density` is signed, roughly −1 to 1: threshold it with `smoothstep` to make clouds with clear gaps. `mid` and `fine` are two finer layers of the same cloud, free to use for dust bands or wisps.
examples: const gas = turbulentMedium({x: pos.x, y: pos.y, z}, {frequency: math.mul(u.gasScale, 3), drift: t, billow: math.float(0.4)})
tips: Inside a `volumeMarch`, pass the step number as `hint` so each step gets its own values.
volume.turbulentMedium.signature: turbulentMedium(p: {x: Expr; y: Expr; z: Expr}, opts: {frequency: Expr; drift?: Expr; seed?: Expr; billow?: Expr; hint?: string}): {density: Expr; mid: Expr; fine: Expr}

params.name: opts
params.type: {frequency: Expr; drift?: Expr; seed?: Expr; billow?: Expr; hint?: string}

volume.volumeMarch.name: volumeMarch
volume.volumeMarch.summary: Walk a ray through the medium front to back, adding up what glows and what dims.
volume.volumeMarch.description: `steps` is how many samples to take (4–8 is typical; it is fixed when the shader compiles). `entry` and `length` come from `interiorRay`. For each step your callback returns `emit`, the rgb light this sample gives off, and `absorb`, the rgb amount it blocks. Absorption is per channel, so a medium can dim blue more than red. Returns the accumulated `color` and the `transmittance` left at the far side: multiply anything behind the medium by it. `jitter` is a small per-pixel offset along the ray, as a fraction of its length (a hash times `1 / steps` works), that trades banding for fine grain. `emissionGain` scales every sample's glow; use `k / steps` so brightness does not change with the step count.
examples: const march = volumeMarch({steps: 6, entry: ray.entry, length: ray.length, jitter}, ({z, i}) => ({emit: math.mul(rgb, dens), absorb: math.splat3(math.mul(dens, u.density))}))
tips: Fewer steps plus `jitter` beats more steps: the noise becomes grain instead of bands.

params.name: opts

radiance.gatherIrradiance.name: gatherIrradiance
radiance.gatherIrradiance.summary: The light arriving at a pixel from a glowing shape edge, with the shape's body blocking it.
radiance.gatherIrradiance.description: Looks out from the pixel in `cones` directions, finds where each touches the shape, and averages the `emission` there. Edges facing away or hidden behind the body contribute nothing. Returns one number: the brightness at this pixel. It runs per pixel per frame, so prefer `irradianceField` unless the light must be live.
examples: const light = gatherIrradiance({origin: frame.sdfUV!, field: far.at, cones: 16, steps: 24, reach: 3, start: far.sdf, surfaceEps: px, jitter: hash, emission: ({normal}) => math.max(math.dot(normal, lightDir), 0), deps: [lightDir]})
tips: Any value computed outside `emission` and read inside it must be listed in `deps`.

radiance.shadowVisibility.name: shadowVisibility
radiance.shadowVisibility.summary: How much of a light reaches a point, 1 when nothing is in the way and 0 when the shape blocks it.
radiance.shadowVisibility.description: Casts a ray from `from` toward the light and stops at the shape. Values between 0 and 1 are the soft edge of the shadow, wider with `softness`. Multiply a light's contribution by it.
examples: const lit = math.mul(strength, shadowVisibility({from: math.add(edge.point, math.mul(edge.normal, math.mul(px, 2))), toward: light.uv, field: far.at, steps: 12, surfaceEps: px, softness: u.shadowSoftness}))
tips: Start `from` two pixels off the edge along its normal or the point shadows itself.

radiance.irradianceField.name: irradianceField
radiance.irradianceField.summary: The light spilling from a shape's edges, gathered once into a texture and read per pixel.
radiance.irradianceField.description: Returns two halves. Put `compute` on your definition's `compute:` field. In your material, call `sample(params)` for the rgb light at the pixel. It returns `undefined` when there is no GPU to gather on, so write `sample(params) ?? splat3(0)`. It reads your standard shape props (`center`, `scale`, `rotation`, `shape`, `shapeSdfUrl`, `shapeType`) plus the props named in the spec. The texture only re-gathers when a light or the shape changes.
examples: const spill = irradianceField(GATHER).sample(params) ?? math.splat3(0)
tips: Build the spec once as a constant and use it for both `compute:` and `sample`.

voxels.voxelSurface.name: voxelSurface
voxels.voxelSurface.summary: Rebuild the shape from blocks and shade each block with your `surface`.
voxels.voxelSurface.description: Returns `{extraFields, compute, gpu}` to spread into a shape-effect definition. Your props must include the standard shape props (`center`, `scale`, `rotation`, `shape`, `shapeSdfUrl`, `shapeType`), a `shadows` amount (0–1) and everything the spec names. Your `surface` gets a `VoxelFrame` per block and returns `vec4(rgb, vox.coverage)`. Geometry props re-build the model when they change. Color and light props never do.
examples: ...voxelSurface({style: p('voxelShape'), gridSpace: p('gridSpace'), voxelSize: p('voxelSize'), fill: p('fill'), voxelScale: p('voxelScale'), bevel: p('bevel'), shadowSoftness: p('shadowSoftness'), lightAngle: p('lightAngle'), lightElevation: p('lightElevation'), depth: p('depth'), surface: (vox, frame, params) => math.vec4(shade(vox), vox.coverage)})
tips: Light with `materials.lambert(vox.normal, L, {wrap: 0.12})` times `1 − vox.shadow · shadows` and the blocks read as solid.

shape.circle.name: circle
shape.circle.summary: A circle of a given radius.
shape.circle.description: `radius` is in uv (1 = the canvas height). Returns the signed distance to the edge, negative inside.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => circle(x, y, u('radius')), bounds: {size: {width: 'radius', height: 'radius'}}, …}
tips: Blend a sharp shape toward this one with `math.mix` to round it off (the Polygon shader does).
shape.circle.signature: circle(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val): Expr

shape.ellipse.name: ellipse
shape.ellipse.summary: An ellipse with separate horizontal and vertical radii.
shape.ellipse.description: `radiusX` and `radiusY` are the half-widths along each axis, in uv.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => ellipse(x, y, u('radiusX'), u('radiusY')), …}
shape.ellipse.signature: ellipse(x: Val, y: Val, radiusX: Val, radiusY: Val): Expr

shape.roundedRect.name: roundedRect
shape.roundedRect.description: `width` and `height` are half-extents (the distance from the centre to each side), in uv. `rounding` is the corner radius. Pass 0 for a sharp rectangle.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => roundedRect(x, y, u('width'), u('height'), u('rounding')), …}
tips: A `width` of 0.5 spans the full canvas height, not half of it.
shape.roundedRect.signature: roundedRect(x: Val, y: Val, width: Val, height: Val, rounding: Val): Expr

shape.polygon.name: polygon
shape.polygon.summary: A regular polygon with any number of sides.
shape.polygon.description: `radius` is the distance from the centre to the middle of each side (not to the corners), in uv. `sides` is the side count, 3 for a triangle and up. A flat side faces right at rotation 0.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => polygon(x, y, u('radius'), u('sides')), …}
tips: `math.mix(polygon(…), circle(…), u('rounding'))` morphs the corners away.
shape.polygon.signature: polygon(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val, sides: Val): Expr

shape.star.name: star
shape.star.summary: A star with straight sides and sharp points.
shape.star.description: `outerRadius` is the distance from the centre to the tips, in uv. `sides` is the number of points. `innerRatio` (0–1) is the inner corner radius as a fraction of the tip radius. 0.382 gives the classic five-point star. One tip points right at rotation 0.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => star(x, y, u('radius'), u('sides'), u('innerRatio')), …}
shape.star.signature: star(x: Val, y: Val, outerRadius: Val, sides: Val, innerRatio: Val): Expr

shape.flower.name: flower
shape.flower.summary: A flower with pointed petals and V-shaped valleys between them.
shape.flower.description: `outerRadius` is the distance from the centre to a petal tip, in uv. `sides` is the petal count. `innerRatio` (0–1) is the valley radius as a fraction of the tip radius.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => flower(x, y, u('radius'), u('sides'), u('innerRatio')), …}
shape.flower.signature: flower(x: Val, y: Val, outerRadius: Val, sides: Val, innerRatio: Val): Expr

shape.heart.name: heart
shape.heart.summary: A heart, point down at rotation 0.
shape.heart.description: `radius` is the size it is fitted into, in uv.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => heart(x, y, u('radius')), bounds: {size: {width: 'radius', height: 'radius'}}, …}
shape.heart.signature: heart(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val): Expr

shape.cross.name: cross
shape.cross.summary: A plus-shaped cross with four equal arms.
shape.cross.description: `size` is the arm half-length (centre to an arm's end), `thickness` the arm half-width, both in uv. `rounding` rounds the corners. Rotate it 45° for an X.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => cross(x, y, u('radius'), u('thickness'), u('rounding')), …}
shape.cross.signature: cross(x: Val, y: Val, size: Val, thickness: Val, rounding: Val): Expr

shape.ring.name: ring
shape.ring.summary: A ring: a circular band around a centre.
shape.ring.description: `radius` is the distance to the middle of the band, `thickness` half the band's width, both in uv. The full band is twice `thickness` wide.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => ring(x, y, u('radius'), u('thickness')), rotatable: false, …}
tips: Rotationally symmetric, so declare `rotatable: false` and the rotation prop is left out.
shape.ring.signature: ring(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val, thickness: Val): Expr

shape.vesica.name: vesica
shape.vesica.summary: A vesica: the lens where two equal circles overlap.
shape.vesica.description: `radius` is each circle's radius, in uv. `spread` (0–1) is how far apart the circles sit as a fraction of the radius. 0 is a full circle, 1 an infinitely thin lens.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => vesica(x, y, u('radius'), u('spread')), …}
shape.vesica.signature: vesica(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val, spread: Val): Expr

shape.crescent.name: crescent
shape.crescent.summary: A crescent: a disc with a smaller disc bitten out of it.
shape.crescent.description: `outerRadius` is the full disc's radius, in uv. `innerRatio` (0–1) is the bite's radius as a fraction of it. `offset` is how far the bite's centre is shifted sideways, in uv.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => crescent(x, y, u('radius'), u('innerRatio'), u('offset')), …}
shape.crescent.signature: crescent(x: Val, y: Val, outerRadius: Val, innerRatio: Val, offset: Val): Expr

shape.trapezoid.name: trapezoid
shape.trapezoid.summary: A trapezoid: a four-sided shape with a flat top and bottom of different widths.
shape.trapezoid.description: `topWidth` and `bottomWidth` are half-widths of the top and bottom edges as seen on screen, `height` the half-height, all in uv. Equal widths give a rectangle.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => trapezoid(x, y, u('topWidth'), u('bottomWidth'), u('height')), …}
shape.trapezoid.signature: trapezoid(x: Val, y: Val, topWidth: Val, bottomWidth: Val, height: Val): Expr

shape.teardrop.name: teardrop
shape.teardrop.summary: A teardrop: a round bulb tapering to a sharp point, point up at rotation 0.
shape.teardrop.description: `radius` is the bulb's radius and `height` the distance from the bulb's centre to the point, both in uv.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => teardrop(x, y, u('radius'), u('height')), …}
shape.teardrop.signature: teardrop(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val, height: Val): Expr

shape.parallelogram.name: parallelogram
shape.parallelogram.summary: A parallelogram: a rectangle with its top edge slid sideways.
shape.parallelogram.description: `width` and `height` are half-extents, in uv. `skew` is how far the top edge is shifted horizontally, in uv. 0 gives a rectangle.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => parallelogram(x, y, u('width'), u('height'), u('skew')), …}
shape.parallelogram.signature: parallelogram(x: Val, y: Val, width: Val, height: Val, skew: Val): Expr

shape.arc.name: arc
shape.arc.summary: A pie wedge: a filled sector of a circle.
shape.arc.description: `radius` is the sector's radius, in uv. `halfAngle` is half the opening angle, in radians. Multiply an aperture prop in degrees by `APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE` to get it. The wedge opens downward at rotation 0.
examples: shape: {distance: ({x, y}, u) => arc(x, y, u('radius'), math.mul(u('aperture'), APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE)), …}
shape.arc.signature: arc(x: Val, y: Val, radius: Val, halfAngle: Val): Expr

shape.APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE.name: APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE
shape.APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE.summary: The factor that turns an opening angle in degrees into the half-angle `arc` takes.
shape.APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE.description: Multiply a 0–360 aperture prop by it. It equals π/360.
examples: distance: ({x, y}, u) => arc(x, y, u('radius'), math.mul(u('aperture'), APERTURE_TO_HALF_ANGLE))

frames.surfaceOf.name: surfaceOf
frames.surfaceOf.summary: The canvas a generator paints on: its `uv`, its `viewport` size in pixels and its `aspect`.
frames.surfaceOf.description: `uv` runs 0–1 across the layer, y down. `aspect` is width over height. When a parent fits the layer into a box, `viewport` and `aspect` describe that box. Every frame takes this as its second argument.
examples: paint: (params) => { const {uv, viewport, aspect} = surfaceOf(params); … }
frames.surfaceOf.signature: surfaceOf(params: GpuFragmentParams): {uv: Expr; viewport: Expr; aspect: Expr}

frames.rawSurfaceOf.name: rawSurfaceOf
frames.rawSurfaceOf.summary: The canvas like `surfaceOf`, but always measured against the whole canvas, never a fitted box.
frames.rawSurfaceOf.description: Use it when a pattern should stay anchored to the canvas as the layer is resized.
examples: const {delta, dist} = centredFrame({center: p('center')})(params, rawSurfaceOf(params))
frames.rawSurfaceOf.signature: rawSurfaceOf(params: GpuFragmentParams): {uv: Expr; viewport: Expr; aspect: Expr}

frames.centredFrame.name: centredFrame
frames.centredFrame.summary: A frame centred on a position prop: each pixel's offset from the centre and its distance.
frames.centredFrame.description: Pass `{center: p('center')}` where `center` is a position prop. Call the result with `params` and a surface. Distances are aspect-corrected, so 1 is the canvas height and a circle stays round on a wide canvas.
examples: const {dist} = centredFrame({center: p('center')})(params, surfaceOf(params))
tips: `dist` is in canvas-height units: a radius of 0.5 reaches the top and bottom edges from the middle.
frames.centredFrame.signature: centredFrame(slots: {center: PropRef}): (params: GpuFragmentParams, surface: { uv: Expr; aspect: Expr; }) => CentredFrame

frames.segmentFrame.name: segmentFrame
frames.segmentFrame.summary: A frame along the line between two position props: how far each pixel is along it and across it.
frames.segmentFrame.description: Pass `{from: p('from'), to: p('to')}` and call the result with `params` and a surface. `along` is 0 at `from` and equals `length` at `to`. `across` is the signed distance from the line. All three are aspect-corrected, in canvas-height units.
examples: const {along, across, length} = segmentFrame({from: p('from'), to: p('to')})(params, surfaceOf(params))
tips: Divide `along` by `length` for a 0–1 position along the line, the natural gradient parameter.
frames.segmentFrame.signature: segmentFrame(slots: {from: PropRef; to: PropRef}): (params: GpuFragmentParams, surface: { uv: Expr; aspect: Expr; }) => SegmentFrame

frames.direction.name: direction
frames.direction.summary: A direction in degrees as a unit vector.
frames.direction.description: 0° points right and angles turn clockwise on screen, so 90° points down. Use it wherever a word wants a light or flow direction as a vector.
examples: const light = direction(params.uniforms.lightAngle, 'light')
frames.direction.signature: direction(angleDeg: Expr | number, hint: string = 'dir'): Expr

frames.directionFrame.name: directionFrame
frames.directionFrame.summary: The two axes of a direction given in degrees, for patterns that run along it.
frames.directionFrame.description: `tangent` points along the direction, `perp` at right angles to it. `coordsOf(point)` returns that point's `along` and `across` distances in the frame. Brush grain, weave, streaks and flow all live in one of these.
examples: const grain = directionFrame(params.uniforms.brushAngle, 'brush'); const {along, across} = grain.coordsOf(delta)
frames.directionFrame.signature: directionFrame(angleDeg: Expr | number, hint: string = 'grain'): DirectionFrame

frames.sectorFold.name: sectorFold
frames.sectorFold.summary: Fold a point into one mirrored wedge around a centre: the kaleidoscope fold.
frames.sectorFold.description: `sectorAngle` is the wedge's angle in radians (2π divided by the number of facets). `center` is where the wedges meet, 0.5 by default. Returns the folded point as an offset from the centre. Sample anything at that point and it repeats and mirrors around the centre.
examples: const folded = sectorFold(uv.member('x'), uv.member('y'), math.div(2 * Math.PI, params.uniforms.facets))
frames.sectorFold.signature: sectorFold(x: Expr, y: Expr, sectorAngle: Expr, center: number = 0.5): Expr

warps.mirrorLine.name: mirrorLine
warps.mirrorLine.summary: Mirror the child across a line through `center` at `angle`.
warps.mirrorLine.description: `center` is in uv, `angle` in degrees. One side of the line stays as it is and the other side shows its reflection.
examples: map: warps.mirrorLine({center: p('center'), angle: p('angle')})
tips: Pair it with an `edges` prop that defaults to `'mirror'` so the reflected half never runs out of picture.

warps.flip.name: flip
warps.flip.summary: Flip the child horizontally, vertically, or both.
warps.flip.description: `flipX` and `flipY` are boolean props declared with `transform: transformBoolean`. The flip never looks outside the child, so set `edges: 'none'` on the definition.
examples:
map: warps.flip({flipX: p('flipX'), flipY: p('flipY')}),
edges: 'none',

warps.bend.name: bend
warps.bend.summary: Curve the child like a bent sheet seen in perspective, so its ends swell or shrink.
warps.bend.description: `strength` runs −1 to 1 and its sign picks the bend direction. `angle` is the bend axis in degrees. `falloff` (0–1) keeps more of the middle flat and pushes the bend toward the ends. Where the sheet leaves the frame there is nothing to show, so pair it with an `edges` prop that defaults to `'transparent'`.
examples: map: warps.bend({strength: p('strength'), falloff: p('falloff'), angle: p('angle')})
warps.bend.signature: bend(slots: {strength: ArgSpec; falloff: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

warps.bulge.name: bulge
warps.bulge.summary: Magnify or pinch the child inside a disc around `center`.
warps.bulge.description: `strength` runs −1 to 1: positive bulges out, negative pinches in. `radius` sets the size of the disc (1 reaches about half the canvas height). `falloff` runs 0 (hard edge) to 1 (soft).
examples: map: warps.bulge({center: p('center'), strength: p('strength'), radius: p('radius'), falloff: p('falloff')})
warps.bulge.signature: bulge(slots: {center: ArgSpec; strength: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; falloff: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type: {center: ArgSpec; strength: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; falloff: ArgSpec}

warps.twirl.name: twirl
warps.twirl.summary: Twist the child around `center`, turning more the farther a pixel is from it.
warps.twirl.description: `intensity` is the twist in radians per unit of distance, so the canvas edge turns by about `intensity` radians. Negative values twist the other way. The library uses −5 to 5.
examples: map: warps.twirl({center: p('center'), intensity: p('intensity')})

warps.kaleidoscope.name: kaleidoscope
warps.kaleidoscope.summary: Fold the child into mirrored pie slices around `center`.
warps.kaleidoscope.description: `segments` is the number of slices (2 or more). `angle` rotates the whole pattern, in degrees. Pair it with an `edges` prop that defaults to `'mirror'`.
examples: map: warps.kaleidoscope({center: p('center'), segments: p('segments'), angle: p('angle')})
warps.kaleidoscope.signature: kaleidoscope(slots: {center: ArgSpec; segments: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

warps.stretch.name: stretch
warps.stretch.summary: Stretch the child along one direction, starting at `center`.
warps.stretch.description: `angle` is the direction in degrees. Content on the side `angle` points to is pulled out; the other side is left alone. `strength` (0–1) sets how far. `falloff` (0–1) softens the start of the stretch, from a hard line at 0 to a long ramp at 1.
examples: map: warps.stretch({center: p('center'), strength: p('strength'), angle: p('angle'), falloff: p('falloff')})
warps.stretch.signature: stretch(slots: {center: ArgSpec; strength: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec; falloff: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type: {center: ArgSpec; strength: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec; falloff: ArgSpec}

warps.wave.name: wave
warps.wave.summary: Ripple the child with a travelling wave.
warps.wave.description: `angle` is the travel direction in degrees, `frequency` the number of waves across the canvas, `strength` (0–1) how far pixels move. `waveType` is a prop marked `compileTime: true` holding `'sine'`, `'triangle'`, `'square'`, `'sawtooth'` or `'bounce'`. The wave moves with the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`.
examples: map: warps.wave({strength: p('strength'), frequency: p('frequency'), angle: p('angle'), waveType: p('waveType')})
tips: Changing `waveType` recompiles the shader; the other inputs update live.
warps.wave.signature: wave(slots: {strength: ArgSpec; frequency: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec; waveType: PropRef}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type: {strength: ArgSpec; frequency: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec; waveType: PropRef}

warps.toPolar.name: toPolar
warps.toPolar.summary: Unroll the child around `center`, so angle becomes x and distance becomes y.
warps.toPolar.description: `wrap` scales how many times the child repeats around (1 is once). `radius` scales the distance axis. `intensity` runs 0 (no change) to 1 (the full polar unwrap), and the values between are a real partial warp, not a cross-fade.
examples: map: warps.toPolar({center: p('center'), wrap: p('wrap'), radius: p('radius'), intensity: p('intensity')})
warps.toPolar.signature: toPolar(slots: {center: ArgSpec; wrap: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; intensity: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type: {center: ArgSpec; wrap: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; intensity: ArgSpec}

warps.fromPolar.name: fromPolar
warps.fromPolar.summary: Wrap the child into a circle around `center`, reading its x as angle and its y as distance.
warps.fromPolar.description: The reverse of `toPolar`. `scale` sets how large the circle is. `intensity` runs 0 (no change) to 1 (the full wrap).
examples: map: warps.fromPolar({center: p('center'), scale: p('scale'), intensity: p('intensity')})
warps.fromPolar.signature: fromPolar(slots: {center: ArgSpec; scale: ArgSpec; intensity: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

warps.cornerPin.name: cornerPin
warps.cornerPin.summary: Pin the four corners of the child to new positions, with true perspective between them.
warps.cornerPin.description: The corners are positions in uv. `amount` (0–1) blends each corner from its normal place (0) to the pinned position (1). Pixels outside the pinned quad are clipped to transparent whatever the edge mode.
examples: map: warps.cornerPin({topLeft: p('topLeft'), topRight: p('topRight'), bottomRight: p('bottomRight'), bottomLeft: p('bottomLeft'), amount: p('amount')})
warps.cornerPin.signature:
cornerPin(slots: {
    topLeft: ArgSpec
    topRight: ArgSpec
    bottomRight: ArgSpec
    bottomLeft: ArgSpec
    amount: ArgSpec
}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    topLeft: ArgSpec
    topRight: ArgSpec
    bottomRight: ArgSpec
    bottomLeft: ArgSpec
    amount: ArgSpec
}

warps.perspective.name: perspective
warps.perspective.summary: Tilt the child in 3D, as if it were a card turned away from the camera.
warps.perspective.description: `pan` and `tilt` are the turns in degrees (−90 to 90). `fov` is the camera's field of view in degrees: wider means stronger perspective. `zoom` scales the picture (1 is unchanged). `center` is the pivot and `offset` shifts the result, both in uv.
examples: map: warps.perspective({center: p('center'), pan: p('pan'), tilt: p('tilt'), fov: p('fov'), zoom: p('zoom'), offset: p('offset')})
warps.perspective.signature:
perspective(slots: {
    center: ArgSpec
    pan: ArgSpec
    tilt: ArgSpec
    fov: ArgSpec
    zoom: ArgSpec
    offset: ArgSpec
}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    center: ArgSpec
    pan: ArgSpec
    tilt: ArgSpec
    fov: ArgSpec
    zoom: ArgSpec
    offset: ArgSpec
}

warps.concentricRings.name: concentricRings
warps.concentricRings.summary: Cut the child into rings around `center` and spin each ring by its own amount.
