warps.concentricRings.description: `rings` is how many rings fit in one unit of distance. `intensity` is the largest still rotation a ring can have, in degrees. `smoothness` (0–1) blends neighbouring rings instead of cutting between them. `seed` reshuffles the per-ring amounts and `speedRandomness` (0–1) lets rings spin at different rates. Declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`.
examples: map: warps.concentricRings({center: p('center'), intensity: p('intensity'), rings: p('rings'), smoothness: p('smoothness'), seed: p('seed'), speedRandomness: p('speedRandomness')})
warps.concentricRings.signature:
concentricRings(slots: {
    center: ArgSpec
    intensity: ArgSpec
    rings: ArgSpec
    smoothness: ArgSpec
    seed: ArgSpec
    speedRandomness: ArgSpec
}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    center: ArgSpec
    intensity: ArgSpec
    rings: ArgSpec
    smoothness: ArgSpec
    seed: ArgSpec
    speedRandomness: ArgSpec
}

warps.flowNoise.name: flowNoise
warps.flowNoise.summary: Push the child around with a slowly flowing liquid motion.
warps.flowNoise.description: `strength` is how far pixels move, in uv (the library uses 0–0.5). `detail` scales the flow pattern (higher is finer). `seed` is a prop that picks a different pattern, even when still. Two clocks drive it: declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` for the drift and `extraAnimatedTimes: {evolution: 'evolutionSpeed'}` for the pattern slowly reshaping.
examples: map: warps.flowNoise({strength: p('strength'), detail: p('detail'), seed: p('seed')})
tips: Speed 0 on both clocks gives a fixed distortion you can still change with `seed`.
warps.flowNoise.signature: flowNoise(slots: {strength: ArgSpec; detail: ArgSpec; seed: PropRef}): UvMapSource

warps.slicedSlide.name: slicedSlide
warps.slicedSlide.summary: Slice the child into strips that slide out of frame in alternating directions.
warps.slicedSlide.description: A wipe transition. `progress` runs 0 (whole) to 1 (gone). `angle` is the cut direction in degrees and `count` the number of strips. Set `edges: 1` (transparent) on the definition so the vacated space clears instead of smearing.
examples:
map: warps.slicedSlide({angle: p('angle'), count: p('sliceCount'), progress: p('progress')}),
edges: 1,
warps.slicedSlide.signature: slicedSlide(slots: {angle: ArgSpec; count: ArgSpec; progress: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

warps.barOffset.name: barOffset
warps.barOffset.summary: Cut the child into parallel bars and shift each one sideways by a random amount.
warps.barOffset.description: A glitch or fractured look. `count` is the number of bars across the canvas, `angle` their direction in degrees, `intensity` (0–1) how far they shift. `seed` reshuffles the offsets. Bars drift with the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`.
examples: map: warps.barOffset({count: p('count'), angle: p('angle'), intensity: p('intensity'), seed: p('seed')})
warps.barOffset.signature: barOffset(slots: {count: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec; intensity: ArgSpec; seed: ArgSpec}): UvMapSource

params.name: slots
params.type: {count: ArgSpec; angle: ArgSpec; intensity: ArgSpec; seed: ArgSpec}

warps.gridCellDisplace.name: gridCellDisplace
warps.gridCellDisplace.summary: Move the child by a displacement field your own simulation produces, one grid cell at a time.
warps.gridCellDisplace.description: `output` names the simulation output (the same name you gave the field), `gridSize` the number of cells across the shorter side of the canvas. Every pixel in a cell moves together, by at most a tenth of the canvas. Add `uvRemapIdentityWhen: ({computeOutputs}) => !computeOutputs?.<output>` to the definition so the warp does nothing until the field exists.
examples:
map: warps.gridCellDisplace({gridSize: p('gridSize'), output: 'displacement'}),
uvRemapIdentityWhen: ({computeOutputs}) => !computeOutputs?.displacement,

warps.liquidDisplace.name: liquidDisplace
warps.liquidDisplace.summary: Move the child smoothly by a displacement field your own simulation produces.
warps.liquidDisplace.description: The liquid or cloth look. `output` names the simulation output. `intensity` scales the movement (the library uses 0–20), capped at about 15% of the canvas. Add `uvRemapIdentityWhen: ({computeOutputs}) => !computeOutputs?.<output>` to the definition so the warp does nothing until the field exists.
examples:
map: warps.liquidDisplace({intensity: p('intensity'), output: 'displacement'}),
uvRemapIdentityWhen: ({computeOutputs}) => !computeOutputs?.displacement,

warps.displaceByLayer.name: displaceByLayer
warps.displaceByLayer.summary: Distort the child using another layer's pixels as a displacement map.
warps.displaceByLayer.description: This one goes in `effect:`, not `map:`, because it reads a second layer. `source` is a prop marked `compileTime: true` that holds the other layer's id. `amount` (0–1) sets how far pixels move. `channels` is a prop holding `'twoAxis'` (red moves x, green moves y) or `'directional'` (brightness pushes along `angle`, in degrees). Mid-grey means no movement. `edges` is a prop marked `compileTime: true` holding `'stretch'`, `'transparent'`, `'mirror'` or `'wrap'`. With no source selected the child passes through unchanged.
examples: effect: warps.displaceByLayer({source: p('source'), amount: p('amount'), channels: p('channelMode'), angle: p('angle'), edges: p('edges')})
tips: An animated source layer displaces live.
warps.displaceByLayer.signature:
displaceByLayer(slots: {
    source: PropRef
    amount: ArgSpec
    channels: PropRef
    angle: ArgSpec
    edges: PropRef
}): GatherEffect

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    source: PropRef
    amount: ArgSpec
    channels: PropRef
    angle: ArgSpec
    edges: PropRef
}

mask.softBand.name: softBand
mask.softBand.summary: A soft band around a line, sharp on one side and long on the other.
mask.softBand.description: `distance` is the signed distance from the line: negative below it, positive above. Coverage rises from 0 to 1 as the distance crosses `below.from` to `below.to`, then falls back to 0 as it crosses `above.from` (default 0) to `above.to`. The shape under curtains, horizons and underlines.
examples: const curtain = mask.softBand({distance: sub(uv.member('y'), pathY), below: {from: -0.04, to: 0.015}, above: {to: height}})

params.name: opts

mask.softDisc.name: softDisc
mask.softDisc.summary: A filled disc with a soft, shaped edge.
mask.softDisc.description: `dist` is the distance from the disc's center and `radius` its size, both in the same units. The edge fades over `softness.width` either side of the radius, and `softness.curve` bends that fade: 1 is even, higher values pull it tighter toward the rim. The look of blobs, orbs and glow dots.
examples: const orb = mask.softDisc({dist, radius: params.uniforms.size, softness: {width: 0.08, curve: 1.5}})

params.name: opts

mask.crispFill.name: crispFill
mask.crispFill.summary: A clean fill of a shape: 1 inside, 0 outside.
mask.crispFill.description: `distance` is a signed distance, negative inside the shape, such as one from the `shape` words. `footprint` is how wide the edge blends. One pixel in the distance's units gives an anti-aliased edge. A wider value gives a deliberate soft edge.
examples: const bar = mask.crispFill({distance: shape.roundedRect(x, y, w, h, rounding), footprint: px})
tips: One pixel in uv is `div(1, viewport.member('y'))`, with `viewport` from `frames.surfaceOf`.
mask.crispFill.signature: crispFill(opts: {distance: Expr; footprint: Expr | number}): Expr

mask.crispStroke.name: crispStroke
mask.crispStroke.summary: A clean outline of a shape, or a drawn curve, of a given width.
mask.crispStroke.description: `distance` is a signed distance to the shape's edge or to the curve. The stroke is centered on the edge and `width` wide, in the distance's units. `footprint` blends the stroke's own edges, as in `crispFill`.
examples: const outline = mask.crispStroke({distance: shape.circle(x, y, radius), width: params.uniforms.lineWidth, footprint: px})
mask.crispStroke.signature: crispStroke(opts: {distance: Expr; width: Expr | number; footprint: Expr | number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {distance: Expr; width: Expr | number; footprint: Expr | number}

mask.radialMask.name: radialMask
mask.radialMask.summary: An amount that is 0 near a center and grows to 1 with distance, for an effect's strength.
mask.radialMask.description: Coverage stays 0 inside `radius` and reaches 1 at `radius + falloff`, measured in uv with the aspect corrected so the ring is round. Every slot takes a prop: `center` is a position prop, `radius` and `falloff` are numbers in uv. Chain `.times(p('intensity'))` to scale it.
examples: effect: tintToward(p('color'), {amount: radialMask({center: p('center'), radius: p('radius'), falloff: p('falloff')}).times(p('intensity'))})
tips: Also exported at the top level of `shaders/std`, so `radialMask` works without the `mask.` prefix.
mask.radialMask.signature: radialMask(slots: {center: PropRef; radius: PropRef; falloff: PropRef}): Scalar

math.add.name: add
math.add.description: Works on numbers and on vectors of the same size.
examples: const lifted = add(mul(noise, 0.5), 0.5) // a −1..1 signal moved into 0..1

math.sub.name: sub
math.sub.summary: The first value minus the second.
examples: const outside = sub(1, coverage) // flip a 0..1 mask

math.mul.name: mul
math.mul.description: Multiply a color by a 0..1 mask to fade it, or a coordinate by a prop to scale it.
examples: const rgb = mul(params.uniforms.color.member('rgb'), coverage)

math.div.name: div
math.div.summary: The first value divided by the second.
math.div.description: Dividing by zero produces infinity on the GPU, so guard a prop with `max` first.
examples: const normalized = div(dist, max(params.uniforms.radius, 0.001))

math.neg.name: neg
math.neg.summary: The value with its sign flipped.
examples: const falloff = exp(neg(mul(dist, 4)))

math.abs.name: abs
math.abs.description: Turns a signed distance into a distance from the line, so a stroke covers both sides.
examples: const fromLine = abs(sub(uv.member('y'), 0.5))

math.floor.name: floor
math.floor.summary: The value rounded down to a whole number.
math.floor.description: Gives the cell index when you tile a coordinate.
examples: const column = floor(mul(uv.member('x'), params.uniforms.columns))

math.ceil.name: ceil
math.ceil.summary: The value rounded up to a whole number.
examples: const rows = ceil(div(height, cell))

math.fract.name: fract
math.fract.summary: The fractional part of a value, 0..1.
math.fract.description: Repeats a coordinate every whole unit, which is how a pattern tiles.
examples: const inCell = fract(mul(uv, params.uniforms.tiles)) // 0..1 inside each tile

math.sqrt.name: sqrt
math.sqrt.summary: The square root of a value.
examples: const dist = sqrt(add(mul(dx, dx), mul(dy, dy)))

math.pow.name: pow
math.pow.summary: The first value raised to the power of the second.
math.pow.description: Shapes a 0..1 value: powers above 1 push it toward 0, powers below 1 toward 1. Keep the base non-negative.
examples: const hardened = pow(coverage, params.uniforms.hardness)

math.exp.name: exp
math.exp.description: With a negative argument it is the classic smooth falloff.
examples: const glow = exp(neg(mul(dist, params.uniforms.falloff)))

math.log.name: log
math.log.summary: The natural logarithm of a value.
examples: const octave = log(max(scale, 1))

math.sin.name: sin
math.sin.summary: The sine of an angle in radians, −1..1.
examples: const wave = sin(add(mul(uv.member('x'), 12), time))
tips: A degrees prop needs `mul(angle, 0.017453292519943295)` first.

math.cos.name: cos
math.cos.summary: The cosine of an angle in radians, −1..1.
examples: const spun = rotate2(delta, cos(angle), sin(angle))
tips: A degrees prop needs `mul(angle, 0.017453292519943295)` first.

math.tan.name: tan
math.tan.summary: The tangent of an angle in radians.
examples: const slope = tan(mul(params.uniforms.tilt, 0.017453292519943295))

math.atan2.name: atan2
math.atan2.summary: The angle of the point (x, y) in radians, −π..π.
math.atan2.description: Takes y first. Turns an offset from a center into an angle around it.
examples: const angle = atan2(delta.member('y'), delta.member('x'))

math.min.name: min
examples: const capped = min(brightness, 1)

math.max.name: max
examples: const safeRadius = max(params.uniforms.radius, 0.001)

math.clamp.name: clamp
math.clamp.summary: The value limited to the range `lo`..`hi`.
examples: const alpha = clamp(add(body, ring), 0, 1)
math.clamp.signature: clamp(x: Val, lo: Val, hi: Val): Expr

math.mix.name: mix
math.mix.summary: A blend from `a` to `b` by `t`, where 0 gives `a` and 1 gives `b`.
math.mix.description: Works on numbers and on colors. For two colors, pass `t` through `splat3` to blend every channel by the same amount.
examples: const rgb = mix(params.uniforms.colorA.member('rgb'), params.uniforms.colorB.member('rgb'), splat3(coverage))
math.mix.signature: mix(a: Val, b: Val, t: Val): Expr

math.step.name: step
math.step.summary: A hard edge: 0 when `x` is below `edge`, 1 from `edge` on.
examples: const lit = step(params.uniforms.threshold, brightness)

math.smoothstep.name: smoothstep
math.smoothstep.summary: A soft edge: 0 below `e0`, 1 above `e1`, an S-curve between.
math.smoothstep.description: The everyday word for turning a distance into a soft mask. Swap `e0` and `e1` to fade the other way.
examples: const coverage = sub(1, smoothstep(radius, add(radius, softness), dist)) // 1 inside, fading out
math.smoothstep.signature: smoothstep(e0: Val, e1: Val, x: Val): Expr

math.sign.name: sign
math.sign.summary: −1, 0 or 1 by the sign of the value.
examples: const side = sign(sub(uv.member('x'), 0.5))

math.length.name: length
math.length.description: The distance from the origin, or from a center when you pass the offset from it.
examples: const dist = length(sub(uv, params.uniforms.center))

math.distance.name: distance
examples: const toPointer = distance(uv, params.ctx.pointer)

math.dot.name: dot
math.dot.summary: The dot product of two vectors.
math.dot.description: With two unit vectors it is the cosine of the angle between them, which is how a light direction meets a surface normal.
examples: const facing = max(dot(normal, lightDir), 0)

math.normalize.name: normalize
math.normalize.description: A zero vector gives NaN, so keep the input non-zero.
examples: const dir = normalize(sub(params.uniforms.target, params.uniforms.origin))

math.cross.name: cross
math.cross.summary: The cross product of two 3D vectors.
examples: const normal = normalize(cross(tangentX, tangentY))

math.rotate2.name: rotate2
math.rotate2.summary: A 2D point rotated around the origin.
math.rotate2.description: Pass the cosine and sine of the angle in radians, computed once, and the same pair rotates every point.
examples: const spun = local(rotate2(delta, cos(angle), sin(angle)), 'spun')
math.rotate2.signature: rotate2(p: Val, cosA: Val, sinA: Val): Expr

math.reflect.name: reflect
math.reflect.summary: The direction `i` bounced off a surface with unit normal `n`.
examples: const bounce = reflect(viewDir, normal)

math.refract.name: refract
math.refract.summary: The direction `i` bent through a surface with unit normal `n`.
math.refract.description: `eta` is the ratio of refractive indices, about 0.66 going from air into glass.
examples: const bent = refract(viewDir, normal, 0.66)
math.refract.signature: refract(i: Val, n: Val, eta: Val): Expr

math.exp2.name: exp2
examples: const octaveScale = exp2(octave)

math.hashPhase.name: hashPhase
math.hashPhase.summary: A random but stable angle in radians, 0..2π, from a seed.
math.hashPhase.description: Use it to start each of several sine motions at a different point so they do not move in step. `salt` is a pair of constants. Give each independent phase its own pair.
examples: const wobble = sin(add(mul(t, 0.7), hashPhase(params.uniforms.seed, {k: 53.7, big: 3847.2})))
math.hashPhase.signature: hashPhase(seed: Val, salt: {k: number; big: number}): Expr

math.lt.name: lt
examples: const rgb = select(lt(dist, radius), insideRgb, outsideRgb)

math.le.name: le
math.le.summary: True when `a` is less than or equal to `b`.
examples: const inBand = select(le(abs(d), width), 1, 0)

math.gt.name: gt
examples: const highlights = select(gt(luma, 0.5), luma, 0)

math.ge.name: ge
math.ge.summary: True when `a` is greater than or equal to `b`.
examples: const rightHalf = select(ge(uv.member('x'), 0.5), 1, 0)

math.select.name: select
math.select.description: Both values are computed at every pixel, so this picks rather than skips work. For a soft transition use `mix` or `smoothstep` instead.
examples: const rgb = select(lt(dist, radius), params.uniforms.fill.member('rgb'), params.uniforms.background.member('rgb'))
math.select.signature: select(cond: Expr, ifTrue: Val, ifFalse: Val): Expr

math.float.name: float
math.float.summary: A plain number as an expression.
math.float.description: Rarely needed: every word here accepts numbers directly. Reach for it when something wants an expression and you only have a constant.
examples: const half = float(0.5)

math.vec2.name: vec2
examples: const offset = vec2(params.uniforms.shiftX, params.uniforms.shiftY)

math.vec3.name: vec3
math.vec3.summary: A 3D vector from three values, often a color without alpha.
examples: const warmWhite = vec3(1, 0.96, 0.9)
math.vec3.signature: vec3(x: Val, y: Val, z: Val): Expr

math.vec4.name: vec4
math.vec4.summary: A 4D vector, usually the final color with alpha.
math.vec4.description: Takes four numbers, or a vec3 followed by alpha. Return one of these from `paint:`.
examples: return vec4(rgb, coverage)

math.splat3.name: splat3
math.splat3.summary: One number copied into all three channels of a vec3.
math.splat3.description: The usual way to blend two colors by a single amount with `mix`.
examples: const rgb = mix(darkRgb, lightRgb, splat3(brightness))

math.local.name: local
math.local.summary: A value computed once per pixel and shared by everything that reads it.
math.local.description: Wrap any expression you use twice or more. `hint` is a short name that appears in the generated code and only has to be readable.
examples: const dist = local(length(sub(uv, params.uniforms.center)), 'dist')
tips: Without it, the same math is repeated at every place you use the value.

math.softPlus.name: softPlus
math.softPlus.summary: A soft hinge: about 0 for values well below zero, about `x` above, rounded near zero.
math.softPlus.description: `k` is the width of the rounded corner. Use it where a hard `max(x, 0)` would show a visible crease.
examples: const past = local(softPlus(sub(beam.along, beam.length), mul(softness, 0.6)), 'past')

math.gaussBell.name: gaussBell
math.gaussBell.summary: A bell curve: 1 at zero, falling toward 0 on both sides.
math.gaussBell.description: `k` sets the width. Larger values give a narrower bell. Pass a distance or a centered coordinate as `x`.
examples: const profile = gaussBell(div(beam.across, beamWidth), 2.5)

motion.phase.name: phase
motion.phase.summary: How far through a repeating cycle the clock is, 0..1.
motion.phase.description: `period` is the cycle length in seconds. The value ramps from 0 to 1 and snaps back.
examples: const sweep = motion.phase(animatedTime(params), params.uniforms.period)
motion.phase.signature: phase(t: Expr, period: Expr | number): Expr

motion.cycle.name: cycle
motion.cycle.summary: A repeating cycle as two numbers: `progress` (0..1 through the current cycle) and `index` (which cycle this is).
motion.cycle.description: `period` is the cycle length in seconds. The "every N seconds" word: fade something in with `progress`, and feed `index` to `cycleSeed` when each pass should look different.
examples: const {progress, index} = motion.cycle(animatedTime(params), 2) // a new pass every 2 s
motion.cycle.signature: cycle(t: Expr, period: Expr | number): {progress: Expr; index: Expr}

motion.cycleSeed.name: cycleSeed
motion.cycleSeed.summary: A random but stable number, 0..1, for each cycle index.
motion.cycleSeed.description: The same index always gives the same value, so a meteor keeps its angle for the whole pass and picks a new one next time. Change `salt` for a second, independent draw.
examples:
const hue = motion.cycleSeed(index)
const size = motion.cycleSeed(index, 1)

motion.pulseTrain.name: pulseTrain
motion.pulseTrain.summary: An on/off rhythm: 1 for the first part of each cycle, 0 for the rest.
motion.pulseTrain.description: `period` is seconds per cycle and `duty` is the on fraction, 0..1. `soften` eases both edges over that fraction of the cycle. Leave it at 0 for a hard blink.
examples: const blink = motion.pulseTrain(animatedTime(params), {period: 1.5, duty: 0.3, soften: 0.05})
motion.pulseTrain.signature: pulseTrain(t: Expr, opts: {period: Expr | number; duty: Expr | number; soften?: number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {period: Expr | number; duty: Expr | number; soften?: number}

motion.oscillate.name: oscillate
motion.oscillate.description: `rate` is cycles per second, default 1. `min` and `max` default to 0 and 1. `offset` shifts the starting point, in radians, so two oscillations can run out of step.
examples: const breathe = motion.oscillate(animatedTime(params), {rate: 0.5, min: 0.6, max: 1})
motion.oscillate.signature: oscillate(t: Expr, opts: {rate?: number; min?: Expr | number; max?: Expr | number; offset?: number}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {rate?: number; min?: Expr | number; max?: Expr | number; offset?: number}

motion.flashes.name: flashes
motion.flashes.summary: Short, bright flashes at a steady rate: dark most of the time, peaking briefly to 1.
motion.flashes.description: `rate` is how fast it runs (radians per second of the clock, so about 1 is one flash every six seconds). `offset` shifts when the flashes land, in radians; give each element its own (a hash times 2π) so they don't flash together. `sharpness` sets how brief each flash is: 2, 4, 8 or 16, where larger is briefer.
examples: const blink = motion.flashes(animatedTime(params), {rate: 1.4, offset: mul(seed, 6.283), sharpness: 8})
motion.flashes.signature: flashes(t: Expr, opts: {rate: Expr | number; offset?: Expr | number; sharpness: 2 | 4 | 8 | 16}): Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {rate: Expr | number; offset?: Expr | number; sharpness: 2 | 4 | 8 | 16}

motion.easeIn.name: easeIn
motion.easeIn.summary: A 0..1 value that starts slow and speeds up.
examples: const grow = motion.easeIn(progress)

motion.easeOut.name: easeOut
motion.easeOut.summary: A 0..1 value that starts fast and slows to a stop.
examples: const settle = motion.easeOut(progress)

motion.easeInOut.name: easeInOut
motion.easeInOut.summary: A 0..1 value that starts slow, speeds up, and slows again at the end.
examples: const glide = motion.easeInOut(progress)

motion.oscillating.name: oscillating
motion.oscillating.summary: A knob that sweeps between `min` and `max` on its own, for any slot that takes a prop.
motion.oscillating.description: Same options as `oscillate`. By default it follows the page clock. Pass `clock: 'node'` to follow the layer's own speed prop instead, after declaring `animatedTime` on the definition.
examples: map: warps.twirl({center: p('center'), intensity: motion.oscillating({rate: 0.25, min: 0.4, max: 1.6, clock: 'node'})})
tips: Inside `map:` it always follows the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` there.
motion.oscillating.signature: oscillating(opts: {rate?: number; min?: Expr | number; max?: Expr | number; offset?: number; clock?: SignalClock}): Scalar

params.name: opts
params.type: {rate?: number; min?: Expr | number; max?: Expr | number; offset?: number; clock?: SignalClock}

motion.pulsing.name: pulsing
motion.pulsing.summary: A knob that switches on and off in a rhythm, for any slot that takes a prop.
motion.pulsing.description: `period` is seconds per cycle, `duty` the on fraction, `soften` the edge ease, as in `pulseTrain`. Follows the page clock unless `clock: 'node'` is set.
examples: effect: effects.color.saturate(motion.pulsing({period: 2, duty: 0.5, soften: 0.1})) // color, then gray, then color
tips: Inside `map:` it always follows the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` there.
motion.pulsing.signature: pulsing(opts: {period: number; duty: number; soften?: number; clock?: SignalClock}): Scalar

params.name: opts
params.type: {period: number; duty: number; soften?: number; clock?: SignalClock}

signal.pointer.name: pointer
signal.pointer.summary: The pointer's position, for a simulation step that reacts to the cursor.
signal.pointer.description: The teleport guard is on by default: when the cursor jumps a long way in one frame, the jump adds no motion, so a cursor entering the canvas does not slam the simulation.
examples: op.splat({at: pointer({teleportGuard: 'on'}), amount: pointerSpeed({max: 2}), radius: p('radius')})
tips: Keep the default `'on'` for cursor effects. Use `'off'` only when a jump should count as a stroke — a pointer that is set by code rather than a real cursor, for example.

signal.pointerSpeed.name: pointerSpeed
signal.pointerSpeed.summary: The pointer's speed, capped at `max`, as the strength of a simulation step.
signal.pointerSpeed.description: Speed is in uv per second. A still cursor gives 0, a flick across the canvas gives a value near `max`. Default cap is 2.
examples: op.splat({at: pointer(), amount: pointerSpeed({max: 2}), radius: p('radius')})

signal.cpuHash01.name: cpuHash01
signal.cpuHash01.summary: A random but stable number, 0..1, from a seed, computed in JavaScript.
signal.cpuHash01.description: Use it when a per-seed constant is worked out once on the CPU rather than at every pixel, such as the size and drift of each light in a set.
examples:
const radiusX = cpuHash01(seed) * 0.5 + 0.2
const radiusY = cpuHash01(seed + 37) * 0.25 + 0.1

filter.tintToward.name: tintToward
filter.tintToward.summary: Mix the child's color toward one color by an amount, leaving its alpha alone.
filter.tintToward.description: `color` is a color prop. `amount` runs 0 (no change) to 1 (fully that color) and can be a number, a prop, or a value that varies per pixel such as a mask. Pointwise.
examples: effect: tintToward(p('color'), {amount: radialMask({center: p('center'), radius: p('radius'), falloff: p('falloff')}).times(p('intensity'))})
tips: Pair it with `identityWhen: isZero('intensity')` so the filter costs nothing at zero.

filter.displaceBy.name: displaceBy
filter.displaceBy.summary: Push the child's pixels around by a vector field from one of your simulations.
filter.displaceBy.description: `field` is a simulation output, such as `waves.output('displacement')` from `simulate.grid`. `strength` scales the push (the library uses 0–20), capped at about 15% of the canvas. `chromatic` (0–3) splits red and blue slightly apart from green along the push, like a lens. `edges` is a prop marked `compileTime: true` holding `'stretch'`, `'transparent'`, `'mirror'` or `'wrap'`. Gather.
examples: effect: displaceBy(waves.output('displacement'), {strength: p('intensity'), chromatic: p('chromaticSplit'), edges: p('edges')})
tips: The simulation must derive the field with `op.gradient()`; the definition fails loudly otherwise.
filter.displaceBy.signature: displaceBy(field: import('./sim').SimOutputRef, opts: {strength: PropRef; chromatic: PropRef; edges: PropRef}): DisplaceByEffect

filter.pointwise.name: pointwise
filter.pointwise.summary: Write your own pointwise effect: a function of the child's color at this pixel.
filter.pointwise.description: Give it `build`, which receives `params.childNode` (the child's color here) and `params.uniforms` (your props), and returns the new color. Keep the child's alpha unless you mean to change it. No texture is involved, so it is the cheapest kind of filter.
examples: effect: pointwise({build: ({childNode, uniforms}) => math.vec4(math.mul(childNode.member('rgb'), uniforms.gain), childNode.member('a'))})

filter.gather.name: gather
filter.gather.summary: Write your own gather effect: a function that can read the child anywhere.
filter.gather.description: Give it `build`, which receives the child as a texture (`params.texture`, or `params.sampleStraight(uv)` for plain colors), `params.ctx.uv` for this pixel and `params.uniforms` for your props. Return the new color. Set `resultAlpha: 'straight'` when you built the color from `sampleStraight`. Costs one extra render of the child.
examples: effect: gather({resultAlpha: 'straight', build: ({sampleStraight, ctx, uniforms}) => sampleStraight(math.add(ctx.uv, uniforms.shift))})
tips: Reach for `pointwise` first. Only gather when the effect needs pixels other than this one.

filter.paintThrough.name: paintThrough
filter.paintThrough.summary: Show a paint through the child, so the child becomes the mask.
filter.paintThrough.description: Like CSS `mask-image` the other way round: the paint is the content and the child decides where it shows. `by: 'alpha'` (the default) reveals the paint wherever the child is opaque, which gives a gradient through text. `by: 'luminance'` reveals it where the child is bright. The paint's own alpha still applies. Pointwise.
examples: effect: paintThrough(paint.rampOver(paint.dist.radial({center: p('center'), radius: p('radius'), aspect: 1, skew: 0}), paint.pair(p('colorA'), p('colorB'), p('colorSpace'))))

effects.color.hueRotate.name: hueRotate
effects.color.hueRotate.summary: Rotate the child's hue around the color wheel.
effects.color.hueRotate.description: `shift` is in degrees. 0 leaves the color unchanged, 180 swaps every color for its complement, 360 comes back around. Alpha kept.
examples: effect: hueRotate(p('shift'))
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isZero('shift')` so the filter is skipped at 0.

effects.color.saturate.name: saturate
effects.color.saturate.description: `intensity` is a multiplier: 0 is grayscale, 1 leaves the color unchanged, values above 1 (up to about 3) push colors past their original saturation.
examples: effect: saturate(p('intensity'))
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isValue('intensity', 1)`; the no-change value is 1, not 0.

effects.color.vibrance.name: vibrance
effects.color.vibrance.summary: Boost muted colors while leaving already-vivid ones mostly alone.
effects.color.vibrance.description: `intensity` is an adjustment around 0 (about −2 to 2): 0 leaves the color unchanged, positive values add saturation to dull pixels, negative values drain it.
examples: effect: vibrance(p('intensity'))
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isZero('intensity')`.

effects.color.brightnessContrast.name: brightnessContrast
effects.color.brightnessContrast.summary: Adjust the child's brightness and contrast together.
effects.color.brightnessContrast.description: Both are sliders from −1 to 1 with 0 as no change. `brightness` adds to every channel. `contrast` stretches colors away from mid-gray (positive) or flattens them toward it (negative).
examples: effect: brightnessContrast({brightness: p('brightness'), contrast: p('contrast')})
tips: Declare `identityWhen: allOf(isZero('brightness'), isZero('contrast'))`.

effects.color.exposure.name: exposure
effects.color.exposure.summary: Multiply the child's brightness, like opening a camera's aperture.
effects.color.exposure.description: `gain` of 1 leaves the color unchanged, 0.5 halves it, 2 doubles it. Blacks stay black. Values pushed above 1 are not clamped, so a glow or bloom filter placed after this one can pick them up.
examples: effect: exposure(p('exposure'))
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isValue('exposure', 1)`; the no-change value is 1.

effects.color.grayscale.name: grayscale
effects.color.grayscale.summary: Turn the child black and white, weighted the way the eye sees brightness.
examples: effect: grayscale()

effects.color.invert.name: invert
effects.color.invert.summary: Flip every color of the child to its negative.
examples: effect: invert()

effects.color.solarize.name: solarize
effects.color.solarize.summary: Invert only the bright parts of the child, the darkroom solarization look.
effects.color.solarize.description: `threshold` (0–1) is the brightness above which a pixel flips. `strength` (0–1) fades the flipped result over the original: 0 is untouched, 1 is fully solarized.
examples: effect: solarize({threshold: p('threshold'), strength: p('strength')})
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isZero('strength')`.

effects.color.posterize.name: posterize
effects.color.posterize.summary: Reduce the child to a few flat color levels, like a screen-printed poster.
effects.color.posterize.description: `steps` is the number of levels per channel; 2 to 20 is the useful range. Fewer steps give bolder bands.
examples: effect: posterize(p('levels'))

effects.color.tint.name: tint
effects.color.tint.summary: Wash the child toward one color.
effects.color.tint.description: `amount` is 0–1: 0 leaves the child alone, 1 replaces its color entirely. While the boolean `preserveLuminosity` prop is on, the result is scaled back to the child's original brightness, so the tint changes hue without darkening. Declare that prop `compileTime: true` with `transform: (v) => (v ? 1 : 0)`. Alpha kept.
examples: effect: tint({color: p('color'), amount: p('amount'), preserveLuminosity: p('preserveLuminosity')})
tips: Reach for `tintToward` instead when you do not need the brightness-preserving mode.
effects.color.tint.signature: tint(slots: {color: PropRef; amount: ArgSpec; preserveLuminosity: PropRef}): PointwiseEffect

effects.color.filmGrain.name: filmGrain
effects.color.filmGrain.summary: Sprinkle film grain over the child, heaviest in the shadows.
effects.color.filmGrain.description: `strength` (0–1) sets how visible the grain is. `bias` (0–10) concentrates it in darker areas; 0 grains everything evenly. While the boolean `animated` prop is on the pattern changes every frame; off, it freezes. The definition must declare the grain's clock: `extraFields: {animTime: {schema: schema.f32, initial: 0}}`. Alpha kept.
examples: effect: filmGrain({strength: p('strength'), bias: p('bias'), animated: p('animated')})
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isZero('strength')`.
effects.color.filmGrain.signature: filmGrain(slots: {strength: ArgSpec; bias: ArgSpec; animated: PropRef}): PointwiseEffect

effects.color.isolines.name: isolines
effects.color.isolines.summary: Draw topographic contour lines over the child, traced from its brightness or its alpha.
effects.color.isolines.description: `levels` is how many contours (2–30). `lineWidth` is in pixels. `softness` (0–1) blurs the line edges. `gamma` crowds the contours toward the highlights (below 1) or the shadows (above 1). The boolean `invert` prop flips the source. `source` (`'luminance' | 'alpha'`) and `colorMode` (`'source' | 'custom'`) are select props declared `compileTime: true`: in source mode the lines take the child's own colors over transparent, in custom mode they take `lineColor` over `backgroundColor`.
examples: effect: isolines({source: p('source'), levels: p('levels'), lineWidth: p('lineWidth'), softness: p('softness'), gamma: p('gamma'), invert: p('invert'), colorMode: p('colorMode'), lineColor: p('lineColor'), backgroundColor: p('backgroundColor')})
tips: The lines replace the child rather than sit over it; set `blendWithChildren: false` in the definition.
effects.color.isolines.signature:
isolines(slots: {
    source: PropRef
    levels: ArgSpec
    lineWidth: ArgSpec
    softness: ArgSpec
    gamma: ArgSpec
    invert: ArgSpec
    colorMode: PropRef
    lineColor: PropRef
    backgroundColor: PropRef
}): PointwiseEffect

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    source: PropRef
    levels: ArgSpec
    lineWidth: ArgSpec
    softness: ArgSpec
    gamma: ArgSpec
    invert: ArgSpec
    colorMode: PropRef
    lineColor: PropRef
    backgroundColor: PropRef
}

effects.color.duotone.name: duotone
effects.color.duotone.summary: Repaint the child in two colors: `colorA` for the shadows, `colorB` for the highlights.
effects.color.duotone.description: `blend` (0–1) is the brightness where the two meet. `colorSpace` is a select prop with `transform: transformColorSpace` and `compileTime: true`; it picks the space the colors mix in (`'oklch'` for vivid, `'linear'` for plain). Alpha kept.
examples: effect: duotone({colorA: p('colorA'), colorB: p('colorB'), blend: p('blend'), colorSpace: p('colorSpace')})
effects.color.duotone.signature: duotone(slots: {colorA: PropRef; colorB: PropRef; blend: ArgSpec; colorSpace: PropRef}): PointwiseEffect

params.name: slots
params.type: {colorA: PropRef; colorB: PropRef; blend: ArgSpec; colorSpace: PropRef}

effects.color.tritone.name: tritone
effects.color.tritone.summary: Repaint the child in three colors: `colorA` for the shadows, `colorB` for the midtones, `colorC` for the highlights.
effects.color.tritone.description: `blendMid` (0–1) is the brightness the midtone color sits at. `colorSpace` is a select prop with `transform: transformColorSpace` and `compileTime: true`; it picks the space the colors mix in. Alpha kept.
examples: effect: tritone({colorA: p('colorA'), colorB: p('colorB'), colorC: p('colorC'), blendMid: p('blendMid'), colorSpace: p('colorSpace')})
effects.color.tritone.signature: tritone(slots: {colorA: PropRef; colorB: PropRef; colorC: PropRef; blendMid: ArgSpec; colorSpace: PropRef}): PointwiseEffect

params.name: slots
params.type: {colorA: PropRef; colorB: PropRef; colorC: PropRef; blendMid: ArgSpec; colorSpace: PropRef}

effects.color.gradientMap.name: gradientMap
effects.color.gradientMap.summary: Recolor the child by its brightness through a gradient, the Photoshop gradient map.
effects.color.gradientMap.description: `palette` is a select prop declared `compileTime: true`: one of the built-in gradients `'rainbow' | 'sunset' | 'ocean' | 'fire' | 'pastel' | 'neon'`, or `'custom'` to use `colorLow`, `colorMid` and `colorHigh` (shadows, midtones, highlights) mixed in `colorSpace`. `blackPoint` and `whitePoint` (0–1) clip the input brightness. `contrast` (0–3) steepens the mapping. `speed` scrolls the gradient over time; 0 holds it still. `strength` (0–1) fades the result over the original. Alpha kept.
examples: effect: gradientMap({palette: p('palette'), colorLow: p('colorLow'), colorMid: p('colorMid'), colorHigh: p('colorHigh'), speed: p('speed'), contrast: p('contrast'), blackPoint: p('blackPoint'), whitePoint: p('whitePoint'), strength: p('strength'), colorSpace: p('colorSpace')})
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isZero('strength')`.
effects.color.gradientMap.signature:
gradientMap(slots: {
    palette: PropRef
    colorLow: PropRef
    colorMid: PropRef
    colorHigh: PropRef
    speed: PropRef
    contrast: ArgSpec
    blackPoint: ArgSpec
    whitePoint: ArgSpec
    strength: PropRef
    colorSpace: PropRef
}): PointwiseEffect

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    palette: PropRef
    colorLow: PropRef
    colorMid: PropRef
    colorHigh: PropRef
    speed: PropRef
    contrast: ArgSpec
    blackPoint: ArgSpec
    whitePoint: ArgSpec
    strength: PropRef
    colorSpace: PropRef
}

effects.color.lutAtlasGrade.name: lutAtlasGrade
effects.color.lutAtlasGrade.summary: Grade a color through a measured 3D color lookup table (LUT), the film-stock look.
effects.color.lutAtlasGrade.description: Returns a stage `(color, params) => gradedColor` for a `gpu:` fragment, not an `effect:`. `select` is a select prop declared `compileTime: true` that names the table; `decode(key)` returns that table's bytes as RGBA, `size` levels per channel laid out as `size` square slices side by side (red across, green down, one slice per blue level), sRGB in and out. `fallback` is the key used when the prop is unset. `strength` (0–1) fades the graded color over the original. Alpha kept; colors brighter than white grade as white.
examples:
const grade = lutAtlasGrade({select: p('stock'), strength: p('strength'), size: 17, decode: decodeStockLut, fallback: 'portrait400', label: 'film-lut'})
// then, inside the definition's gpu.fragment: grade(childColor, params)
tips: Changing `select` rebuilds the shader; keep the table list short.
effects.color.lutAtlasGrade.signature:
lutAtlasGrade(slots: {
    select: PropRef
    strength: PropRef
    size: number
    decode: (key: string) => Uint8Array
    fallback: string
    label: string
}): (color: Expr, params: FilterParams | GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    select: PropRef
    strength: PropRef
    size: number
    decode: (key: string) => Uint8Array
    fallback: string
    label: string
}

effects.blurs.gatherStack.name: gatherStack
effects.blurs.gatherStack.summary: Assemble an effect from one sampling stage and an ordered list of overlay stages.
effects.blurs.gatherStack.description: The child renders to a texture, the sampling stage reads it, and each overlay edits the result in turn. Put the result in a filter's `effect:` field. Pass `{resultAlpha: 'straight'}` only when the stack already returns straight (not premultiplied) alpha, as `crispTap` and `refractedTaps` do.
examples: effect: gatherStack(rgbSplit({amount: p('colorShift')}), [scanlines({frequency: p('lines'), intensity: 0.3}), opaque()])
tips: An empty overlay list is fine: `gatherStack(stage, [])` wraps a lone sampling stage.
effects.blurs.gatherStack.signature: gatherStack(sample: SampleStage, overlays: OverlayStage[], opts?: {resultAlpha?: 'premultiplied' | 'straight'}): GatherEffect

effects.blurs.rgbSplit.name: rgbSplit
effects.blurs.rgbSplit.summary: The child with its red and blue pulled a little to either side, like a misaligned CRT.
effects.blurs.rgbSplit.description: `amount` is the shift; 1 moves red and blue each by 0.002 of the canvas width, 0–10 is the usual range. Returns a three-channel color, so finish the stack with `opaque`.
examples: effect: gatherStack(rgbSplit({amount: p('colorShift')}), [opaque()])

effects.blurs.tapeWarp.name: tapeWarp
effects.blurs.tapeWarp.summary: The wobbling, jittering coordinates of a worn VHS tape, to feed into `chromaSmearTaps`.
effects.blurs.tapeWarp.description: `wobble` (0–5) is the tape damage: waves, creases and head-switching noise that burst on and off over time. `jitter` (0–1) is fine per-scanline noise. `speed` scales the global clock, so the definition needs no `animatedTime`.
examples: chromaSmearTaps({warp: tapeWarp({wobble: p('wobble'), jitter: p('scanlineNoise'), speed: p('speed')}), smear: p('smear')})
effects.blurs.tapeWarp.signature: tapeWarp(opts: {wobble: ArgSpec; jitter: ArgSpec; speed: ArgSpec}): (params: RttFilterParams) => Expr

effects.blurs.chromaSmearTaps.name: chromaSmearTaps
effects.blurs.chromaSmearTaps.summary: The child sampled like a VHS deck: brightness stays sharp while color bleeds sideways.
effects.blurs.chromaSmearTaps.description: `warp` is the coordinate set from `tapeWarp`. `smear` sets how far color trails; positive trails it to the right, negative to the left, −2 to 2 is the usual range. Alpha comes from the sharp tap.
examples: effect: gatherStack(chromaSmearTaps({warp: tapeWarp({wobble: p('wobble'), jitter: p('noise'), speed: p('speed')}), smear: p('smear')}), [beatPulse({wobble: p('wobble'), speed: p('speed')})])
effects.blurs.chromaSmearTaps.signature: chromaSmearTaps(opts: {warp: (params: RttFilterParams) => Expr; smear: ArgSpec}): SampleStage

effects.blurs.brightestNear.name: brightestNear
effects.blurs.brightestNear.summary: The brightest color in a small ring around a point: the layer grown outward, so a spot just outside a bright area still reads as bright.
effects.blurs.brightestNear.description: `read` samples the layer at a uv and returns straight color (pass `params.sampleStraight`). `center` is the uv to look around; `radius` is the ring's radius per axis in uv, as a `vec2` (divide a pixel radius by the viewport size). `taps` points sit evenly round the ring starting at `angle` degrees, plus the centre itself. Returns the brightest of them as `color` (straight) and its brightness as `luma` (Rec.709 luminance times alpha).
examples: const {color, luma} = brightestNear(params.sampleStraight, pointUV, {radius: div(p, viewport), taps: 4, angle: 45})
tips:
Thin bright details smaller than the gap between taps can slip through; more taps
close the gaps at one sample each.

effects.blurs.adjust.name: adjust
effects.blurs.adjust.summary: Brightness and contrast, pivoting around mid-grey.
effects.blurs.adjust.description: 1 leaves both unchanged; 0.5–2 is the usual range. Works on the three-channel color of a stack begun with `rgbSplit`.
examples: adjust({brightness: p('brightness'), contrast: p('contrast')})

effects.blurs.scanlines.name: scanlines
effects.blurs.scanlines.summary: Horizontal scanlines darkening the child in a smooth wave.
effects.blurs.scanlines.description: `frequency` is the number of lines from top to bottom (100–800). `intensity` (0–1) is how dark the troughs get. Works on the three-channel color of a stack begun with `rgbSplit`.
examples: scanlines({frequency: p('scanlineFrequency'), intensity: p('scanlineIntensity')})

effects.blurs.phosphorMask.name: phosphorMask
effects.blurs.phosphorMask.summary: A faint red, green and blue phosphor stripe pattern across the child.
effects.blurs.phosphorMask.description: `pitch` sets how many stripes fit across the canvas, about half of `pitch`; 8–128 is the usual range. Works on the three-channel color of a stack begun with `rgbSplit`.
examples: phosphorMask({pitch: p('pixelSize')})

effects.blurs.vignetteOverlay.name: vignetteOverlay
effects.blurs.vignetteOverlay.summary: Darkens the child toward its corners.
effects.blurs.vignetteOverlay.description: `radius` (0–1) is how far the darkening reaches inward, 0 for the edges only and 1 for all the way to the centre. `intensity` (0–1) blends it in. Round on any canvas shape. Works on the three-channel color of a stack begun with `rgbSplit`.
examples: vignetteOverlay({radius: p('vignetteRadius'), intensity: p('vignetteIntensity')})

effects.blurs.opaque.name: opaque
effects.blurs.opaque.summary: Closes a three-channel stack as a solid color with alpha 1.
effects.blurs.opaque.description: Put it last after `rgbSplit`, `adjust`, `scanlines`, `phosphorMask` or `vignetteOverlay`, which work on color only and drop the child's alpha.
examples: effect: gatherStack(rgbSplit({amount: 1}), [scanlines({frequency: 200, intensity: 0.3}), opaque()])

effects.blurs.beatPulse.name: beatPulse
effects.blurs.beatPulse.summary: A faint brightness throb, like the mains hum of an old television.
effects.blurs.beatPulse.description: `wobble` scales the throb (0 turns it off). `speed` scales the global clock. Works on the four-channel color of a stack begun with `chromaSmearTaps`.
examples: beatPulse({wobble: p('wobble'), speed: p('speed')})

effects.blurs.blurPath.linear.name: linear
effects.blurs.blurPath.linear.summary: A straight streak along an angle prop, in degrees (0 points right, 90 points down).
examples: effect: motionBlur({path: blurPath.linear(p('angle')), amount: p('intensity')})

effects.blurs.blurPath.orbit.name: orbit
effects.blurs.blurPath.orbit.summary: An arc streak rotating around a center prop (a position in uv).
examples: effect: motionBlur({path: blurPath.orbit(p('center')), amount: p('intensity')})

effects.blurs.blurPath.zoom.name: zoom
effects.blurs.blurPath.zoom.summary: A radial streak rushing outward from a center prop (a position in uv).
examples: effect: motionBlur({path: blurPath.zoom(p('center')), amount: p('intensity')})

effects.blurs.blurPath.name: blurPath
effects.blurs.blurPath.summary: The three paths `motionBlur` can smear along.
examples: effect: motionBlur({path: blurPath.zoom(p('center')), amount: p('intensity')})

effects.blurs.motionBlur.name: motionBlur
effects.blurs.motionBlur.summary: Smears the child along a path: a straight streak, an arc around a point, or a zoom out of a point.
effects.blurs.motionBlur.description: `amount` is a 0–100 intensity. A linear streak spans about twice `amount` in pixels; at 100 an orbit sweeps about 29 degrees and a zoom pulls in from twice the distance to its center. `detail` adds the lens dials (`dispersion`, `falloff`, `focus`) and streak dials (`bias`, `highlights`, `jitter`, and `spiral` for a zoom); all are off at 0 and cost nothing until one is set.
examples: effect: motionBlur({path: blurPath.linear(p('angle')), amount: p('intensity')})

effect: motionBlur({path: blurPath.zoom(p('center')), amount: p('intensity'), detail: {dispersion: p('dispersion'), falloff: p('falloff'), focus: p('focus'), bias: p('bias'), highlights: p('highlights'), jitter: p('jitter'), spiral: p('spiral')}})
tips: Samples past the canvas edge repeat the border color. Wrap the layer in a larger group if the smear must fade out instead.
Give every `detail` prop `recompile: crosses(0)`; the detail gather is only compiled while one of them is non-zero.
effects.blurs.motionBlur.signature: motionBlur(opts: {path: BlurPathSpec; amount: ArgSpec; detail?: MotionBlurDetailSlots}): GatherEffect

effects.blurs.scatter.name: scatter
effects.blurs.scatter.summary: Scatters every pixel of the child by a random offset: a grainy diffusion, not a smooth blur.
effects.blurs.scatter.description: `amount` is the largest offset in pixels. `edges` is a prop with `transform: transformEdges` and `compileTime: true` ('stretch' | 'transparent' | 'mirror' | 'wrap') that says what to read where an offset lands outside the canvas. `chromatic` (0–1, optional) scatters red and blue on their own, for a sparkly colour grain; it is off at 0, so give it `recompile: crosses(0)`.
examples: effect: scatter({amount: p('intensity'), edges: p('edges')})
effects.blurs.scatter.signature: scatter(opts: {amount: ArgSpec; edges: PropRef; chromatic?: PropRef}): GatherEffect

effects.blurs.sharpen.name: sharpen
effects.blurs.sharpen.summary: Sharpens the child by boosting the contrast between each pixel and its neighbours.
effects.blurs.sharpen.description: `amount` 0 leaves the child unchanged; 0–5 is the usual range. Alpha is untouched.
examples: effect: sharpen(p('sharpness'))
tips: Declare `identityWhen: isZero('sharpness')` and `recompile: crosses(0)` on the prop so 0 costs nothing.

effects.blurs.pixelate.name: pixelate
effects.blurs.pixelate.summary: Turns the child into a grid of flat cells, each showing one color.
effects.blurs.pixelate.description: `scale` is the number of cells along the canvas's longer edge (1–200; more cells means smaller pixels). `gap` (0–1) is the transparent space between cells as a fraction of a cell. `roundness` (0–1) rounds each cell from a square to a circle.
examples: effect: pixelate({scale: p('scale'), gap: p('gap'), roundness: p('roundness')})
effects.blurs.pixelate.signature: pixelate(opts: {scale: ArgSpec; gap: ArgSpec; roundness: ArgSpec}): GatherEffect

effects.blurs.sphereFrame.name: sphereFrame
effects.blurs.sphereFrame.summary: The geometry of a sphere bulging out of the canvas: where each pixel reads the child from, where the sphere ends, and which way its surface faces.
effects.blurs.sphereFrame.description: `center` is a position in uv. `radius` 1 is half the canvas height. `depth` is how far it bulges toward the viewer, 0 for flat and up to about 3. Feed the frame to `crispTap` and `rimLit`.
examples: const sphere = sphereFrame({center: p('center'), radius: p('radius'), depth: p('depth')})
effects.blurs.sphereFrame.signature: sphereFrame(opts: {center: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec; depth: ArgSpec}): GatherFrame

effects.blurs.crispTap.name: crispTap
effects.blurs.crispTap.summary: One clean sample of the child at a frame's warped coordinate.
effects.blurs.crispTap.description: Use it under a warp that magnifies: hard edges in the child (text, a logo) stay smooth instead of breaking into facets. Returns straight alpha, so close the stack with `{resultAlpha: 'straight'}`.
examples: effect: gatherStack(crispTap(sphere), [rimLit(sphere, {position: p('light'), intensity: 0.5, softness: 0.5, color: p('lightColor')})], {resultAlpha: 'straight'})

effects.blurs.rimLit.name: rimLit
effects.blurs.rimLit.summary: A tinted rim of light around the edge of a bulged surface, added on top of the child's color.
effects.blurs.rimLit.description: `position` is where the light sits, in uv. `intensity` (0–1) is its strength, 0 for off. `softness` (0–1) runs from a hard edge to a soft glow. `color` is a color prop. Outside the frame's surface the result is transparent.
examples: rimLit(sphere, {position: p('lightPosition'), intensity: p('lightIntensity'), softness: p('lightSoftness'), color: p('lightColor')})

params.name: opts

effects.blurs.glitchFrame.name: glitchFrame
effects.blurs.glitchFrame.summary: The shared geometry of a digital glitch: when bursts fire, which horizontal bands jitter, and which blocks shift or flip.
effects.blurs.glitchFrame.description: `intensity` (0–1) sets both the strength and how often bursts happen. `speed` scales the global clock, so no `animatedTime` is needed. `blockDensity` is the base number of bands (2–50). `mirrorAmount` (0–1) is the chance a block shows flipped content. Keep the frame in a module constant and pass it to `glitchRgbSplit`, `colorBarFills` and `distortedScanlines`.
examples: const glitch = glitchFrame({intensity: p('intensity'), speed: p('speed'), blockDensity: p('blockDensity'), mirrorAmount: p('mirrorAmount')})

params.name: opts

effects.blurs.glitchRgbSplit.name: glitchRgbSplit
effects.blurs.glitchRgbSplit.summary: The child sampled through a glitch frame, with red and blue pulled apart inside the active bands.
effects.blurs.glitchRgbSplit.description: `shift` is the split distance, 0–20. A transparent child stays transparent through the glitch.
examples: effect: gatherStack(glitchRgbSplit(glitch, {shift: p('rgbShift')}), [colorBarFills(glitch, {intensity: 0.2})])

effects.blurs.colorBarFills.name: colorBarFills
effects.blurs.colorBarFills.summary: Neon color bars filling the blocks a glitch frame currently has active.
effects.blurs.colorBarFills.description: `intensity` (0–1) is how strongly the bars show. They respect the child's alpha.
examples: colorBarFills(glitch, {intensity: p('colorBarIntensity')})

effects.blurs.distortedScanlines.name: distortedScanlines
effects.blurs.distortedScanlines.summary: CRT-style scanlines that appear only where a glitch frame is currently distorting.
examples: distortedScanlines(glitch, {intensity: p('scanlineIntensity')})

effects.blurs.gaussianBlur.name: gaussianBlur
effects.blurs.gaussianBlur.summary: A soft, even blur of the child.
effects.blurs.gaussianBlur.description: `intensity` is a prop from 0 to about 200; 100 is a blur radius of about 36 pixels. Bind the prop to a map to vary the blur across the canvas. Only color blurs; the child's alpha stays sharp, so soft edges need a group or mask around the layer.
examples: ...gaussianBlur({intensity: p('intensity')})
tips: The blur runs at a fixed working resolution, so its cost does not grow with the canvas.

effects.blurs.channelBlur.name: channelBlur
effects.blurs.channelBlur.summary: Blurs red, green and blue by separate amounts, for a soft chromatic fringe.
effects.blurs.channelBlur.description: Each of `red`, `green` and `blue` is a prop from 0 to 100; 100 is a radius of about 10 pixels. A channel at 0 stays exactly sharp.
examples: ...channelBlur({red: p('redIntensity'), green: p('greenIntensity'), blue: p('blueIntensity')})
effects.blurs.channelBlur.signature: channelBlur(opts: {red: PropRef; green: PropRef; blue: PropRef}): ComputeBackedEffect

effects.blurs.progressiveBlur.name: progressiveBlur
effects.blurs.progressiveBlur.summary: A blur that ramps from sharp to full strength in one direction across the child.
effects.blurs.progressiveBlur.description: The ramp starts at `center` (a position in uv) and runs along `angle` (degrees, 0 points right), reaching full blur `falloff` (0–1, in uv) past the center. `intensity` (0–100) is the blur at the far end; 100 is a radius of about 36 pixels. Bind `intensity` to a map to vary the ceiling per pixel. Alpha stays sharp. `detail` adds the lens dials (see `VariableBlurDetailSlots`), both off at 0.
examples: ...progressiveBlur({intensity: p('intensity'), angle: p('angle'), center: p('center'), falloff: p('falloff')})
effects.blurs.progressiveBlur.signature:
progressiveBlur(opts: {
    intensity: PropRef
    angle: PropRef
    center: PropRef
    falloff: PropRef
    detail?: VariableBlurDetailSlots
}): ComputeBackedEffect

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    intensity: PropRef
    angle: PropRef
    center: PropRef
    falloff: PropRef
    detail?: VariableBlurDetailSlots
}

effects.blurs.tiltShift.name: tiltShift
effects.blurs.tiltShift.summary: Keeps a band of the child in focus and blurs everything beyond it, like a tilt-shift lens.
effects.blurs.tiltShift.description: The band runs through `center` (a position in uv) at `angle` (degrees, 0 is horizontal) and is `width` wide (0–1, in uv). Beyond it the blur ramps to full strength over `falloff` (0–1). `intensity` (0–100) is the blur at the far edges. Pixels inside the band stay pixel-sharp. `detail` adds the lens dials (see `VariableBlurDetailSlots`), both off at 0.
examples: ...tiltShift({intensity: p('intensity'), width: p('width'), falloff: p('falloff'), angle: p('angle'), center: p('center')})
effects.blurs.tiltShift.signature:
tiltShift(opts: {
    intensity: PropRef
    width: PropRef
    falloff: PropRef
    angle: PropRef
    center: PropRef
    detail?: VariableBlurDetailSlots
}): ComputeBackedEffect

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    intensity: PropRef
    width: PropRef
    falloff: PropRef
    angle: PropRef
    center: PropRef
    detail?: VariableBlurDetailSlots
}

effects.blurs.bloom.name: bloom
effects.blurs.bloom.summary: A glow: the child's bright parts spread into a soft halo that adds back on top.
effects.blurs.bloom.description: Pixels brighter than `threshold` (0–1) glow. `size` is the halo's spread in pixels (clean up to about 72). `intensity` (0–50) is how bright the halo is. The halo reaches past the child's alpha, so a glowing shape lights up transparent space around it. At size 0 nothing runs; give the size prop `recompile: crosses(0)`.
examples: ...bloom({intensity: p('intensity'), threshold: p('threshold'), size: p('size')})
effects.blurs.bloom.signature: bloom(opts: {intensity: PropRef; threshold: PropRef; size: PropRef}): ComputeBackedEffect

effects.blurs.childTap.name: childTap
effects.blurs.childTap.summary: The child's own color at this pixel, unchanged.
effects.blurs.childTap.description: The sampling stage for an effect that only adds something around the child, like a shadow.
examples: effect: gatherStack(childTap(), [shadowComposite({coverage, color: p('color'), intensity: p('intensity'), cutout: p('cutout')})])

effects.blurs.shadowOffset.name: shadowOffset
effects.blurs.shadowOffset.summary: The coordinate a shadow reads the child's silhouette from: `distance` away in the compass direction `angle`.
effects.blurs.shadowOffset.description: `angle` is in degrees, 0 up, 90 right, 180 down. `distance` (0–1) is a fraction of the canvas height and covers the same number of pixels in either axis. Pass the result as the `at` of `silhouetteCoverage`.
examples: silhouetteCoverage({at: shadowOffset({angle: p('angle'), distance: p('distance')}), blur: p('blur')})
effects.blurs.shadowOffset.signature: shadowOffset(opts: {angle: ArgSpec; distance: ArgSpec}): (params: RttFilterParams) => Expr

effects.blurs.silhouetteCoverage.name: silhouetteCoverage
effects.blurs.silhouetteCoverage.summary: A soft copy of the child's alpha silhouette: a number per pixel from 0 to 1.
effects.blurs.silhouetteCoverage.description: `at` is where to read the silhouette from, usually `shadowOffset`. `blur` is the softness as a radius in pixels (0–20). Feed it to `shadowComposite` as the `coverage`.
examples: silhouetteCoverage({at: shadowOffset({angle: 135, distance: 0.1}), blur: p('blur')})
effects.blurs.silhouetteCoverage.signature: silhouetteCoverage(opts: {at: (params: RttFilterParams) => Expr; blur: ArgSpec}): (params: RttFilterParams) => Expr

effects.blurs.shadowComposite.name: shadowComposite
effects.blurs.shadowComposite.summary: A tinted shadow behind the child.
effects.blurs.shadowComposite.description: `coverage` is the soft silhouette from `silhouetteCoverage`, tinted with `color` (a color prop) at `intensity` (0–1) and placed under the child. `cutout` is a boolean prop with `compileTime: true`; when true only the shadow shows, with the child's shape punched out of it.
examples: effect: gatherStack(childTap(), [shadowComposite({coverage: silhouetteCoverage({at: shadowOffset({angle: p('angle'), distance: p('distance')}), blur: p('blur')}), color: p('color'), intensity: p('intensity'), cutout: p('cutout')})])

params.name: opts

effects.blurs.fluteFrame.name: fluteFrame
effects.blurs.fluteFrame.summary: The geometry of fluted (reeded) glass over the child: where each pixel reads through the glass, how far its colors split, and the slope of the flute at that point.
effects.blurs.fluteFrame.description: `shape` is a `compileTime` prop whose transform maps 'bars', 'rounded' and 'waves' to 0, 1 and 2. `angle` is in degrees, 0 for vertical flutes. `frequency` is the number of flutes across the longer edge (1–20). `softness` (0–1) eases each flute from flat-with-sharp-seams to a gentle curve. `waveAmplitude` and `waveFrequency` shape the waves variant only. `refraction` (0–4) is how hard each flute bends the child. `aberration` (0–1) is the color split at the seams. The pattern drifts on the layer's clock, so declare `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}`. Keep the frame in a module constant and pass it to `refractedTaps` and `fluteHighlight`.
examples: const flute = fluteFrame({shape: p('shape'), angle: p('angle'), frequency: p('frequency'), softness: p('softness'), waveAmplitude: p('waveAmplitude'), waveFrequency: p('waveFrequency'), refraction: p('refraction'), aberration: p('aberration')})
effects.blurs.fluteFrame.signature:
fluteFrame(opts: {
    shape: PropRef
    angle: ArgSpec
    frequency: ArgSpec
    softness: ArgSpec
    waveAmplitude: ArgSpec
    waveFrequency: ArgSpec
    refraction: ArgSpec
    aberration: ArgSpec
}): GatherFrame

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    shape: PropRef
    angle: ArgSpec
    frequency: ArgSpec
    softness: ArgSpec
    waveAmplitude: ArgSpec
    waveFrequency: ArgSpec
    refraction: ArgSpec
    aberration: ArgSpec
}

effects.blurs.refractedTaps.name: refractedTaps
effects.blurs.refractedTaps.summary: The child seen through a flute frame, with edge handling and a color split when `aberration` is above 0.
effects.blurs.refractedTaps.description: `edges` is a prop with `transform: transformEdges` and `compileTime: true`. `aberration` is the same prop the frame uses; give it a recompile rule that fires when it crosses 0. Returns straight alpha, so close the stack with `{resultAlpha: 'straight'}`.
examples: effect: gatherStack(refractedTaps(flute, {aberration: p('aberration'), edges: p('edges')}), [fluteHighlight(flute, {lightAngle: 30, highlight: 0.2, softness: 0.3, color: p('highlightColor')})], {resultAlpha: 'straight'})
effects.blurs.refractedTaps.signature: refractedTaps(frame: GatherFrame, opts: {aberration: PropRef; edges: PropRef}): SampleStage

effects.blurs.fluteHighlight.name: fluteHighlight
effects.blurs.fluteHighlight.summary: A specular highlight running along each flute, added on top of the child's color.
effects.blurs.fluteHighlight.description: `lightAngle` is the light's direction in degrees, 0 head-on and 90 grazing (−90 to 90). `highlight` (0–2) is its strength. `softness` (0–1) spreads the peak from pin-tight to a broad sheen. `color` is a color prop. Transparent parts of the child pick up no highlight.
examples: fluteHighlight(flute, {lightAngle: p('lightAngle'), highlight: p('highlight'), softness: p('highlightSoftness'), color: p('highlightColor')})

params.name: opts

effects.blurs.peelFrame.name: peelFrame
effects.blurs.peelFrame.summary: The geometry of a page curling up from one corner: where the curl reads the child from, how far it has turned, and how far each pixel is from the crease.
effects.blurs.peelFrame.description: `corner` is a `compileTime` string prop ('top-left' | 'top-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-right') with no transform. `amount` (0–1) is how far the peel has progressed, 0 flat and 1 fully peeled. `radius` is the tightness of the curl as a fraction of the page diagonal (0.02–0.4). Keep the frame in a module constant and pass it to the peel shading words and `peelCompose`.
examples: const peel = peelFrame({corner: p('corner'), amount: p('amount'), radius: p('radius')})
tips: Leave the `corner` prop without a `transform`: it must stay a string for the frame to read.
effects.blurs.peelFrame.signature: peelFrame(opts: {corner: PropRef; amount: ArgSpec; radius: ArgSpec}): GatherFrame

effects.blurs.curlShading.name: curlShading
effects.blurs.curlShading.summary: The darkening in the crook of a curl, easing to full brightness at the lip.
effects.blurs.curlShading.description: `shading` (0–1) is how deep the darkening goes.
examples: curlShading(peel, {shading: p('shading')})

effects.blurs.curlSheen.name: curlSheen
effects.blurs.curlSheen.summary: The band of light running up a curl.
effects.blurs.curlSheen.description: `highlight` (0–1) is its strength. `softness` (0–1) runs from a tight gloss to a broad satin.
examples: curlSheen(peel, {highlight: p('highlight'), softness: p('highlightSoftness')})
effects.blurs.curlSheen.signature: curlSheen(frame: GatherFrame, opts: {highlight: ArgSpec; softness: ArgSpec}): PeelShade

effects.blurs.overhangShadow.name: overhangShadow
effects.blurs.overhangShadow.summary: The shadow a lifted curl casts on the flat page just past the crease.
effects.blurs.overhangShadow.description: `amount` is the same peel amount the frame uses. `shadow` (0–1) is the shadow's strength.
examples: overhangShadow(peel, {amount: p('amount'), shadow: p('shadow')})
effects.blurs.overhangShadow.signature: overhangShadow(frame: GatherFrame, opts: {amount: ArgSpec; shadow: ArgSpec}): PeelShade

effects.blurs.revealShadow.name: revealShadow
effects.blurs.revealShadow.summary: The shadow on the surface a peel reveals, just inside the crease.
effects.blurs.revealShadow.description: `amount` is the same peel amount the frame uses. `shadow` (0–1) is the shadow's strength.
examples: revealShadow(peel, {amount: p('amount'), shadow: p('shadow')})
effects.blurs.revealShadow.signature: revealShadow(frame: GatherFrame, opts: {amount: ArgSpec; shadow: ArgSpec}): PeelShade

effects.blurs.peelCompose.name: peelCompose
effects.blurs.peelCompose.summary: A finished page peel: the cast shadows, the flat page and the lit curl, layered back to front.
effects.blurs.peelCompose.description: The sampling stage of a peel. Pass the four shading terms built on the same frame. Wrap it in `gatherStack` with no overlays.
examples: effect: gatherStack(peelCompose(peel, {shade: curlShading(peel, {shading: 0.55}), sheen: curlSheen(peel, {highlight: 0.4, softness: 0.2}), overhang: overhangShadow(peel, {amount: p('amount'), shadow: 1}), reveal: revealShadow(peel, {amount: p('amount'), shadow: 1})}), [])

params.name: parts

effects.blurs.mirrorAcrossRow.name: mirrorAcrossRow
effects.blurs.mirrorAcrossRow.summary: The coordinate mirrored across a horizontal line, for reading a reflection below it.
effects.blurs.mirrorAcrossRow.description: `line` is a prop, 0–1 down the canvas in uv. Returns a function of the fragment params that gives the mirrored uv. Above the line the coordinate is still mirrored; `planarReflection` only shows the reflection below it.
examples: const reflectedUV = mirrorAcrossRow(p('height'))

effects.blurs.depthRampBlur.name: depthRampBlur
effects.blurs.depthRampBlur.summary: The blur half of a mirror floor: blurs the child more the further a row sits below the line.
effects.blurs.depthRampBlur.description: `line` is the same 0–1 line prop as `mirrorAcrossRow`. `blur` is the blur far below the line, 0–5 where 1 is a radius of about 12 pixels. `blurDistance` (in uv, 0.01–1) is how far below the line the blur takes to reach full strength. `halfKernel` is the number of taps each side per pass; 30 is a good value. Spread it into a definition with `species: 'custom'` and read the result in the fragment as `computeOutputs.blurredTexture`.
examples: ...depthRampBlur({line: p('height'), blur: p('blur'), blurDistance: p('blurDistance'), halfKernel: 30})
effects.blurs.depthRampBlur.signature: depthRampBlur(opts: {line: PropRef; blur: PropRef; blurDistance: PropRef; halfKernel: number}): {compute: GpuComputeNode}

params.name: opts
params.type: {line: PropRef; blur: PropRef; blurDistance: PropRef; halfKernel: number}

effects.blurs.planarReflection.name: planarReflection
effects.blurs.planarReflection.summary: A mirror floor: the child as it is above a line, and its reflection fading out below it.
effects.blurs.planarReflection.description: `line` (0–1 in uv), `distance` (how far below the line the reflection stays visible, in uv) and `falloff` (the width of the fade as a fraction of `distance`) are props. `edges` is a prop with `transform: transformEdges` and `compileTime: true`. `original` is the child's color at this pixel, `reflection` samples the child (or its blurred copy) at a coordinate, and `reflectedUV` is usually `mirrorAcrossRow(line)`. Returns a fragment function whose result is premultiplied; unpremultiply it before returning from `gpu.fragment`.
examples: planarReflection({line: p('height'), distance: p('distance'), falloff: p('falloff'), edges: p('edges')}, source.sample(ctx.uv), (uv) => blurred.sample(uv), mirrorAcrossRow(p('height')))(params)
effects.blurs.planarReflection.signature: planarReflection(opts: {line: PropRef; distance: PropRef; falloff: PropRef; edges: PropRef}, original: Expr, reflection: (uv: Expr) => Expr, reflectedUV: (params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr): (params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

params.name: opts
params.type: {line: PropRef; distance: PropRef; falloff: PropRef; edges: PropRef}

effects.blurs.screenedBloom.name: screenedBloom
effects.blurs.screenedBloom.summary: A tinted glow of the child's bright parts, screened over a color you have already graded: film halation, phosphor bloom.
effects.blurs.screenedBloom.description: `strength` is a prop; at 0 the glow pass does not run, so give it `recompile: crosses(0)`. `radius` is a prop for the glow's spread in pixels. `tint` is an rgb triple (0–1) and `threshold` (0–1) the brightness a pixel must pass to glow. `output` and `extractName` are names unique to your definition. Returns `compute`, to set as the definition's `compute:`, and `screen(base, at, params)`, which screens the glow at coordinate `at` over `base` in the fragment. The glow reaches past the child's alpha.
examples: const halation = screenedBloom({strength: p('halation'), radius: p('halationRadius'), tint: [1, 0.38, 0.16], threshold: 0.62, output: 'halationTexture', extractName: 'myHalationExtract'})
tips: Build it once at module level so the `compute:` field and the fragment read the same part.

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    strength: PropRef
    radius: PropRef
    tint: [number, number, number]
    threshold: number
    output: string
    extractName: string
}

effects.blurs.frameSway.name: frameSway
effects.blurs.frameSway.summary: A slight drifting shift and rotation of where the child is read from, like film in an unsteady projector gate.
effects.blurs.frameSway.description: `amount` is a prop from 0 to 1. `field` names an entry you declare in the definition's `extraFields` as `{schema: schema.f32, initial: 0}`; the sway's clock lives there. Returns a function of the fragment params that gives the uv to sample the child at. When `amount` drops to 0 the motion freezes in place rather than snapping back.
examples: const weave = frameSway({amount: p('weave'), field: 'weaveTime'})
tips: Build it once at module level and call it inside `gpu.fragment`; it registers its own per-frame clock.
effects.blurs.frameSway.signature: frameSway(slots: {amount: PropRef; field: string}): (params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr

effects.blurs.bokehDefocus.name: bokehDefocus
effects.blurs.bokehDefocus.summary: A photographic lens blur where bright highlights bloom into aperture-shaped discs.
effects.blurs.bokehDefocus.description: `radius` (0–100) is the defocus; 100 is a disc about 80 pixels across. `gain` (0–10) is how strongly highlights bloom and `threshold` (0–1) the brightness they must pass. `shape` is a string prop: 'blades' | 'circle' | 'star' | 'heart' | 'flower' | 'cross' | 'ring'. `blades` (0–9) counts blades or points for the blades, star and flower shapes; 0–2 is a round iris. `rotation` is in degrees and `fringe` (0–1) adds color fringing at the disc edges. `catEye` (0–1, optional) clips the discs into cat-eye shapes toward the frame corners, the way a lens barrel vignettes its aperture; 0 is off. Both color and coverage blur, so silhouettes soften like a real lens. Changing the aperture never recompiles. Spread it into a definition with `species: 'custom'`, `requiresRTT: true` and `requiresChild: true`.
examples: ...bokehDefocus({radius: p('radius'), gain: p('highlightGain'), threshold: p('highlightThreshold'), shape: p('bladeShape'), blades: p('bladeCount'), rotation: p('bladeRotation'), fringe: p('chromaticFringe')})

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    radius: PropRef
    gain: PropRef
    threshold: PropRef
    shape: PropRef
    blades: PropRef
    rotation: PropRef
    fringe: PropRef
    catEye?: PropRef
}

effects.stylize.bleedWarp.name: bleedWarp
effects.stylize.bleedWarp.summary: A sample position that drifts slowly past hard edges, so paint bleeds instead of stopping.
effects.stylize.bleedWarp.description: `amount` scales the drift in logical pixels (about four pixels per unit; 0 turns it off). Build it once and pass the same stage as `at` to both `kuwahara` and `wash`, so the brush and the original sample agree.
examples: const wet = bleedWarp({amount: p('bleed')})
tips: Give the `amount` prop `recompile: crosses(0)` so turning the bleed off removes the work.

effects.stylize.kuwahara.name: kuwahara
effects.stylize.kuwahara.summary: A painter's brush: the flattening that turns fine detail into soft patches of one color.
effects.stylize.kuwahara.description: `radius` is the brush size in logical pixels, 1 to 8, and must be a compile-time prop. `at` is the sample position, normally the same `bleedWarp` stage you hand to `wash`. Returns the brush for `wash`.
examples: brush: kuwahara({at: wet, radius: p('radius')})
tips: Mark `radius` `compileTime: true`. A hidden prop with a fixed default is the usual choice.

effects.stylize.paperGrain.name: paperGrain
effects.stylize.paperGrain.summary: Fine paper grain for the pigment to settle into, one brightness value per screen pixel.
effects.stylize.paperGrain.description: `amount` runs 0 to 1; at 0 the grain is left out entirely. Returns the stage for the `grain` slot of `wash`. Pass the same prop as `paper` there too.
examples: grain: paperGrain({amount: p('paper')})
tips: Give the `amount` prop `recompile: crosses(0)`.

effects.stylize.wash.name: wash
effects.stylize.wash.summary: The watercolor look: the layer inside flattened into soft patches of color over paper grain.
effects.stylize.wash.description: Closes the recipe and returns the effect for `effect:`. `strength` runs from 0 (the original) to 1 (the full wash). `paper` (0 to 1) sets how much grain shows and how far the result tints toward `paperColor`. `at`, `brush` and `grain` are the stages from `bleedWarp`, `kuwahara` and `paperGrain`.
examples: effect: wash({at: wet, brush: kuwahara({at: wet, radius: p('radius')}), grain: paperGrain({amount: p('paper')}), paper: p('paper'), paperColor: p('paperColor'), strength: p('strength')})
tips: `strength` at 0 skips the whole effect. Give the prop `recompile: crosses(0)`.
effects.stylize.wash.signature:
wash(slots: {
    at: GatherStage
    brush: KuwaharaBrush
    grain: GatherStage
    paper: PropRef
    paperColor: PropRef
    strength: PropRef
}): GatherEffect

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    at: GatherStage
    brush: KuwaharaBrush
    grain: GatherStage
    paper: PropRef
    paperColor: PropRef
    strength: PropRef
}

effects.stylize.sobelTaps.name: sobelTaps
effects.stylize.sobelTaps.summary: Eight brightness samples in a ring around each pixel, for finding edges.
effects.stylize.sobelTaps.description: `spacing` is the distance to the ring in device pixels (about 0.5 to 4; thicker strokes at larger values). Returns the ring for `chalkSketch`.
examples: edges: sobelTaps({spacing: p('edgeThickness')})

effects.stylize.chalkSketch.name: chalkSketch
effects.stylize.chalkSketch.summary: The chalk-drawing look: edges become chalk strokes and dark areas fill with cross-hatching.
effects.stylize.chalkSketch.description: Closes the recipe and returns the effect for `effect:`. `sensitivity` (0 to 1) sets how faint an edge still draws. `hatchScale` is the hatch line spacing in device pixels. `shading` (0 to 1) is how much cross-hatch fills the dark regions and `grain` (0 to 1) how dusty the strokes are. `board` and `chalk` are colors. Alpha follows the layer inside.
examples: effect: chalkSketch({edges: sobelTaps({spacing: p('edgeThickness')}), sensitivity: p('edgeSensitivity'), hatchScale: p('hatchScale'), shading: p('shading'), grain: p('grain'), board: p('boardColor'), chalk: p('chalkColor')})
effects.stylize.chalkSketch.signature:
chalkSketch(slots: {
    edges: SobelRing
    sensitivity: PropRef
    hatchScale: PropRef
    shading: PropRef
    grain: PropRef
    board: PropRef
    chalk: PropRef
}): GatherEffect

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    edges: SobelRing
    sensitivity: PropRef
    hatchScale: PropRef
    shading: PropRef
    grain: PropRef
    board: PropRef
    chalk: PropRef
}

effects.stylize.charGrid.name: charGrid
effects.stylize.charGrid.summary: The character grid: which cell each pixel falls in, and where it sits inside that cell.
effects.stylize.charGrid.description: `cellSize` is the cell size in pixels on a 1080-pixel-tall canvas; it scales with the canvas height. `spacing` is how much of the cell the character fills (1 fills it). Build it once and share it with `cellSample`, `glyphFor` and `glyphTint`.
examples: const grid = charGrid({cellSize: p('cellSize'), spacing: p('spacing')})

effects.stylize.cellSample.name: cellSample
effects.stylize.cellSample.summary: The color of the layer inside at the centre of each character cell.
effects.stylize.cellSample.description: One sample per cell, straight alpha. Feeds `glyphFor` (to pick the character) and `glyphTint` (to color it).
examples: const cell = cellSample({grid})

effects.stylize.glyphFor.name: glyphFor
effects.stylize.glyphFor.summary: The character drawn in each cell, picked by how bright the cell is.
effects.stylize.glyphFor.description: `gamma` bends the brightness curve: below 1 favours the light characters, above 1 the dark ones. `atlas` is your function that draws the character set into a texture and returns it (the Ascii shader shows one). The definition needs three extra fields the atlas fills in: `_charCount`, `_atlasScale` and `_atlasSize`.
examples: glyph: glyphFor({grid, cell, gamma: p('gamma'), atlas: setupGlyphAtlas})

params.name: slots

effects.stylize.glyphTint.name: glyphTint
effects.stylize.glyphTint.summary: The finished ASCII look: each character tinted with its cell's color, everything else transparent.
