effects.stylize.glyphTint.description: Returns the fragment for `gpu.fragment`. Cells whose alpha is below `alphaThreshold` (0 to 1) turn transparent. With `preserveAlpha` on, the output keeps the alpha of the layer inside; off, visible characters are fully opaque.
examples: gpu: {fragment: glyphTint({grid, cell, glyph, alphaThreshold: p('alphaThreshold'), preserveAlpha: p('preserveAlpha')})}
effects.stylize.glyphTint.signature:
glyphTint(slots: {
    grid: FragmentStage

    glyph: FragmentStage
    alphaThreshold: PropRef
    preserveAlpha: PropRef
}): FragmentStage

{
    grid: FragmentStage
    cell: FragmentStage
    glyph: FragmentStage
    alphaThreshold: PropRef
    preserveAlpha: PropRef
}

effects.stylize.linework.name: linework
effects.stylize.linework.summary: The engraving look: the layer inside redrawn as ink lines that swell where it is dark.
effects.stylize.linework.description: Closes the recipe and returns the effect for `effect:`. `style` is a compile-time select: `'line'` (one set of parallel lines), `'crosshatch'` (more sets appear in the shadows) or `'spiral'` (one line coiling out from `center`, a position prop). `frequency` is how many lines span the canvas height. `angle` is in degrees. `relief` (0 to 2) is how far brightness pushes the lines sideways, `waviness` (0 to 1) how much they meander, and `contrast` (0.25 to 3) the tone curve before inking. `ink` and `paper` are colors.
examples: effect: linework({style: p('style'), frequency: p('frequency'), angle: p('angle'), center: p('center'), relief: p('relief'), waviness: p('waviness'), contrast: p('contrast'), ink: p('inkColor'), paper: p('paperColor')})
tips: Set `blendWithChildren: false` on the definition. The lines replace the layer rather than sit on it.

    style: PropRef
    frequency: PropRef
    angle: PropRef

    waviness: PropRef
    contrast: PropRef
    ink: PropRef
    paper: PropRef
}): GatherEffect

{

    frequency: PropRef
    angle: PropRef

    paper: PropRef
}

effects.lens.chromaticFan.name: chromaticFan
effects.lens.chromaticFan.summary: Split the child into red, green and blue copies pushed apart along one direction.
effects.lens.chromaticFan.description: `angle` is in degrees (0 pushes along x); give the prop `transform: transformAngle`. `strength` is 0–1, where 1 moves a channel by a tenth of the canvas height. `red`, `green` and `blue` multiply that shift per channel, usually −1, 0 and 1. Returns a sampling stage; wrap it in `gatherStack` to make the effect.
examples: effect: gatherStack(chromaticFan({strength: p('strength'), angle: p('angle'), red: p('redOffset'), green: p('greenOffset'), blue: p('blueOffset')}), [])
tips: Alpha comes from the green copy, so keep `green` at 0 to hold the layer's outline in place.
effects.lens.chromaticFan.signature:
chromaticFan(opts: {
    strength: ArgSpec
    angle: ArgSpec
    red: ArgSpec
    green: ArgSpec
    blue: ArgSpec
}): SampleStage

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    strength: ArgSpec
    angle: ArgSpec
    red: ArgSpec
    green: ArgSpec
    blue: ArgSpec
}

effects.lens.spectralLens.name: spectralLens
effects.lens.spectralLens.summary: Fan the child out into many color-shifted copies through a warped lens, the spectral-lens look.
effects.lens.spectralLens.description: A whole fragment for a `gpu:` definition; the child is read as a texture. `count` copies spread along `angle` around `center`, `dispersion` colors them across the spectrum, the focus slots fade the split near the center and the edges, `lensBulge` and `lensCircle` warp the whole image, and `swirl`, `noise` and the grain slots scatter it. Every slot is a prop ref; the field list on `SpectralLensSlots` gives units and ranges.
examples: gpu: {fragment: spectralLens({center: p('center'), spread: p('spread'), bias: p('bias'), angle: p('angle'), perspective: p('perspective'), count: p('count'), dispersion: p('dispersion'), dispersionShift: p('dispersionShift'), dispersionColor: p('dispersionColor'), focusCenter: p('focusCenter'), focusEdges: p('focusEdges'), swirl: p('swirl'), noise: p('noise'), noiseFrequency: p('noiseFrequency'), noiseOffset: p('noiseOffset'), lensBulge: p('lensBulge'), lensCircle: p('lensCircle'), grainMixer: p('grainMixer'), grainOverlay: p('grainOverlay')})}
tips: Every pixel samples the child `count` times, and phones cap `count` at 24. Keep it low on large canvases.

effects.reveal.Coverage.name: Coverage
effects.reveal.Coverage.summary: The order pixels disappear in: a number per pixel from 0 (goes first) to 1 (goes last).
effects.reveal.Coverage.description: Get one from a `coverage` word, then reshape it with the methods below. Each method returns a new coverage, so they chain. Pass the result to `reveal`.
examples: coverage: coverage.directional(p('angle')).folded()

effects.reveal.BandedCoverage.name: BandedCoverage
effects.reveal.BandedCoverage.description: Bands vanish in order, or in a fixed random order after `.shuffled()`.
examples: coverage: coverage.radial(p('center')).bands(p('rings'))

effects.reveal.CellCoverage.name: CellCoverage
effects.reveal.CellCoverage.summary: The canvas cut into a grid of square cells, waiting for you to pick the order the cells go in.
effects.reveal.CellCoverage.description: Not a coverage on its own. Call `.diamond()`, `.checker()` or `.shuffled()` to get one.
examples: coverage: coverage.cells(p('blockSize')).shuffled()

effects.reveal.coverage.directional.name: directional
effects.reveal.coverage.directional.summary: A straight edge sweeping across the canvas.
effects.reveal.coverage.directional.description: `angleDeg` is in degrees; 0 wipes left to right, 90 top to bottom. The edge reaches both ends of the canvas exactly at whatever angle you give.
examples: coverage: coverage.directional(p('angle'))

effects.reveal.coverage.radial.name: radial
effects.reveal.coverage.radial.summary: A circle growing out from `center`, an iris wipe.
effects.reveal.coverage.radial.description: `center` is a position prop (`transform: transformPosition`). The circle is sized to the farthest corner, so it clears the whole canvas even from an off-center start.
examples: coverage: coverage.radial(p('center'))

effects.reveal.coverage.angular.name: angular
effects.reveal.coverage.angular.description: `startDeg` is where the sweep begins, in degrees. `direction` is `'cw'`, `'ccw'` or `'both'` (two hands opening from the start and meeting opposite it), either as a literal or as a select prop declared `compileTime: true`.
examples: coverage: coverage.angular(p('center'), p('startAngle'), p('direction'))
effects.reveal.coverage.angular.signature: coverage.angular(center: ArgSpec, startDeg: ArgSpec, direction: PropRef | AngularDirection): Coverage

effects.reveal.coverage.cells.name: cells
effects.reveal.coverage.cells.summary: A grid of square cells `size` wide.
effects.reveal.coverage.cells.description: `size` is a fraction of the canvas width (0.01–0.5). Finish with `.diamond()`, `.checker()` or `.shuffled()` to say how the cells go.
examples: coverage: coverage.cells(p('blockSize')).checker()

effects.reveal.coverage.noise.name: noise
effects.reveal.coverage.noise.summary: Soft blobs eating the image away, the classic film dissolve.
effects.reveal.coverage.noise.description: `scale` sets the blob size (0.5–20; higher is smaller blobs). `seed` picks a different pattern. The pattern itself never moves; only `progress` does.
examples: coverage: coverage.noise(p('scale'), p('seed'))

effects.reveal.coverage.name: coverage
effects.reveal.coverage.summary: The orders a wipe can follow.
effects.reveal.coverage.description:
Each word returns a `Coverage` for `reveal`.

All of them read the canvas in uv (0–1 across, y down) and correct for its aspect ratio, so a circle stays round and a diagonal stays at its true angle.
examples: coverage: coverage.radial(p('center'))
effects.reveal.coverage.signature: coverage: { directional, radial, angular, cells, noise }

effects.reveal.reveal.name: reveal
effects.reveal.reveal.summary: Fade the child away in coverage order as `progress` goes from 0 to 1.
effects.reveal.reveal.description: At 0 the child is fully visible, at 1 it is gone, whatever `feather` is. Only the child's alpha changes; its colors stay put. Turning `invert` on reverses the order, so the last pixels go first.
examples: effect: reveal({coverage: coverage.directional(p('angle')), progress: p('progress'), feather: p('feather'), invert: p('invert')})
tips: Animate `progress` from outside (a prop driven by scroll or a tween); the wipe itself has no clock.

effects.instances.grid.name: grid
effects.instances.grid.summary: Copies in rows and columns, filling this layer's bounding box.
effects.instances.grid.description: Pass it as the recipe's `placement`, or as one member of `byMode`.
examples: placement: grid({columns: p('columns'), rows: p('rows'), gapX: p('gapX'), gapY: p('gapY'), stagger: p('stagger'), flip: p('flip')})
tips: Mark `flip` `compileTime: true`. Only the chosen mirroring is compiled in.

effects.instances.radial.name: radial
effects.instances.radial.summary: Copies around a circle centred on the layer inside.
effects.instances.radial.description: `sweep` at 360 spaces them evenly all the way round; smaller sweeps make an arc starting at `startAngle`.
examples: placement: radial({count: p('count'), radius: p('radius'), startAngle: p('startAngle'), sweep: p('sweep'), faceCenter: p('faceCenter')})

effects.instances.line.name: line
effects.instances.line.summary: Copies in a row, marching away from the layer inside in one direction.
examples: placement: line({count: p('count'), direction: p('direction'), spacing: p('spacing')})

effects.instances.byMode.name: byMode
effects.instances.byMode.summary: Lets one select prop switch between a grid, a radial and a linear layout.
effects.instances.byMode.description: `mode` is a compile-time select with the values `'grid'`, `'radial'` and `'linear'`; only the chosen layout is compiled in.
examples: placement: byMode(p('mode'), {grid: grid({...}), radial: radial({...}), linear: line({...})})

effects.instances.repeatInstances.name: repeatInstances
effects.instances.repeatInstances.summary: Many copies of the layer inside, laid out and varied as the recipe says.
effects.instances.repeatInstances.description: Returns the fragment for `gpu.fragment` on a definition with `requiresRTT`, `requiresChild` and `wantsBoundsParams` set. Copies stack with normal alpha in the recipe's `order`. The result is straight alpha.
examples: gpu: {fragment: repeatInstances({source: {crop: {left: p('cropLeft'), right: p('cropRight'), top: p('cropTop'), bottom: p('cropBottom')}}, placement: radial({count: p('count'), radius: p('radius'), startAngle: p('startAngle'), sweep: p('sweep'), faceCenter: p('faceCenter')}), variation: {scale: p('instanceScale'), rotation: p('instanceRotation'), opacity: p('instanceOpacity'), jitter: {position: p('jitterPosition'), rotation: p('jitterRotation'), scale: p('jitterScale'), opacity: p('jitterOpacity')}, seed: p('seed'), phase: p('phase')}, hueShift: p('hueShift'), order: p('zOrder')})}
tips: `hueShift` costs nothing at 0. Give the prop `recompile: crosses(0)` so it switches on cleanly.

effects.fracture.cellLaneUVFor.name: cellLaneUVFor
effects.fracture.cellLaneUVFor.summary: Where one shard's value sits in a one-row data texture.
effects.fracture.cellLaneUVFor.description: Lay the texture out as four values per shard, so `laneWidth` is the shard count times four. The returned GPU function takes a shard index and a value index (0 to 3) and gives the uv to sample with `'nearestClamp'`. Built once per width.
examples:
const cellLaneUV = cellLaneUVFor(16 * 4)
const dataAt = (idx: Expr, field: number) => dataKit.sample(call(cellLaneUV, 'cellLaneUV', [idx, floatE(field)]), 'nearestClamp').member('r')
effects.fracture.cellLaneUVFor.signature: cellLaneUVFor(laneWidth: number): TgpuFn<(idx: F32, field: F32) => Vec2f>

effects.fracture.crackGeom.name: crackGeom
effects.fracture.crackGeom.summary: How much crack there is at a pixel, and which way the shard under it has moved.
effects.fracture.crackGeom.description: Takes the pixel's uv, the nearest and second-nearest shard positions (x and y, in uv), the nearest shard's displacement (x and y, in uv) and `crackWidth` (about 0.5 to 5). Returns a record with `crackIntensity` (0 to 1, and 0 until the shard has actually moved), `edgeNormal` (the direction across the crack), `displacedUV` (where to sample the layer inside) and `disp` (the displacement again, for `crackShardCompose`).
examples: const geom = call(crackGeom, 'crackGeom', [ctx.uv, dataAt(nearest, 0), dataAt(nearest, 1), dataAt(second, 0), dataAt(second, 1), dataAt(nearest, 2), dataAt(nearest, 3), uniforms.crackWidth])
effects.fracture.crackGeom.signature: crackGeom(uv: v2f, nPosX: number, nPosY: number, sPosX: number, sPosY: number, dispX: number, dispY: number, crackWidth: number): { crackIntensity: number; edgeNormal: v2f; displacedUV: v2f; disp: v2f; }

params.name: args
params.type: [uv: v2f, nPosX: number, nPosY: number, sPosX: number, sPosY: number, dispX: number, dispY: number, crackWidth: number]

effects.fracture.crackRefractUV.name: crackRefractUV
effects.fracture.crackRefractUV.summary: Where to sample one color channel so the crack bends the light and splits it like a prism.
effects.fracture.crackRefractUV.description: `channel` is 1 for red, 0 for green and -1 for blue; the three samples land slightly apart. `refractionStrength` (0 to 10) bends the sample across the crack and `chromaticSplit` (0 to 5) spreads the channels. Both fade with `crackIntensity`, so unbroken glass is untouched.
examples: const red = child.sample(call(crackRefractUV, 'crackRefractUV', [geom.member('displacedUV'), geom.member('edgeNormal'), geom.member('crackIntensity'), uniforms.refractionStrength, uniforms.chromaticSplit, floatE(1)]))
effects.fracture.crackRefractUV.signature: crackRefractUV(displacedUV: v2f, edgeNormal: v2f, crackIntensity: number, refractionStrength: number, chromaticSplit: number, channel: number): v2f

params.name: args
params.type: [displacedUV: v2f, edgeNormal: v2f, crackIntensity: number, refractionStrength: number, chromaticSplit: number, channel: number]

effects.fracture.crackShardCompose.name: crackShardCompose
effects.fracture.crackShardCompose.summary: The finished glass: the three refracted channels blended into the crack, with a hint of light on tilted shards.
effects.fracture.crackShardCompose.description: Pass the plain sample at `displacedUV`, the red, green and blue samples from `crackRefractUV`, then `crackIntensity` and `disp` from `crackGeom`, and `shardLighting` (0 to 0.5). The samples come from the layer's texture, so unpremultiply the result before returning it.
examples: const glass = call(crackShardCompose, 'crackShardCompose', [plain, red, green, blue, geom.member('crackIntensity'), geom.member('disp'), uniforms.shardLighting])
effects.fracture.crackShardCompose.signature: crackShardCompose(normalColor: v4f, rFinal: v4f, gFinal: v4f, bFinal: v4f, crackIntensity: number, disp: v2f, shardLighting: number): v4f

params.name: args
params.type: [normalColor: v4f, rFinal: v4f, gFinal: v4f, bFinal: v4f, crackIntensity: number, disp: v2f, shardLighting: number]

effects.fracture.voronoiRegionField.name: voronoiRegionField
effects.fracture.voronoiRegionField.summary: Splits the canvas into shards around random sites and records, per pixel, its shard and the next-nearest one.
effects.fracture.voronoiRegionField.description: A compute hook for the `compute:` field. `count` is the number of shards, `size` the field's resolution in pixels, `sites(seed)` your function returning the shard positions as `[x, y, x, y, …]` in uv, and `seedProp` the prop that re-rolls them. The field only recomputes when the seed changes. In the fragment, sample `computeOutputs[output]` with `'nearestClamp'`: `.r` is the nearest shard's index, `.g` the second-nearest.
examples: compute: voronoiRegionField({count: 16, size: 1024, sites: shardSites, seedProp: 'seed', seedDefault: 2, output: 'voronoiField'})
tips: Fill your shard data texture from the same `sites` function, or the cracks drift off their shards.
effects.fracture.voronoiRegionField.signature:
voronoiRegionField(opts: {
    count: number
    size: number
    sites: (seed: number) => Float32Array
    seedProp: string
    seedDefault: number
    output: string
}): GpuComputeNode

params.name: opts
params.type:
{
    count: number
    size: number
    sites: (seed: number) => Float32Array
    seedProp: string
    seedDefault: number
    output: string

effects.edgeGlow.heartbeatPulse.name: heartbeatPulse
effects.edgeGlow.heartbeatPulse.summary: A double heartbeat, 0 to 1, driven by the layer's clock.
effects.edgeGlow.heartbeatPulse.description: Compute it once per pixel and hand the same value to `edgeGlowBand` and every `orbitSpotsAccum` call, so the band's smoke and the spots beat together.
examples: const beat = asLocal(call(heartbeatPulse, 'heartbeatPulse', [animatedTime(params)]), 'beat')

effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowBand.name: edgeGlowBand
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowBand.summary: The glowing band around the shape's edge, with drifting smoke, plus the angle around the shape.
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowBand.description: Takes the shape's signed distance (`frame.surf0.member('r')`), the shape-space uv (`frame.sdfUV`), the viewport size, the `scale` prop, `thickness` (0.01 to 1; 1 is about as wide as the default shape), `softness` (0 is a crisp ring, 1 a wide gradient), `smokeSize` and `smokeAmt` (0 to 1), the layer's clock, `pulse` (0 to 1) and the shared `beat`. Returns `.x` the band (0 to 1) and `.y` the angle around the shape in turns (0 to 1), which `orbitSpotsAccum` needs.
examples: const band = call(edgeGlowBand, 'edgeGlowBand', [frame.surf0!.member('r'), frame.sdfUV!, params.ctx.viewportSize, uniforms.scale, uniforms.thickness, uniforms.softness, uniforms.smokeSize, uniforms.smoke, t, uniforms.pulse, beat])

params.name: args
params.type: [fieldRaw: number, sdfUV: v2f, viewport: v2f, scale: number, thickness: number, softness: number, smokeSize: number, smokeAmt: number, animTime: number, pulse: number, beat: number]

effects.edgeGlow.orbitSpotsAccum.name: orbitSpotsAccum
effects.edgeGlow.orbitSpotsAccum.summary: The spots of one color orbiting the band, as coverage at this pixel.
effects.edgeGlow.orbitSpotsAccum.description: Call it once per color. Takes the angle and band from `edgeGlowBand`, the layer's clock, the shared `beat`, `spots` (1 to 5 per color), `spotSize` (0 to 1), `pulse` (0 to 1), `intensity` (0 to 1), `softness`, `seed` and the color's index. Returns a pair for `edgeGlowAccumColorFor`: `.x` the layered coverage and `.y` the additive sum used for bloom.
examples: const sectors = call(orbitSpotsAccum, 'orbitSpotsAccum', [band.member('y'), band.member('x'), t, beat, uniforms.spots, uniforms.spotSize, uniforms.pulse, uniforms.intensity, uniforms.softness, uniforms.seed, floatE(colorIndex)])
effects.edgeGlow.orbitSpotsAccum.signature: orbitSpotsAccum(angle01: number, border: number, animTime: number, beat: number, spotsF: number, spotSize: number, pulse: number, intensity: number, softness: number, seed: number, colorIdxF: number): v2f

params.name: args
params.type: [angle01: number, border: number, animTime: number, beat: number, spotsF: number, spotSize: number, pulse: number, intensity: number, softness: number, seed: number, colorIdxF: number]

effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumZero.name: edgeGlowAccumZero
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumZero.summary: The empty state to start folding colors into.
examples: let state = call(edgeGlowAccumZero, 'edgeGlowAccumZero', [])
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumZero.signature: edgeGlowAccumZero(): { rgb: v3f; w: number; ba: number; ac: v3f; aa: number; }

effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumColorFor.name: edgeGlowAccumColorFor
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumColorFor.summary: The fold step for one color space: adds one color's spots to the running state.
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumColorFor.description: `mode` is the compile-time value of a `colorSpace` prop (see `transformColorSpace`); where colors overlap they mix in that space. The returned GPU function takes the state, a color and the pair from `orbitSpotsAccum`, and returns the new state. Call it once per color, then close with `edgeGlowCompose`.
examples:
const accumColor = edgeGlowAccumColorFor(propValues.colorSpace as number)
state = call(accumColor, 'edgeGlowAccumColor', [state, uniforms.colorA, sectors])
tips: OKLCh keeps overlapping lights vivid; linear RGB muddies them.
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowAccumColorFor.signature: edgeGlowAccumColorFor(mode: number): TgpuFn<(st: WgslStruct<{ rgb: Vec3f; w: F32; ba: F32; ac: Vec3f; aa: F32; }>, color: Vec4f, sectors: Vec2f) => WgslStruct<{ rgb: Vec3f; w: F32; ba: F32; ac: Vec3f; aa: F32; }>>

effects.edgeGlow.colorAtIndex.name: colorAtIndex
effects.edgeGlow.colorAtIndex.summary: One color from a `stops` prop, by index.
effects.edgeGlow.colorAtIndex.description: Reads the packed stops array (`uniforms.colorsArray` when the definition uses `colorStopsPropConfig`). Stop positions are ignored; the stops are a list of orbit colors.
examples: const color = call(colorAtIndex, 'colorAtIndex', [uniforms.colorsArray, floatE(i)])

effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowCompose.name: edgeGlowCompose
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowCompose.summary: The final color from the folded state, over a transparent background.
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowCompose.description: `bloom` (0 to 1) sets how additively overlapping lights pile up; high values overdrive to white. Returns straight alpha, ready to return from the surface function.
examples: return call(edgeGlowCompose, 'edgeGlowCompose', [state, uniforms.bloom])
effects.edgeGlow.edgeGlowCompose.signature: edgeGlowCompose(st: { rgb: v3f; w: number; ba: number; ac: v3f; aa: number; }, bloom: number): v4f

params.type: [st: { rgb: v3f; w: number; ba: number; ac: v3f; aa: number; }, bloom: number]

effects.overlay.detectionOverlay.name: detectionOverlay
effects.overlay.detectionOverlay.summary: Draw computer-vision style detection boxes over whatever the child contains.
effects.overlay.detectionOverlay.description: A whole fragment for a `gpu:` definition. The canvas is cut into cells (`layout`, `cellSize`, `maxDepth`); each cell that holds content of the chosen kind (`detectionMode` above `threshold`) gets a box drawn tight around that content, with an optional label showing its size or coverage. The child shows through underneath. Every slot is a prop ref; the field list on `DetectionOverlaySlots` gives units and options.
examples: gpu: {fragment: detectionOverlay({detectionMode: p('detectionMode'), threshold: p('threshold'), layout: p('layout'), cellSize: p('cellSize'), maxDepth: p('maxDepth'), boxStyle: p('boxStyle'), lineWidth: p('lineWidth'), cornerRadius: p('cornerRadius'), strokeColor: p('strokeColor'), fillColor: p('fillColor'), labelColor: p('labelColor'), labelBackgroundColor: p('labelBackgroundColor'), labelMode: p('labelMode'), labelPosition: p('labelPosition'), labelInset: p('labelInset'), labelRadius: p('labelRadius'), fontFamily: p('fontFamily'), fontWeight: p('fontWeight'), fontSize: p('fontSize'), letterSpacing: p('letterSpacing')})}
tips: Cost grows with `maxDepth`; 2 is plenty for most layouts. Set `labelMode` to `'none'` to skip the text pass entirely.

effects.overlay.motionTrackerHud.name: motionTrackerHud
effects.overlay.motionTrackerHud.summary: Draw motion-tracker gizmos that chase content across the child, leaving keyframe trails.
effects.overlay.motionTrackerHud.description: A whole fragment for a `gpu:` definition. It only draws; the trackers themselves come from the tracker pursuit simulation, which the same definition must run as its `compute:` pass (`trackerSim.createTrackerPursuitSim` from the kit, as the KeyFrames shader does). Without that pass the child passes through untouched. Every slot is a prop ref; the field list on `MotionTrackerHudSlots` gives units.
examples: gpu: {fragment: motionTrackerHud({trackers: p('trackers'), trail: p('trail'), markerSize: p('markerSize'), lineWidth: p('lineWidth'), markerColor: p('markerColor'), keyframeColor: p('keyframeColor'), pathColor: p('pathColor')})}
tips: Copy the KeyFrames shader as a whole; the compute pass and this fragment share the `trackers` prop and the detection props.

effects.pointerFields.SPLAT_MIN_GRID.name: SPLAT_MIN_GRID
effects.pointerFields.SPLAT_MIN_GRID.summary: The smallest grid `pointerSplatField` runs on: 8 cells per side.

effects.pointerFields.SPLAT_MAX_GRID.name: SPLAT_MAX_GRID
effects.pointerFields.SPLAT_MAX_GRID.summary: The largest grid `pointerSplatField` runs on: 128 cells per side.

effects.pointerFields.clampSplatGridSize.name: clampSplatGridSize
effects.pointerFields.clampSplatGridSize.summary: The grid size `pointerSplatField` really uses for a prop value: floored, then held to 8–128.
effects.pointerFields.clampSplatGridSize.description: Use it in the `gridSize` prop's recompile rule, so the simulation rebuilds only when the cell count changes and not on every drag of the slider.
examples: gridSize: {default: 20, recompile: recompileWhen((prev, next) => clampSplatGridSize(prev as number) !== clampSplatGridSize(next as number))}

effects.pointerFields.pointerSplatField.name: pointerSplatField
effects.pointerFields.pointerSplatField.summary: A field the cursor smears: cells near the pointer move with it, then fade back to rest.
effects.pointerFields.pointerSplatField.description: Spread it with `...sim.grids.gridSim(...)`. `gridSize` is the cells per side (8 to 128, see `clampSplatGridSize`). `decay` (about 0 to 10) is how fast the smear fades; `intensity` (about 0 to 5) how hard the cursor pushes; `radius` the brush size (1 is about 5% of the canvas). The field is published under `output` for a warp map such as `warps.gridCellDisplace`.
examples: ...sim.grids.gridSim(pointerSplatField({gridSize: p('gridSize'), decay: p('decay'), intensity: p('intensity'), radius: p('radius'), output: 'displacement'}))
tips: Add `uvRemapIdentityWhen: ({computeOutputs}) => !computeOutputs?.displacement` so the warp is a no-op before the field exists.
effects.pointerFields.pointerSplatField.signature:
pointerSplatField(slots: {
    gridSize: PropRef
    decay: PropRef
    intensity: PropRef
    radius: PropRef
    output: string
}): (params: GpuFragmentParams, root: GridRoot) => GridSimConfig

params.name: slots
params.type:
{
    gridSize: PropRef
    decay: PropRef
    intensity: PropRef
    radius: PropRef
    output: string
}

effects.pointerFields.springLatticeField.name: springLatticeField
effects.pointerFields.springLatticeField.summary: A cloth of springs the cursor pushes: it stretches, rings and settles like fabric.
effects.pointerFields.springLatticeField.description: Spread it with `...sim.grids.gridSim(...)`. `stiffness` (about 1 to 30) is how rigid the cloth is; `damping` (about 0 to 10) how quickly it stops moving; `radius` the push area (1 is about 8% of the canvas). The grid is fixed at 64 cells per side. The field is published under `output` for a warp map such as `warps.liquidDisplace`.
examples: ...sim.grids.gridSim(springLatticeField({stiffness: p('stiffness'), damping: p('damping'), radius: p('radius'), output: 'displacement'}))
tips: Add `uvRemapIdentityWhen: ({computeOutputs}) => !computeOutputs?.displacement` so the warp is a no-op before the field exists.

params.name: slots

simulate.op.wave.name: wave
simulate.op.wave.summary: A wave step: the grid ripples outward from any disturbance and fades by `damping` (a prop, 0–20).
examples: op.wave({damping: p('decay')})
tips: Declare `history: 2` on the grid. A wave needs the two previous frames.

simulate.op.splat.name: splat
simulate.op.splat.summary: A brush step: a soft round push into the grid at the pointer, scaled by how fast it moves.
simulate.op.splat.description: `radius` is a prop on a 0.1–1 scale.
examples: op.splat({at: pointer({teleportGuard: 'on'}), amount: pointerSpeed({max: 2}), radius: p('radius')})
tips: Use `pointer({teleportGuard: 'on'})`. The pointer entering the canvas is then not a stroke.
simulate.op.splat.signature: op.splat(config: {at: PointerSignal; amount: PointerSpeedSignal; radius: PropRef}): SplatOp

simulate.op.gradient.name: gradient
simulate.op.gradient.summary: A derived output: the grid's slope at every cell as a 2D vector, ready for `displaceBy`.
examples: derive: {displacement: op.gradient()}

simulate.op.name: op
simulate.op.summary: The steps and outputs a grid simulation is built from.
simulate.op.description: `op.wave` and `op.splat` go in `step` and run in order once per frame. `op.gradient` goes in `derive`, named, and becomes an output an effect can read with `sim.output('name')`.
examples:
step: [op.wave({damping: p('decay')}), op.splat({at: pointer({teleportGuard: 'on'}), amount: pointerSpeed({max: 2}), radius: p('radius')})],
derive: {displacement: op.gradient()},
tips: The current engine implements exactly `[op.wave, op.splat]` with `op.gradient` derived. Other combinations throw at definition time.

simulate.GridSim.name: GridSim
simulate.GridSim.description: Read its outputs with `output('name')` and pass them to an effect.
examples: effect: displaceBy(waves.output('displacement'), {strength: p('intensity'), chromatic: p('chromaticSplit'), edges: p('edges')})
tips: Asking for an output that was not declared in `derive` throws with the list of names that were.

simulate.simulate.grid.name: grid
simulate.simulate.grid.summary: A square grid of numbers advanced once per frame by `step`, with named outputs in `derive`.
examples: const waves = simulate.grid({resolution: 128, history: 2, step: [op.wave({damping: p('decay')}), op.splat({at: pointer({teleportGuard: 'on'}), amount: pointerSpeed({max: 2}), radius: p('radius')})], derive: {displacement: op.gradient()}})

simulate.simulate.name: simulate
simulate.simulate.summary: Declare a simulation the engine runs for you.
simulate.simulate.description:
`simulate.grid` gives a square grid of numbers advanced once per frame by the steps you list.

Declare it once at module scope, then read its outputs inside the definition. The engine allocates the state, keeps the history, tracks the pointer and sleeps the simulation once it has settled.
examples: const waves = simulate.grid({resolution: 128, history: 2, step: [op.wave({damping: p('decay')}), op.splat({at: pointer({teleportGuard: 'on'}), amount: pointerSpeed({max: 2}), radius: p('radius')})], derive: {displacement: op.gradient()}, rest: {settlesWhen: 'derived-from-damping'}})
tips: Reach for `sim.grids`, `sim.fluids`, `sim.feedback` or `sim.agents` only when the effect needs its own GPU step. If a wave field and a displacement say it, stay here.

sim.grids.gridSim.name: gridSim
sim.grids.gridSim.summary: A field of cells advanced every frame by an ordered list of stages.
sim.grids.gridSim.description:
Spread it into a definition next to a `gpu.fragment` that samples one of its outputs.

The build callback runs once per instance of the layer, with the GPU device, and returns the outputs, the frame-delta clamp and the stages. Return null to run nothing (a required child is missing). Without a GPU the fragment should fall back to the child or to transparent.
examples: ...gridSim((params, root) => ({outputs: {state}, clampDt: 0.05, stages: [op.values('write', (f) => paramsU.write({dt: f.dt, radius: f.num('radius', 0.4)})), op.pass(update), op.publish(() => output)]}))
tips: Everything created in the build callback (buffers, passes, trackers) belongs to that layer instance. Create nothing at module scope that holds per-frame state.
sim.grids.gridSim.signature: gridSim(build: (params: GpuFragmentParams, root: GridRoot) => GridSimConfig | null): {compute: GpuComputeNode}

sim.grids.op.host.name: host
sim.grids.op.host.summary: A named step that runs before any gate: pointer smoothing, activity flags, anything a later `settle` needs to know.
examples: op.host('cursor', (f) => { active = (f.frameParams.pointer?.x ?? 0.5) !== lastX })
sim.grids.op.host.signature: op.host(name: string, run: (f: GridFrame) => void): GridStage

sim.grids.op.values.name: values
sim.grids.op.values.summary: A named step that writes this frame's values for the passes after it.
examples: op.values('write', (f) => paramsU.write({dt: f.dt, radius: f.num('radius', 0.4)}))
tips: Read props here with `f.num('prop', fallback)` so a prop that is briefly not a number cannot reach the GPU as `undefined`.
sim.grids.op.values.signature: op.values(name: string, run: (f: GridFrame) => void): GridStage

sim.grids.op.settle.name: settle
sim.grids.op.settle.summary: Sleep the simulation once nothing has driven it for `settleMs` of simulated time.
sim.grids.op.settle.description:
Frames are skipped and the last published texture stays on screen, so a still field costs nothing.

`activeWhen` says whether something drove the field this frame. `settleMs` is how long the field takes to fade after the last activity, in milliseconds.
examples: op.settle({activeWhen: () => moving, settleMs: (f) => 4000 / Math.max(f.num('decay', 1), 0.1)})
tips: Simulated time, not wall-clock: a hidden tab does not count, so the field is still fading when the user comes back.
sim.grids.op.settle.signature: op.settle(opts: {activeWhen: (f: GridFrame) => boolean; settleMs: (f: GridFrame) => number}): GridStage

sim.grids.op.readyWhen.name: readyWhen
sim.grids.op.readyWhen.summary: Run nothing until `fn` returns true, typically once the child's picture has arrived through `bindInputs`.
examples: op.readyWhen(() => lumaReady)

sim.grids.op.pass.name: pass
sim.grids.op.pass.summary: One GPU pass, the same every frame.
examples: op.pass(update)

sim.grids.op.cache.name: cache
sim.grids.op.cache.summary: A GPU pass chosen per frame, for a pass whose input is rebound after the frame starts.
examples: op.cache(() => lumaPipeline)

sim.grids.op.publish.name: publish
sim.grids.op.publish.summary: The last stage: write the state into the texture the layer samples.
sim.grids.op.publish.description: Chosen per frame so it can follow whichever buffer holds the current result.
examples: op.publish(() => outputPass.with(sort.side() === 'A' ? outputBgA : outputBgB))

sim.grids.op.seedOnce.name: seedOnce
sim.grids.op.seedOnce.summary: A one-shot reset run before the rest of the frame whenever `staleWhen` says the state is stale: on the first frame, or when a seed prop changes.
examples: op.seedOnce({pass: seed, staleWhen: () => needsSeed, onSeed: () => { needsSeed = false }})
sim.grids.op.seedOnce.signature: op.seedOnce(opts: {pass: ComputeStep; staleWhen: (f: GridFrame) => boolean; onSeed?: () => void}): GridStage

params.name: opts
params.type: {pass: ComputeStep; staleWhen: (f: GridFrame) => boolean; onSeed?: () => void}

sim.grids.op.iterate.name: iterate
sim.grids.op.iterate.summary: Run a step `count` times this frame.
sim.grids.op.iterate.description: Your `step` adds the pass for iteration `i` and picks which buffer it reads and writes.
examples: op.iterate({count: (f) => Math.round(f.num('speed', 8)), step: (i, nodes) => nodes.push(react.with(i % 2 ? groupBA : groupAB))})
tips: A reaction-diffusion field reads smoother when you raise the iteration count than when you raise the step size.
sim.grids.op.iterate.signature: op.iterate(opts: {count: (f: GridFrame) => number; step: (i: number, nodes: ComputeStep[], f: GridFrame) => void}): GridStage

params.name: opts
params.type: {count: (f: GridFrame) => number; step: (i: number, nodes: ComputeStep[], f: GridFrame) => void}

sim.grids.op.sortPass.name: sortPass
sim.grids.op.sortPass.summary: A compare-and-swap sort that converges a little more every frame: `passes` swaps per frame, alternating odd and even pairs and the two buffers.
sim.grids.op.sortPass.description: `side()` tells `publish` which buffer holds the current order.
examples: const sort = op.sortPass({passes: () => 1 + Math.round(strength * 4), pass: (parity, side) => (parity ? swap1 : swap0).with(side === 'A' ? groupAB : groupBA)})
tips: The alternation continues across frames instead of restarting, which is what makes the sort settle bit by bit.
sim.grids.op.sortPass.signature: op.sortPass(opts: {passes: (f: GridFrame) => number; pass: (parity: 0 | 1, side: 'A' | 'B') => ComputeStep}): SortPassStage

sim.grids.op.name: op
sim.grids.op.summary: The stages a grid frame is built from.
sim.grids.op.description:
List them in `stages` in the order they should run.

Bookkeeping: `host` (before any gate), `values` (write this frame's values), `readyWhen` (wait for an input), `settle` (sleep once the field is still). Work: `pass` (one GPU pass), `cache` (a pass picked per frame), `seedOnce` (a one-shot reset), `iterate` (a pass N times), `sortPass` (a compare-swap chain), `publish` (write the result the layer samples).
examples: stages: [op.readyWhen(() => ready), op.values('write', (f) => paramsU.write({dt: f.dt})), op.iterate({count: () => 8, step: (i, nodes) => nodes.push(react.with(i % 2 ? groupBA : groupAB))}), op.publish(() => output)]
tips: A `values` stage sits before the passes that read it. Stages run in list order.
sim.grids.op.signature: op: { host, values, settle, readyWhen, pass, cache, publish, seedOnce, iterate, sortPass }

sim.grids.trackedViewport.name: trackedViewport
sim.grids.trackedViewport.summary: The canvas size in pixels, kept current across resizes, in the two forms a stage wants.
sim.grids.trackedViewport.description: `tracked()` is the size at the last resize, for a pass that works in the canvas's own pixels. `safe(fp)` prefers the size this frame reports and never returns less than 1, for an aspect ratio.
examples:
const viewport = trackedViewport(params)
op.values('write', (f) => { const s = viewport.safe(f.frameParams); paramsU.write({aspect: s.width / s.height}) })

sim.grids.hostStep.name: hostStep
sim.grids.hostStep.summary: One named step of a JavaScript-stepped grid.
sim.grids.hostStep.description: Return `'skip'` to end the frame here, which is how an idle gate is written.
examples: hostStep('dtGuard', (f) => (f.dt <= 0 ? 'skip' : undefined))
sim.grids.hostStep.signature: hostStep(name: string, run: (f: HostFrame) => void | 'skip'): HostStep

sim.grids.hostGridProgram.name: hostGridProgram
sim.grids.hostGridProgram.summary: A frame program for a small grid stepped in plain JavaScript: the steps run in order every frame until one returns `'skip'`.
sim.grids.hostGridProgram.description:
Hand the result to `onBeforeRender`.

Use it when the field is small (a 32×32 flow grid) and the arithmetic reads better as loops. Publish the cells with `hostFieldTexture` in the last step.
examples: onBeforeRender(hostGridProgram({clampDt: 0.016, steps: [hostStep('advect', (f) => advect(f.dt)), hostStep('publish', () => { pack(field.texData); field.upload() })]}))
sim.grids.hostGridProgram.signature: hostGridProgram(opts: {clampDt: number; steps: HostStep[]}): (fp: unknown) => void

sim.grids.hostFieldTexture.name: hostFieldTexture
sim.grids.hostFieldTexture.summary: The texture a JavaScript-stepped grid is read through.
sim.grids.hostFieldTexture.description:
Pack the cells into `texData` (four half-floats per cell, row by row), call `upload()`, and sample `texture` in the fragment.

`size` is the grid's side in cells. The texture filters smoothly, so a coarse grid reads as a continuous field.
examples: const field = hostFieldTexture(params, {size: 32, label: 'flow'})
tips: Values go in as half-floats: convert each number with `toHalfFloat` before writing it into `texData`.
sim.grids.hostFieldTexture.signature: hostFieldTexture(params: GpuFragmentParams, opts: {size: number; label: string}): {texData: Uint16Array; texture: ReturnType<GpuFragmentParams['registerMediaTexture']>; upload(): void}

sim.fluids.ambientForce.name: ambientForce
sim.fluids.ambientForce.summary: A force applied to the whole field before every solve: a turbulence field, a steady wind.
examples: solve: [ambientForce(turbulenceKernel)]

sim.fluids.restoreToward.name: restoreToward
sim.fluids.restoreToward.summary: A correction applied after every solve: re-seed a color that the solve slowly blurs away.
examples: solve: [restoreToward(colorRestoreKernel)]

sim.fluids.fluidSim.name: fluidSim
sim.fluids.fluidSim.summary: A fluid the engine solves every frame.
sim.fluids.fluidSim.description:
Spread it into a definition next to a `gpu.fragment` that samples the output texture under `output.key`.

The build callback runs once per instance of the layer, with the GPU device, and returns the grid size, the solver, the output pass, the parts and the `values` function. Everything created inside it belongs to that instance. Without a GPU nothing runs and the fragment should fall back to transparent.
examples: ...fluidSim(() => ({resolution: 256, layout: fluidLayout, outputLayout, paramsSchema: FluidParams, solver: {kernels: solverKernels, jacobiIters: 10}, output: {kernel: outputKernel, key: 'smokeTexture'}, pointer: {minDrag: 0.0005}, inject: [splat({kernel: splatKernel})], values: (f) => ({dt: f.dt, emitX: 0.5 * 256, emitY: 256, emitRad: f.num('emitRadius', 0.06) * 256, dyeFade: f.num('dissipation', 1), velFade: 0.2, curlStrength: f.num('detail', 30), colorDecay: 1})}))
tips: Positions and radii in `values` are in grid cells, not uv: multiply a uv value by `resolution`.
sim.fluids.fluidSim.signature: fluidSim<TParams>(build: (params: GpuFragmentParams, root: FluidRoot) => FluidSimConfig<TParams>): {compute: GpuComputeNode}

sim.fluids.splat.name: splat
sim.fluids.splat.summary: An emitter at a fixed source: one pass per frame that adds dye and momentum where your pass function says (a cone from a point, a line along an edge).
sim.fluids.splat.description: Give it the pass function, or a `setup` that builds the pass on resources of its own.
examples: inject: [splat({kernel: splatKernel})]
tips: The source position and radius come from `values`, in grid cells.
sim.fluids.splat.signature: splat<TParams = unknown>(opts: {kernel: FluidKernel} | {setup: (ctx: FluidSetupCtx) => KitComputePipeline}): FluidEmitter<TParams>

sim.fluids.cursorRibbon.name: cursorRibbon
sim.fluids.cursorRibbon.summary: An emitter that paints along the pointer's stroke: a ribbon of stamps between last frame's position and this one, so a fast flick leaves a continuous line, not dots.
sim.fluids.cursorRibbon.description: It tracks the pointer itself, marks the frame active when `activeWhen` says so, and sleeps the simulation `fadeSeconds` after the last activity. `ribbon` describes this frame's stamps. Read the pointer back with `.ptr()` and `.active()` inside `values`.
examples: const strokes = cursorRibbon<Params>({activeWhen: (ptr) => ptr.smoothSpeed > 0.005, fadeSeconds: (f) => decayFadeSeconds(255, f.num('dissipation', 0.4)), pass: {kernel: splatKernel}, ribbon: (f, ptr, values) => ({stepSize: Math.max(0.004, f.num('emitRadius', 0.07) * 0.5), maxSteps: 64, write: (emitX, emitY) => f.writeParams({...values, emitX, emitY})})})
tips: Raise the tracker's `teleportGuard` when fast flicks should paint: the default treats a quarter-canvas jump as the cursor re-entering and emits nothing.

params.name: opts

sim.fluids.seededFieldInit.name: seededFieldInit
sim.fluids.seededFieldInit.summary: A field that starts full: seed it from a pass function, then run the solve silently `warm.steps` times so the first visible frame already flows.
sim.fluids.seededFieldInit.description: Re-seeds whenever `seed` returns a new value. Each warm step advances a private clock by `warm.dt` seconds and writes `warm.values(t)`. When it finishes, the simulation's clock continues from where the warm-up ended.
examples: init: seededFieldInit({kernel: initKernel, seed: (f) => f.num('seed', 0), warm: {steps: 50, jacobiIters: 10, dt: 0.033, startTime: () => Math.random() * 100, values: (t, f) => ({...baseValues(f), time: t})}})
tips: A random `startTime` makes two instances of the same layer drift differently.

params.name: opts

sim.feedback.feedbackSim.name: feedbackSim
sim.feedback.feedbackSim.summary: A simulation that advances a picture of its own last frame by one step of your rule, every frame.
sim.feedback.feedbackSim.description:
Spread it into a definition next to a `gpu.fragment` that samples `display`.

The build callback runs once per instance of the layer, so anything you create inside it (resources, a kernel variant picked from a compile-time prop) belongs to that instance. The simulation needs a child. Without one, or without a GPU, nothing runs and the fragment should fall back to the child.
examples: ...feedbackSim((params, root) => ({size: 768, format: 'rgba16float', speedProp: 'speed', paramsSchema: decoder.Params, bindGroups: ({childTexture, display, paramsBuffer}, read, write) => root.createBindGroup(decoder.layout, {src: childTexture, prev: read.state, next: write.state, display, params: paramsBuffer} as never), step: decoder.kernel, values: ({dt, localTime}) => ({time: localTime, dt, intensity: params.getCpuValue('intensity') as number})}))
tips: Read time from `localTime`, not the layer's clock. It stops when `speedProp` is 0 and every frame's step matches it.
sim.feedback.feedbackSim.signature: feedbackSim<TParams, TGroups = unknown>(build: (params: GpuFragmentParams, root: FeedbackRoot) => FeedbackSimConfig<TParams, TGroups>): {compute: GpuComputeNode}

sim.agents.renderAgents.orientedWorld.name: orientedWorld
sim.agents.renderAgents.orientedWorld.summary: Agents with a heading, drawn as a shape pointing the way they move (or the way they are turned), colored from a rest color to an excited color.
sim.agents.renderAgents.orientedWorld.description: `heading: 'velocity'` reads the direction from the agent's velocity, `'angle'` from a stored angle plus a `home` part. `agitation: 'buffer'` reads excitement from a per-agent value, `'speed'` from the agent's speed. `comet: true` stretches a glow along the heading. `res` is the canvas side in texels.
examples: renderAgents.orientedWorld(simLayout, {shape, res: 1024, splatRCap: 16, heading: 'velocity', agitation: 'buffer', comet: true, ramp: {colorSpace: 2, trails: 'on'}, names: {splat: 'boidsSplat', resolve: 'boidsResolve'}})

params.name: cfg

sim.agents.renderAgents.pointWorld.name: pointWorld
sim.agents.renderAgents.pointWorld.summary: Round motes with no heading, drawn in one tint with a live softness.
sim.agents.renderAgents.pointWorld.description: Where each mote is placed, how bright it is and how big it is come from `pointSlot` parts.
examples: renderAgents.pointWorld(simLayout, {shape, res: 1024, place: pointSlot.orbitalPlace(simLayout, {radius: 0.035, rate: 1.4}), brightness: pointSlot.twinkleBrightness(simLayout, {freq: 2}), bodyRadius: pointSlot.presenceRadius(simLayout), names: {splat: 'motesSplat', resolve: 'motesResolve'}})
sim.agents.renderAgents.pointWorld.signature: renderAgents.pointWorld(layout: PointWorldSplatLayout & Parameters<typeof resolve.tint>[0], cfg: Omit<PointWorldSplatConfig, 'name'> & {names: {splat: string; resolve: string}}): RenderAgentsPipelines

sim.agents.renderAgents.volume.name: volume
sim.agents.renderAgents.volume.summary: A 3D swarm seen in perspective: nearer particles draw larger and brighter, and the color runs from rest to excited with speed.
examples: renderAgents.volume(simLayout, {shape, outRes: 1024, maxSplatSize: 12, extQ: 6, ramp: {colorSpace: 0, exposure: true, trails: 'none'}, names: {splat: 'swarmSplat', glow: 'swarmGlow', profile: 'swarmProfile', resolve: 'swarmResolve'}, extraOnSplat: true})

params.name: cfg

sim.agents.renderAgents.relief.name: relief
sim.agents.renderAgents.relief.summary: Particles standing on an image, seen through a camera: each carries the child's color at its home, and nearer particles win the color where they overlap.
sim.agents.renderAgents.relief.description: `out` is the output size in texels.
examples: renderAgents.relief(fieldLayout, {shape, splatRCap: 24, aaW: 0.75, minAlpha: 0.02, fp: 1024, wobbleFreq: 1.3, perspK: 0.9, out: [outW, outH], weightedColor: {alphaK: 1.6}, names: {splat: 'reliefSplat', resolve: 'reliefResolve'}})

params.name: cfg

sim.agents.renderAgents.name: renderAgents
sim.agents.renderAgents.summary: How the agents are drawn, as one declared part: a splat (each agent stamps its shape into a shared canvas) paired with the matching resolve (the canvas becomes the output picture).
sim.agents.renderAgents.description: Four variants, one per kind of agent: `orientedWorld` for agents with a heading (arrows, streaks, comets) colored from rest to excited, `pointWorld` for round motes in one tint, `volume` for a 3D swarm seen in perspective, `relief` for particles that stand on an image. Put the returned `splat` and `resolve` into `bake`'s pipelines and end the program with them.
examples: const render = renderAgents.orientedWorld(simLayout, {shape: 'arrow', res: 1024, splatRCap: 16, heading: 'velocity', agitation: 'buffer', comet: true, ramp: {colorSpace: 2, trails: 'on'}, names: {splat: 'boidsSplat', resolve: 'boidsResolve'}})
