examples: splat: {kernel: splat.relief(fieldLayout, {shape: 'dot', splatRCap: 24, aaW: 0.75, minAlpha: 0.02, fp: 1024, wobbleFreq: 1.3, perspK: 0.9, name: 'reliefSplat'}), threads: 'grid'}
sim.agentRender.splat.relief.signature: splat.relief: (layout: ReliefRenderLayout, cfg: ReliefSplatConfig) => (x: number, y: number) => void

sim.agentRender.splat.name: splat
sim.agentRender.splat.summary: The step that draws every agent into the shared canvas, one variant per kind of agent.
sim.agentRender.splat.description: `renderAgents` pairs each with its resolve; reach for `splat` alone when you need another pairing.
examples: splat: {kernel: splat.orientedWorld(simLayout, {shape: 'arrow', res: 1024, splatRCap: 16, heading: 'velocity', agitation: 'buffer', comet: true, name: 'boidsSplat'}), threads: 'agents'}
tips: `relief` dispatches over a 2D grid (`threads: 'grid'`); the other three dispatch over `agents`.

sim.agentRender.resolve.ramp.name: ramp
sim.agentRender.resolve.ramp.summary: Rest-to-excited color from two colors, with optional motion trails.
examples: resolve: {kernel: resolve.ramp(simLayout, {colorSpace: 2, res: 1024, invGain: 1 / 255, trails: 'on', name: 'boidsResolve'}), threads: 'fixed', size: [1024, 1024]}
sim.agentRender.resolve.ramp.signature: resolve.ramp: (layout: RampResolveLayout, cfg: RampResolveConfig) => (x: number, y: number) => void

sim.agentRender.resolve.tint.name: tint
sim.agentRender.resolve.tint.summary: One color, with an alpha from coverage.
examples: resolve: {kernel: resolve.tint(simLayout, {res: 1024, name: 'motesResolve'}), threads: 'fixed', size: [1024, 1024]}
sim.agentRender.resolve.tint.signature: resolve.tint: (layout: { readonly $: { readonly accumE: atomicU32[]; readonly outTex: StorageTex; readonly params: { readonly color: v4f; }; }; }, cfg: { res: number; name: string; }) => (x: number, y: number) => void

sim.agentRender.resolve.weightedColor.name: weightedColor
sim.agentRender.resolve.weightedColor.summary: The average of the colors that landed, nearer particles first.
examples: resolve: {kernel: resolve.weightedColor(fieldLayout, {fp: 1024, alphaK: 1.6, name: 'reliefResolve'}), threads: 'fixed', size: [outW, outH]}
sim.agentRender.resolve.weightedColor.signature: resolve.weightedColor: (layout: ReliefRenderLayout, cfg: { fp: number; alphaK: number; name: string; }) => (x: number, y: number) => void

sim.agentRender.resolve.name: resolve
sim.agentRender.resolve.summary: The step that turns the shared canvas into the output picture and clears it for the next frame.
examples: resolve: {kernel: resolve.tint(simLayout, {res: 1024, name: 'motesResolve'}), threads: 'fixed', size: [1024, 1024]}
tips: Dispatch a resolve with `threads: 'fixed'` over the canvas size. It must touch every texel to clear it.

sim.shapeFields.shapeField.analyticExtru.name: analyticExtruded
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.analyticExtru.summary: A flat shape given depth: the 2D distance of a circle, polygon or star, extruded in z by `params.halfDepth`.
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.analyticExtru.description: The shape's sub-props are read live from `params.sa*`.
examples: shapeField.analyticExtruded(simLayout, buildAnalyticSdfFn('hexagon'))
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.analyticExtru.signature: shapeField.analyticExtruded(layout: {readonly $: {readonly params: ExtrudedAnalyticParamsView}}, sdf2d: AnalyticSdf2d): ShapeField3

sim.shapeFields.shapeField.svgExtruded.name: svgExtruded
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.svgExtruded.summary: An SVG outline given depth: the outline's distance texture, extruded in z by `params.halfDepth`.
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.svgExtruded.description: `size` is the texture's side in texels.
examples: shapeField.svgExtruded(simLayout, svgSdfLayout, {size: 512})
tips: Outside the texture's footprint the distance keeps growing, so strays still find their way back.
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.svgExtruded.signature: shapeField.svgExtruded(layout: {readonly $: {readonly params: {readonly halfDepth: number}}}, svgLayout: {readonly $: {readonly sdfSource: d.Infer<d.WgslTexture2d<d.F32>>}}, cfg: {size: number}): ShapeField3

sim.shapeFields.shapeField.analytic3d.name: analytic3d
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.analytic3d.summary: A true 3D solid (sphere, torus, knot…) from its baked distance function, rotated by the shape's live rotation so the swarm follows the surface as it turns.
examples: shapeField.analytic3d(setup3d.layout, setup3d.sdfFn as ShapeField3)

sim.shapeFields.shapeField.svgLifted3d.name: svgLifted3d
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.svgLifted3d.summary: An SVG outline lifted into a 3D solid, rotated by the shape's live rotation.
examples: shapeField.svgLifted3d(setup3d.layout, setup3d.sdfFn as ShapeField3)

sim.shapeFields.shapeField.name: shapeField
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.summary: The signed-distance function of the shape a swarm lives in, for `force.containment`.
sim.shapeFields.shapeField.description: Four builders, one per shape source. Each returns a `ShapeField3`: a GPU function from a shape-local 3D point to a signed distance, negative inside. `analyticExtruded` takes a flat shape (circle, polygon, star…) and gives it a depth from `params.halfDepth`. `svgExtruded` does the same for an SVG outline uploaded as a distance texture. `analytic3d` wraps a true 3D solid so it rotates under the swarm. `svgLifted3d` wraps an SVG lifted into 3D.
examples: force.containment(simLayout, {field: shapeField.analyticExtruded(simLayout, buildAnalyticSdfFn(shapeType)), gradEps: 0.02, wall: {featherFrom: -0.1, featherTo: 0.01, base: 1.1, springK: 22}, recall: {from: 1.5, to: 1.9, k: 9}, homing: {from: 0.12, to: 0.45, k: 5}, entrainment: {featherHalf: 0.05}})
tips: Pick the builder at bake time from the shape props and hand ONE field to the integrator. The swarm never needs to know which kind it is.

define.WgslType.name: WgslType
define.WgslType.summary: The WGSL types a bound name can have inside a body.

define.WgslInput.name: WgslInput
define.WgslInput.text: type WgslInput = ArgSpec | {readonly value: ArgSpec; readonly type: WgslType}
define.WgslInput.summary: One entry of `inputs`: the value to bind under a name — a prop `p('x')`, a context token `ctx.time`, a `Scalar`, or a number — optionally with its WGSL type spelled out as `{value, type}`.
define.WgslInput.description: A prop takes its own type; a `Scalar` or a number is `f32`.

define.WgslSpec.name: WgslSpec
define.WgslSpec.summary: The long form of a body: `wgsl({body, inputs, alpha, name})`.

define.WgslHost.name: WgslHost
define.WgslHost.summary: Where a body runs: a generator's `paint:`, or a pointwise or gather filter's `effect:`.

define.RecompileRule.name: RecompileRule
define.RecompileRule.summary: When a prop change rebuilds the shader: `crosses(value)` at a threshold, or `recompileWhen(fn)` by your own test.

define.StdPropConfig.name: StdPropConfig
define.StdPropConfig.summary: One prop of a definition: `default`, optional `transform`, `ui`, `description`, `compileTime`, and a `recompile:` rule.

define.StdProps.name: StdProps
define.StdProps.text: type StdProps<T extends ComponentProps> = {[K in keyof T]: StdPropConfig<T[K]>}
define.StdProps.summary: The `props` object of a definition: one `StdPropConfig` per prop name.

define.IdentityRule.name: IdentityRule
define.IdentityRule.summary: When a filter does nothing and can be skipped: built with `isZero`, `isValue`, `allOf` or `identityWhenever`.

define.PointwiseEffect.name: PointwiseEffect
define.PointwiseEffect.summary: A filter that edits the layer inside one pixel at a time: what the color words (`saturate`, `hueRotate`, …) and `pointwise({build})` return.
define.PointwiseEffect.description: Give either `body` (a compiled GPU function taking the child's color first, then `args`) or `build` (a function of the params that returns the new color from `params.childNode`). The child arrives in straight alpha and there is no extra render pass.

define.GatherEffect.name: GatherEffect
define.GatherEffect.summary: A filter that reads the layer inside anywhere, not just at this pixel: blurs, halftones, displacements.
define.GatherEffect.description: The child is rendered to a texture first (`params.texture`, premultiplied) and `params.sampleStraight(uv)` reads it back in straight alpha. Return premultiplied color and it is unpremultiplied for you; say `resultAlpha: 'straight'` when you already did.

define.DisplaceByEffectRef.name: DisplaceByEffectRef
define.DisplaceByEffectRef.summary: A filter that moves the layer inside by a simulation's vector field.

define.StdDefinitionBase.name: StdDefinitionBase
define.StdDefinitionBase.text:
interface StdDefinitionBase<T extends ComponentProps> {
    name: string
    category?: string
    description?: string
    deprecatedNames?: string[]
    boundingBoxDeclaration?: BoundingBoxDeclaration
    props: StdProps<T>

    // Declarative engine contract (passthrough).
    usesPointer?: boolean
    acceptsUVContext?: boolean
    acceptsOptionalChild?: boolean
    blendWithChildren?: boolean
    capturesDOM?: boolean
    wantsBoundsParams?: boolean
    providesUVContextViaCompute?: boolean
    naturalSizeKey?: {fromProp: string} | {fixed: string}
    experimental?: ComponentProps
    animatedTime?: {speed: string}
    extraAnimatedTimes?: Record<string, string>
    extraFields?: Record<string, {schema: import('typegpu/data').AnyWgslData; initial: number | number[]}>

    /** A compute pass that runs before the pixel work (simulation state, a prepass). */
    compute?: GpuComputeNode
    /** Where a per-prop map driver samples its map (cell-centre sampling, for grids). */
    mapSampleUVs?: GpuMapSampleUVs
}
define.StdDefinitionBase.summary: The fields every definition shares: `name`, `props`, optional `description` and `category`, the `animatedTime` clock, and engine flags.
define.StdDefinitionBase.description: `animatedTime: {speed: 'speed'}` gives the layer its own clock scaled by that prop. `usesPointer` asks for mouse tracking, `acceptsOptionalChild` lets a generator take a nested layer, `extraFields` declares per-frame values you compute on the CPU. Most definitions need only the first three fields.

define.StdPointwiseFilterDefinition.name: StdPointwiseFilterDefinition
define.StdPointwiseFilterDefinition.summary: A filter that edits the layer inside one pixel at a time: `effect:` holds a color word, `tintToward`, `pointwise({…})` or a `wgsl` body that reads `child`.
define.StdPointwiseFilterDefinition.description: `role` and `species` are optional; the `effect:` field already says filter, and its kind says pointwise. `identityWhen` skips the filter while a rule holds. `missingChildMessage` is shown when nothing is nested inside; omit it to fail silently with a transparent output.

define.StdGatherFilterDefinition.name: StdGatherFilterDefinition
define.StdGatherFilterDefinition.text:
interface StdGatherFilterDefinition<T extends ComponentProps> extends StdDefinitionBase<T> {
    role?: 'filter'
    species?: 'gather'
    effect: GatherEffect | import('./filter').DisplaceByEffect | WgslBody
    identityWhen?: IdentityRule
    missingChildMessage?: string
}
define.StdGatherFilterDefinition.summary: A filter that reads the layer inside anywhere: `effect:` holds `gather({…})`, `displaceBy(…)` or a `wgsl` body that samples `childTexture`.
define.StdGatherFilterDefinition.description: Same optional fields as the pointwise form. The child gets its own render pass so the filter can read neighbouring pixels.

define.StdWgslFilterDefinition.name: StdWgslFilterDefinition
define.StdWgslFilterDefinition.text:
interface StdWgslFilterDefinition<T extends ComponentProps> extends StdDefinitionBase<T> {
    role?: 'filter'
    species?: undefined
    effect: WgslBody
    identityWhen?: IdentityRule
    missingChildMessage?: string
}
define.StdWgslFilterDefinition.summary: A filter whose `effect:` is a `wgsl` body with no `species` declared: gather when the body samples `childTexture`, pointwise otherwise.
define.StdWgslFilterDefinition.description: Declare `species` to override what the body implies.

define.StdWarpDefinition.name: StdWarpDefinition
define.StdWarpDefinition.summary: A distortion: `map:` is one function from the pixel's coordinate to where in the layer inside to read.
define.StdWarpDefinition.description: The map returns the source uv, or `{uv, coverage}` when parts of the output should be transparent. `edges` says what happens past the layer's edge (`'prop'` reads an `edges` prop, a number fixes a mode, `'none'` skips it). `resample` picks the filter used to read the layer (`'catmullRom'` by default, `'bilinear'` for blocky or many-tap maps).

define.StdShapeDefinition.name: StdShapeDefinition
define.StdShapeDefinition.text:
interface StdShapeDefinition {
    role?: 'shape'
    name: string
    description?: string
    category?: string
    shape: Omit<SdfShapeShaderSpec, 'name' | 'description' | 'category'>
}
define.StdShapeDefinition.summary: A 2D shape: `shape:` gives the distance function and the shape's own props; fill, stroke, softness and bounds come for free.

define.StdGeneratorDefinition.name: StdGeneratorDefinition
define.StdGeneratorDefinition.summary: A generator: `paint:` produces a color from coordinates and needs nothing nested inside.
define.StdGeneratorDefinition.description: `paint` is either a std composition (`rampOver(…)`, a builder function of the params) or a `wgsl` body.

define.StdCustomDefinition.name: StdCustomDefinition
define.StdCustomDefinition.summary: A raw builder: `gpu:` holds a fragment function (and optionally a `uvRemap`) for effects the words cannot say yet.
define.StdCustomDefinition.description: `role` here is only a label. Set `requiresChild` and `requiresRTT` yourself.

define.StdDefinition.name: StdDefinition
define.StdDefinition.text:
type StdDefinition<T extends ComponentProps> =
    | StdPointwiseFilterDefinition<T>
    | StdGatherFilterDefinition<T>
    | StdWgslFilterDefinition<T>
    | StdWarpDefinition<T>
    | StdShapeDefinition
    | StdGeneratorDefinition<T>
    | StdCustomDefinition<T>
define.StdDefinition.summary: What `defineShader` accepts: one of the definition shapes, told apart by which field carries the per-pixel work.
define.StdDefinition.description: `paint:` is a generator, `effect:` a filter (pointwise or gather from the effect), `map:` a distortion, `shape:` a 2D shape, `gpu:` a raw builder. `role` and `species` may be declared but must agree with the field; a contradiction throws when the definition is built.

values.PropRef.name: PropRef
values.PropRef.summary: A reference to one of the definition's props by name.

values.ScalarSource.name: ScalarSource
values.ScalarSource.summary: The shapes a `Scalar` can hold: a prop, a product of two values, a radial mask, or a live signal.

values.SignalSlotParams.name: SignalSlotParams
values.SignalSlotParams.summary: What a signal is given when it builds: the props, and the context values where the host has them (a warp's `map:` has no `ctx`).

values.ScalarInput.name: ScalarInput
values.ScalarInput.summary: What a number-valued input accepts: a prop ref `p('x')` or a `Scalar`.

invoke.CtxToken.name: CtxToken
invoke.CtxToken.summary: One of the context values as a token you can pass where a word takes a value: `ctx.uv`, `ctx.time`, …

invoke.ArgSpec.name: ArgSpec
invoke.ArgSpec.text: type ArgSpec = PropRef | Scalar | CtxToken | number
invoke.ArgSpec.summary: Anything a word accepts as an input value: a prop ref `p('x')`, a `Scalar`, a context token, or a plain number.

invoke.SlotParams.name: SlotParams
invoke.SlotParams.summary: The least a value needs to resolve against: the props, plus `ctx` where the host has one (a warp's `map:` does not).

lists.ListItemAt.name: ListItemAt
lists.ListItemAt.summary: One item's fields at a loop index, read by field name and kind.

lists.ListRef.name: ListRef
lists.ListRef.summary: A list prop bound for reading: the live item count and each item's fields.

paint.Paint.name: Paint
paint.Paint.summary: What a generator's `paint:` field takes: a function that returns the color at this pixel.

paint.Field.name: Field
paint.Field.text: type Field = (params: GpuFragmentParams, coord: Expr) => Expr
paint.Field.summary: A number per pixel, computed from a coordinate.
paint.Field.description: Distance fields (`dist.*`) and `flowField` take a uv coordinate (0–1 across the canvas, y down). Noise fields take a 3D coordinate, so wrap them in `scaledVolume`.

paint.Palette.name: Palette
paint.Palette.text: type Palette = (t: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr
paint.Palette.summary: A color for a field value between 0 and 1.
paint.Palette.description: Build one with `pair` (two colors) or `stops` (a multi-stop ramp), then hand it to `rampOver`.

paint.FieldScalar.name: FieldScalar
paint.FieldScalar.text: type FieldScalar = ArgSpec | {base: ArgSpec; add?: number; mul?: number}
paint.FieldScalar.summary: A number input: a prop `p('name')`, a plain number, or a prop remapped as `{base, add, mul}`.
paint.FieldScalar.description: The remapped form resolves to `(base + add) * mul`. Use it when a slider's range is not the unit the word wants, such as a 0–100 slider that should become a small bias.

paint.NoiseBasis.name: NoiseBasis
paint.NoiseBasis.description: `mx3` is smooth all-purpose noise, `perlin` classic gradient noise, `value` softer and blockier. All three return 0–1. `mx3signed` returns −1 to 1 for use with `threshold`.

gradients.Paint.name: Paint
gradients.Paint.summary: What a generator's `paint:` field takes: a function that returns the color at this pixel.

patterns.PatternPaint.name: PatternPaint
patterns.PatternPaint.summary: A pattern value: something you place in `paint:` or hand to another pattern word, yielding a color or a mask per pixel.

patterns.PaintSlot.name: PaintSlot
patterns.PaintSlot.summary: What a pattern slot accepts: a prop `p('name')` or another pattern value.

patterns.CellFrameConvention.name: CellFrameConvention
patterns.CellFrameConvention.summary: Which way a lattice's rows and rotation run.
patterns.CellFrameConvention.description: `'flippedY'` counts rows up from the bottom and rotates counter-clockwise (grids, triangles). `'clockwise'` counts rows down from the top and rotates clockwise (hexagons, truchet, cubes). `'plain'` counts down from the top and rotates counter-clockwise (weave). Use the one named in the line word's example; the others still work but shift the look.

patterns.ScatterOptions.name: ScatterOptions

patterns.ScatteredPoint.name: ScatteredPoint
patterns.ScatteredPoint.summary: One scattered point: where it sits, the pixel's offset from it, and three random 0–1 values for its cell.

patterns.InkPlateSpec.name: InkPlateSpec
patterns.InkPlateSpec.summary: One ink plate of a `cmykPress`: which channel it prints, its screen-angle prop (degrees) and its ink-color prop.

patterns.GatherStage.name: GatherStage
patterns.GatherStage.summary: A value computed per pixel from the layer inside a gather effect, such as a dither level.

patterns.PixelGrid.name: PixelGrid
patterns.PixelGrid.summary: The pixel grid a dither works on, from `pixelGrid`: the cell `size` prop, the cell coordinate `coord`, and `source`, the child's color sampled once per cell.

figures.Paint.name: Paint
figures.Paint.summary: What a generator's `paint:` field takes: a function that returns the color at this pixel.

figures.StrokedSegmentSlots.name: StrokedSegmentSlots

figures.SineStrokeSlots.name: SineStrokeSlots

compose.Layer.name: Layer
compose.Layer.summary: One entry in `layers`: a color, or a color with options.
compose.Layer.description: `blend` is `'add'` (the default, sums light) or `'screen'` (brightens without blowing out). `opacity` scales the layer. `behind` is a 0–1 factor the layer is seen through, such as the transmittance of fog in front of it.

media.MediaSurfaceHalf.name: MediaSurfaceHalf
media.MediaSurfaceHalf.summary: What a media word returns: the GPU half of a definition.

noise.Wave.name: Wave
noise.Wave.summary: One traveling sine wave, written as plain data.
noise.Wave.description: `x`, `y` and `t` are the wave's frequency along that axis: larger is tighter, and `t` is its drift speed along the layer's clock. Leave an axis out to ignore it. A negative value runs the wave the other way. `phase` shifts the wave, in radians.

noise.WaveTerm.name: WaveTerm
noise.WaveTerm.summary: One term of a wave schedule: a single wave, or several multiplied together.
noise.WaveTerm.description: Multiplying an x-wave by a y-wave gives an interference pattern instead of stripes. `weight` scales the term, default 1.

noise.Fold.name: Fold
noise.Fold.summary: One ridge of a draped cloth as `foldSet` lays it out: where it rests across the drape, how wide and how high it is, and the phase that keeps its ripple out of step with its neighbours.

noise.DrapeOptions.name: DrapeOptions
noise.DrapeOptions.summary: The knobs that shape and animate a draped cloth, shared by `drapedFolds` and `clothCoords`.

noise.RgbStage.name: RgbStage
noise.RgbStage.text: type RgbStage = (rgb: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr
noise.RgbStage.summary: A color-only step for `overRgb`: takes a paint's rgb and returns new rgb.

noise.ReliefBasis.name: ReliefBasis
noise.ReliefBasis.summary: A height field `noiseRelief` can emboss a layer with.

light.LightValue.name: LightValue
light.LightValue.summary: A light or a frame waiting for the shader's params.
light.LightValue.description: Call it with `params` inside a `paint` or `effect` function to get its value at this pixel.

light.LightPart.name: LightPart
light.LightPart.text: type LightPart = (frame: Expr, params: GpuFragmentParams) => Expr
light.LightPart.summary: A light shaped over a frame's coordinates.
light.LightPart.description: Parts for `radialFrame` read distance and angle (`vec2(dist, angle)`); parts for `beamFrame` read distance along and across the beam (`vec2(u, v)`). Evaluate one with `withFrame`, combine several with `modulate`.

light.HeatRamp.name: HeatRamp
light.HeatRamp.summary: What `heatRamp` returns: call its `taps(heat, params)` to color a heat field.

materials.SurfaceFrame.name: SurfaceFrame
materials.SurfaceFrame.summary: What `shapedSurface` hands your `surface` function: the shape's distance field, sampled and ready to shade.
materials.SurfaceFrame.description: Read the taps through `surfaceField` rather than directly. `volumetric` tells you at build time whether the shape is a 3D one (a sphere, a cube, an extruded SVG) or a flat one.

materials.ShapedSurfaceSpec.name: ShapedSurfaceSpec

materials.ShapedSurfaceEffect.name: ShapedSurfaceEffect

materials.SurfaceField.name: SurfaceField
materials.SurfaceField.summary: The field values a material reads, bound once: the taps, the signed distance and the pixel size.

volume.InteriorRay.name: InteriorRay
volume.InteriorRay.summary: The line of sight through a shape's interior, from `interiorRay`.

volume.VolumeMarchStep.name: VolumeMarchStep
volume.VolumeMarchStep.summary: One sample along a `volumeMarch`, handed to its callback.

radiance.GatherSpec.name: GatherSpec

radiance.ShadowSpec.name: ShadowSpec

radiance.IrradianceFieldSpec.name: IrradianceFieldSpec
radiance.IrradianceFieldSpec.description: Every string is the name of one of your props.

voxels.VoxelStyle.name: VoxelStyle
voxels.VoxelStyle.summary: What each block is: `'cube'`, `'sphere'` or `'rounded'` (a cube with rounded corners).

voxels.VoxelGridSpace.name: VoxelGridSpace
voxels.VoxelGridSpace.summary: Where the grid sits: `'shape'` turns with the shape like a built model, `'view'` stays fixed to the canvas.

voxels.VoxelSurfaceSpec.name: VoxelSurfaceSpec
voxels.VoxelSurfaceSpec.description: Every field but `surface` is a prop ref, `p('name')`.

voxels.VoxelFrame.name: VoxelFrame
voxels.VoxelFrame.summary: One block, as `voxelSurface` hands it to your `surface`.

frames.CentredFrame.name: CentredFrame
frames.CentredFrame.summary: What `centredFrame` gives you for each pixel.

frames.SegmentFrame.name: SegmentFrame
frames.SegmentFrame.summary: What `segmentFrame` gives you for each pixel.

frames.DirectionFrame.name: DirectionFrame

signal.PointerSignal.name: PointerSignal
signal.PointerSignal.summary: Where the pointer is this frame, for a simulation step.
signal.PointerSignal.description: `teleportGuard: 'on'` means a sudden jump (the cursor entering the canvas somewhere new) adds no motion that frame.

signal.PointerSpeedSignal.name: PointerSpeedSignal
signal.PointerSpeedSignal.summary: How fast the pointer is moving, for a simulation step.
signal.PointerSpeedSignal.description: Measured in uv per second and capped at `max`, so a fast flick cannot overdrive the simulation.

filter.TintTowardEffect.name: TintTowardEffect
filter.TintTowardEffect.summary: What `tintToward` returns: the color prop and the amount, ready for `effect:`.

filter.DisplaceByEffect.name: DisplaceByEffect
filter.DisplaceByEffect.summary: What `displaceBy` returns: the simulation field and the props it reads, ready for `effect:`.

effects.blurs.SampleStage.name: SampleStage
effects.blurs.SampleStage.summary: The first stage of a stacked effect: reads the child as a texture and returns the starting color at this pixel.
effects.blurs.SampleStage.description: Pass one to `gatherStack` as its first argument. The overlay stages then edit its result in order.

effects.blurs.OverlayStage.name: OverlayStage
effects.blurs.OverlayStage.text: type OverlayStage = (color: Expr, params: RttFilterParams) => Expr
effects.blurs.OverlayStage.summary: One editing stage of a stacked effect: takes the color so far and returns the edited color.
effects.blurs.OverlayStage.description: Stages run in the order you list them in `gatherStack`.

effects.blurs.GatherFrame.name: GatherFrame
effects.blurs.GatherFrame.summary: A geometry that several stages of one effect share: a warped coordinate, a surface normal, a coverage mask.
effects.blurs.GatherFrame.description: Make one with a frame word (`sphereFrame`, `glitchFrame`, `fluteFrame`, `peelFrame`), keep it in a module constant, and hand that same frame to every stage. It is computed once per pixel however many stages read it.

effects.blurs.BlurPathSpec.name: BlurPathSpec
effects.blurs.BlurPathSpec.summary: The path a motion blur smears along: its kind plus the prop that anchors it.
effects.blurs.BlurPathSpec.description: Make one with `blurPath.linear`, `blurPath.orbit` or `blurPath.zoom` and pass it to `motionBlur`.

effects.blurs.MotionBlurDetailSlots.name: MotionBlurDetailSlots
effects.blurs.MotionBlurDetailSlots.summary: The optional lens and streak dials of `motionBlur`.
effects.blurs.MotionBlurDetailSlots.description: Each is a prop ref whose value 0 is off; give every one `recompile: crosses(0)` so the shader switches between the plain gather and the detail gather exactly when a dial leaves or returns to 0.

effects.blurs.ComputeBackedEffect.name: ComputeBackedEffect
effects.blurs.ComputeBackedEffect.summary: The two halves a heavy blur adds to a definition: a pass that blurs the child ahead of time, and the fragment that reads it.
effects.blurs.ComputeBackedEffect.description: Spread the whole object into a definition that declares `species: 'custom'`, `requiresRTT: true` and `requiresChild: true`.

effects.blurs.VariableBlurDetailSlots.name: VariableBlurDetailSlots
effects.blurs.VariableBlurDetailSlots.summary: The optional lens dials of `progressiveBlur` and `tiltShift`.
effects.blurs.VariableBlurDetailSlots.description: `dispersion` (−1 to 1) blurs red and blue by different radii for a defocus colour fringe that grows with the blur; `jitter` (0–1) dithers the tap comb so long radii do not band. Both are off at 0 and read per frame; give `dispersion` `recompile: crosses(0)`, since its kernel is only built while it is non-zero.

effects.blurs.PeelShade.name: PeelShade
effects.blurs.PeelShade.summary: One shading term of a page peel: a number per pixel read against the peel frame.
effects.blurs.PeelShade.description: `curlShading`, `curlSheen`, `overhangShadow` and `revealShadow` each make one; `peelCompose` takes all four.

effects.stylize.GatherStage.name: GatherStage
effects.stylize.GatherStage.summary: A stage that reads the layer inside (rendered to a texture) and gives one value per pixel.

effects.stylize.KuwaharaBrush.name: KuwaharaBrush
effects.stylize.KuwaharaBrush.text: type KuwaharaBrush = (params: RttFilterParams) => {quadrants: {sum: Expr; sq: Expr}[]; invN: number}
effects.stylize.KuwaharaBrush.summary: The brush `kuwahara` builds: four overlapping patches of samples around each pixel.

effects.stylize.SobelRing.name: SobelRing
effects.stylize.SobelRing.text: type SobelRing = (params: RttFilterParams) => {sobelA: Expr; sobelB: Expr; centre: Expr; centreLum: Expr}
effects.stylize.SobelRing.summary: The ring of edge samples `sobelTaps` builds around each pixel.

effects.stylize.FragmentStage.name: FragmentStage
effects.stylize.FragmentStage.summary: A stage of the ASCII look: one value per pixel, computed in the fragment.

effects.lens.SpectralLensSlots.name: SpectralLensSlots
effects.lens.SpectralLensSlots.description: Every field is a prop ref (`p('name')`); ranges are the useful slider ranges.

effects.reveal.AngularDirection.name: AngularDirection
effects.reveal.AngularDirection.summary: Which way an angular sweep turns.
effects.reveal.AngularDirection.description: Baked into the shader, so a change rebuilds it.

effects.reveal.RevealSlots.name: RevealSlots
effects.reveal.RevealSlots.summary: What `reveal` needs: the order pixels go in, and the three timing props every wipe shares.

effects.instances.GridSlots.name: GridSlots
effects.instances.GridSlots.summary: The props of a grid layout: `columns` and `rows` (counts), `gapX` and `gapY` (fractions of the canvas width and height), `stagger` (0 to 1, shifts every other row by that much of a cell) and `flip`, a compile-time select that mirrors alternate cells (`'none'`, `'alternate-flip-x'`, `'alternate-flip-y'`, `'both'`).

effects.instances.RadialSlots.name: RadialSlots
effects.instances.RadialSlots.text:
interface RadialSlots {
    count: PropRef
    radius: PropRef
    startAngle: PropRef
    sweep: PropRef
    faceCenter: PropRef
}
effects.instances.RadialSlots.summary: The props of a radial layout: `count`, `radius` (a fraction of the canvas height), `startAngle` and `sweep` (degrees), and `faceCenter`, a boolean that turns each copy to face the middle of the circle.

effects.instances.LineSlots.name: LineSlots
effects.instances.LineSlots.summary: The props of a line layout: `count`, `direction` (degrees, 0 points right) and `spacing` between copies (a fraction of the canvas height).

effects.instances.PlacementSpec.name: PlacementSpec

effects.instances.PlacementPick.name: PlacementPick
effects.instances.PlacementPick.summary: A layout chosen by a select prop, built by `byMode`.

effects.instances.VariationSlots.name: VariationSlots
effects.instances.VariationSlots.summary: How each copy differs from the last.
effects.instances.VariationSlots.description: `scale` and `opacity` multiply with every copy (1 keeps them equal), `rotation` adds per copy in radians (give the prop a degrees-to-radians transform). The `jitter` props (0 to 1) add seeded randomness to position, rotation, scale and opacity; `seed` re-rolls it. `phase` (0 to 1) slides the whole layout by one cell or one copy and wraps seamlessly, for looping animation.

effects.instances.RepeatInstancesRecipe.name: RepeatInstancesRecipe
effects.instances.RepeatInstancesRecipe.summary: Everything `repeatInstances` needs: what to copy, where to put the copies, and how they vary.

effects.overlay.DetectionOverlaySlots.name: DetectionOverlaySlots
effects.overlay.DetectionOverlaySlots.description: Every field is a prop ref (`p('name')`). Props marked "select" are declared `compileTime: true`.

effects.overlay.MotionTrackerHudSlots.name: MotionTrackerHudSlots
effects.overlay.MotionTrackerHudSlots.description: Every field is a prop ref (`p('name')`).

simulate.WaveOp.name: WaveOp
simulate.WaveOp.summary: A step that makes the grid ripple like a water surface, fading by `damping`.
simulate.WaveOp.description: Needs `history: 2` on the grid, because a wave reads the two previous frames. `damping` is a prop on a 0–20 scale: 0 rings forever, 20 dies in a few frames.

simulate.SplatOp.name: SplatOp
simulate.SplatOp.summary: A step that presses a soft round brush into the grid wherever the pointer moves.
simulate.SplatOp.description: `at` is the pointer signal, `amount` the pointer-speed signal that scales the push (a still pointer adds nothing), `radius` a prop on a 0.1–1 scale.

simulate.GradientOp.name: GradientOp
simulate.GradientOp.summary: A derived output: the slope of the grid at every cell, as a 2D vector.
simulate.GradientOp.description: This is what a distortion wants: `displaceBy` moves each pixel along the slope.

simulate.GridStepOp.name: GridStepOp
simulate.GridStepOp.summary: Any step that advances the grid each frame.

simulate.GridDeriveOp.name: GridDeriveOp
simulate.GridDeriveOp.summary: Any output derived from the grid after the steps have run.

simulate.GridSimConfig.name: GridSimConfig
simulate.GridSimConfig.summary: What a grid simulation declares: its size, how many past frames it keeps, its steps, and its named outputs.

simulate.SimOutputRef.name: SimOutputRef
simulate.SimOutputRef.summary: A handle to one named output of a simulation, the thing you hand to `displaceBy`.

sim.grids.GridRoot.name: GridRoot
sim.grids.GridRoot.summary: The GPU device handle the build callback receives, for creating the buffers and passes your stages use.

sim.grids.GridFrameParams.name: GridFrameParams
sim.grids.GridFrameParams.summary: What the renderer reports each frame: the pointer in uv, the frame delta in seconds, the canvas size in pixels.

sim.grids.GridFrame.name: GridFrame
sim.grids.GridFrame.summary: One frame, as every stage sees it: the clamped delta, the clock, and your props.

sim.grids.GridStage.name: GridStage
sim.grids.GridStage.description:
Build them with `op.*` rather than by hand.

Each frame runs every stage's `ready`, then every `tick`, then every `skip`, then every `emit`, in list order.

sim.grids.GridSimConfig.name: GridSimConfig
sim.grids.GridSimConfig.summary: What a GPU grid simulation declares: its outputs, its frame-delta clamp, and its stages.

sim.grids.SortPassStage.name: SortPassStage
sim.grids.SortPassStage.summary: A sort chain's stage, which also reports which of its two buffers holds the current result.

sim.grids.HostFrame.name: HostFrame
sim.grids.HostFrame.summary: One frame of a JavaScript-stepped grid: the clamped delta, the clock and the pointer in uv.

sim.grids.HostStep.name: HostStep
sim.grids.HostStep.description: Return `'skip'` to end the frame early.

sim.fluids.FluidRoot.name: FluidRoot
sim.fluids.FluidRoot.summary: The GPU device handle the build callback receives, for creating the resources your passes use.

sim.fluids.FluidKernel.name: FluidKernel
sim.fluids.FluidKernel.text: type FluidKernel = (cx: number, cy: number) => void
sim.fluids.FluidKernel.summary: A pass function run once per grid cell, with the cell's column and row.

sim.fluids.FluidFrameParams.name: FluidFrameParams
sim.fluids.FluidFrameParams.summary: What the renderer reports each frame: the pointer in uv, the frame delta in seconds, the canvas size in pixels.

sim.fluids.FluidFrame.name: FluidFrame
sim.fluids.FluidFrame.summary: One frame, as every part and `values` sees it: the clamped delta, the clocks, the pointer and your props.

sim.fluids.FluidSetupCtx.name: FluidSetupCtx
sim.fluids.FluidSetupCtx.summary: What a part receives when it builds its passes: the device, the grid size, the buffers and a pass builder.

sim.fluids.FluidEmitter.name: FluidEmitter
sim.fluids.FluidEmitter.summary: Something that injects into the field each frame.

sim.fluids.FluidSolveStage.name: FluidSolveStage
sim.fluids.FluidSolveStage.summary: A pass that runs inside every solve, before it (`pre`) or after it (`post`).

sim.fluids.FluidInitIo.name: FluidInitIo
sim.fluids.FluidInitIo.summary: What an init part appends with: the frame's pass list, a queued values write, and a full solve.

sim.fluids.FluidInitPart.name: FluidInitPart
sim.fluids.FluidInitPart.summary: How the field starts, and when it must start over.

sim.fluids.FluidContainerParts.name: FluidContainerParts
sim.fluids.FluidContainerParts.summary: What a container (a shape the fluid is confined to) contributes each frame.

sim.fluids.FluidSimConfig.name: FluidSimConfig
sim.fluids.FluidSimConfig.summary: What a fluid simulation declares: its grid, its solver, its output, its parts and its per-frame values.

sim.fluids.CursorRibbonSpec.name: CursorRibbonSpec
sim.fluids.CursorRibbonSpec.summary: This frame's ribbon of stamps along the stroke: spacing, cap, and how each stamp is written.

sim.feedback.FeedbackRoot.name: FeedbackRoot
sim.feedback.FeedbackRoot.summary: The GPU device handle the build callback receives, for creating the resources your step reads.

sim.feedback.FeedbackKernel.name: FeedbackKernel
sim.feedback.FeedbackKernel.text: type FeedbackKernel = (cx: number, cy: number) => void
sim.feedback.FeedbackKernel.summary: A step function run once per state cell, with the cell's column and row.

sim.feedback.FeedbackBindContext.name: FeedbackBindContext
sim.feedback.FeedbackBindContext.summary: What you get when wiring your layout: the child's picture, the display texture, any extra textures you declared, and the buffer holding your per-frame values.

sim.feedback.FeedbackSimConfig.name: FeedbackSimConfig
sim.feedback.FeedbackSimConfig.summary: What a feedback simulation declares: the state's size and format, one step function, the wiring that hands it the read and write sides, and the values it reads each frame.

sim.agents.RenderAgentsPipelines.name: RenderAgentsPipelines
sim.agents.RenderAgentsPipelines.summary: The two draw steps every agent frame ends with: `splat` draws the agents, `resolve` turns the drawing into the output picture.

sim.agents.AgentSimBaked.name: AgentSimBaked
sim.agents.AgentSimBaked.summary: What `bake` returns: the steps, their order, and anything the frame needs from composition.

sim.agents.AgentSimFragmentConfig.name: AgentSimFragmentConfig
sim.agents.AgentSimFragmentConfig.summary: How the layer samples the simulation's picture.

sim.agents.AgentSimConfig.name: AgentSimConfig
sim.agents.AgentSimConfig.summary: What an agent simulation declares: its state layout, its values, its count, its output, and the bake, frame and fragment halves.

sim.agents.AgentSimSpread.name: AgentSimSpread
sim.agents.AgentSimSpread.summary: The two halves `agentSim` adds to a definition: the simulation and the fragment that samples it.

sim.agentForces.Vec4StateArray.name: Vec4StateArray
sim.agentForces.Vec4StateArray.summary: A per-agent buffer of four numbers each (`agents`, `pos`, `vel`, …).

sim.agentForces.AgentForce3.name: AgentForce3
sim.agentForces.AgentForce3.text: type AgentForce3 = (pos: d.v3f, vel: d.v3f, seed: number) => d.v3f
sim.agentForces.AgentForce3.summary: A push on a 3D agent, from its position, velocity and per-agent seed.

sim.agentForces.ShapeField3.name: ShapeField3
sim.agentForces.ShapeField3.summary: The signed distance to a shape's surface at a shape-local 3D point, negative inside.

sim.agentForces.VolumeSwarmLayout.name: VolumeSwarmLayout
sim.agentForces.VolumeSwarmLayout.summary: What a 3D swarm's layout must name: `pos`, `vel`, the `dens` grid and the `params` values.

sim.agentForces.PressureForce.name: PressureForce
sim.agentForces.PressureForce.summary: What `force.pressure` returns: the force, plus the two density-grid steps and the grid's cell count for the program.

sim.agentForces.AgentSteer2.name: AgentSteer2
sim.agentForces.AgentSteer2.text: type AgentSteer2 = (pos: d.v2f, vel: d.v2f, maxSpeedI: number) => d.v2f
sim.agentForces.AgentSteer2.summary: A steering push on a 2D agent, from its position, velocity and its own top speed.

sim.agentForces.SteeringLayout.name: SteeringLayout
sim.agentForces.SteeringLayout.summary: What a flock's layout must name: `agents`, the `agit` excitement buffer and the `params` values.

sim.agentForces.AgentTorque.name: AgentTorque
sim.agentForces.AgentTorque.text: type AgentTorque = (fld: FieldSampleValue, theta: number, fi: number) => number
sim.agentForces.AgentTorque.summary: A turn on a turning agent, from the field at its position, its angle and its index.

sim.agentForces.AgentFieldAt.name: AgentFieldAt
sim.agentForces.AgentFieldAt.summary: A sample of a field at a 2D position.

sim.agentForces.AgentHome2.name: AgentHome2
sim.agentForces.AgentHome2.summary: An agent's resting position, from its index.

sim.agentForces.OrientationLayout.name: OrientationLayout
sim.agentForces.OrientationLayout.summary: What a turning-agent layout must name: `agents`, the `agit` excitement buffer and the `params` values.

sim.agentForces.DriftLayout.name: DriftLayout
sim.agentForces.DriftLayout.summary: What a drifting-mote layout must name: `agents` and the `params` values.

sim.agentForces.AgentDrift.name: AgentDrift
sim.agentForces.AgentDrift.summary: A built-in velocity for an agent, from its index alone.

sim.agentForces.ReliefLayout.name: ReliefLayout
sim.agentForces.ReliefLayout.summary: What an image-relief layout must name: `pos`, `vel`, `col`, the child picture `src` and the `params` values.

sim.agentForces.AgentChannel.name: AgentChannel
sim.agentForces.AgentChannel.text: type AgentChannel = (rgb: d.v3f, a: number) => number
sim.agentForces.AgentChannel.summary: One number in 0–1 read out of a color and its alpha: a brightness, a channel, a saturation.

sim.agentForces.AdvectLayout.name: AdvectLayout
sim.agentForces.AdvectLayout.summary: What a fluid-carried layout must name: `agents`, the fluid's velocity texture `velTex` and the `params` values.

sim.agentRender.WorldSplatLayout.name: WorldSplatLayout
sim.agentRender.WorldSplatLayout.summary: What an oriented splat's layout must name: `agents`, the `accumE` and `accumS` canvases, and `params.aspect` and `params.bodyR`.

sim.agentRender.RampResolveLayout.name: RampResolveLayout
sim.agentRender.RampResolveLayout.summary: What a ramp resolve's layout must name: the two canvases, the output texture `outTex`, and the two colors `params.colA` and `params.colB`.

sim.agentRender.OrientedWorldSplatConfig.name: OrientedWorldSplatConfig
sim.agentRender.OrientedWorldSplatConfig.summary: How agents with a heading are drawn.

sim.agentRender.PointWorldSplatConfig.name: PointWorldSplatConfig
sim.agentRender.PointWorldSplatConfig.summary: How round motes are drawn: the shape, the canvas size, and the three `pointSlot` parts.

sim.agentRender.PointWorldSplatLayout.name: PointWorldSplatLayout
sim.agentRender.PointWorldSplatLayout.summary: What a point splat's layout must name: `agents`, the `accumE` canvas, and `params.aspect` and `params.softness`.

sim.agentRender.VolumeSplatConfig.name: VolumeSplatConfig
sim.agentRender.VolumeSplatConfig.summary: How a 3D swarm is drawn: the shape, the output size, the largest particle, and the reach of each particle's profile.

sim.agentRender.ReliefSplatConfig.name: ReliefSplatConfig
sim.agentRender.ReliefSplatConfig.summary: How particles standing on an image are drawn.

sim.agentRender.RampResolveConfig.name: RampResolveConfig
sim.agentRender.RampResolveConfig.summary: How the rest-to-excited color resolve behaves.
